ontario-established.name: Lincoln-Jordon Valley Campground
ontario-established.notes: Very nice campground with large grassy fields and a river close by. One of the cleanest sanitaries of our whole trip. Very friendly owner. Pool. Laundry. Dump station. Slow WiFi for one hour free. 37.45 CAD for two adults without electricity. Highly recommendable.

ontario-established.name: Smith's Trailer Park
ontario-established.notes: Very large trailer park but only a few places seem to be available for short term visitors. Fast Wifi but the restrooms could have been better and cleaner. Hot shower is 1 CAN extra!!! No laundry available. If you don't need their facilities the close-by Walmart is the better alternative. We had to pay 40,50 CAN/night.

ontario-established.name: Rainbow Ridge
ontario-established.notes: LGBTQ2 campground. Offers both serviced and I serviced sites. Heated pool. Chip truck.  Dancehall. Very well kept property.

ontario-established.name: Pukaskwa National Park Hattie Cove Campsite

Sep7/22 we paid $55+tax. I guess price changes at a whim.

ontario-established.name: Trowbridge Falls Park
ontario-established.notes:
big parking lot in the park, the campground here was closed, but no sign for no overnight in the parking area, very quiet and peaceful  

Comment: now is a campground. 15 CAN x night

This is a pretty standard RV park... There is an outdoor pool but we were staying in late September so not open. Extra fees for Internet, additional vehicles, guests, you name it. There is a laundry room and showers/washrooms. If you need services and have the budget... not a terrible place.

ontario-established.name: Bentick riverside community park

ontario-established.name: River View Park Chapple
ontario-established.notes: small campground for free! at least for 3 days. view at the river. 5 sites for RVs, electricity included (30Amps, 15Amps at the pavilion)! don't know about tents but there is enough space for some. 1 water tap (not in off season), 1 pit toilet, pic nic tables, 1 fire pit. train few hundred meters away could annoy somebody but was ok for us. wonderful place!

ontario-established.name: Pancake Bay Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Site 372, facing Lake Superior.  The wind helps blow away the mosquitos, but leaves the butterflies and Canada geese.

ontario-established.name: Neys Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Park on the north shore of Lake Superior.  Lovely sites available on the beach or in the woods.

ontario-established.name: Blue Lake Provincial Park

ontario-established.name: Chutes Provincial Park

ontario-established.name: Fishers' Paradise
ontario-established.notes:
Primitive campsites used for the River and Sky Music Festival.  Beautiful spot on the Sturgeon river.  Great swimming in the river.

Wifi available at entrance area

ontario-established.name: Little Mississippi Trails and Campgrounds
ontario-established.notes: Lovely campground on a river in the middle of nowhere.  The hosts keep it in pristine condition.  Firewood is stacked and ready to use at each site, included in the price.  There are canoes, kayaks, and a paddle boat for the guests.  There is a washing machine and a place to hang up laundry.  Everything is clean and works well.  The host brought over a pressure washer for us to wash our RV.  Friendly and helpful.  Full service sites are available.

ontario-established.name: Hammock Harbor RV Park
ontario-established.notes: Mostly permanent or semi-permanent seasonal trailers.  The grounds are well kept, especially the gardens that individuals have built up.  It is relatively expensive, and the showers and bathrooms are old and shabby.  You would think that for $264 per week they would provide hot water in the showers, but for only a quarter you can have some hot water.  The park is full of small canals and most people have a boat tied up next to their trailer.

ontario-established.name: Cité de l'Or
ontario-established.notes:
Gold mining museum
they have 4 site with services ($30)
and gravel parking lot ($15)

can take a 2 hours tour of this desaffected gold mine

ontario-established.name: Le nis d'Aigle

ontario-established.name: Riverwaterfall
ontario-established.notes: site overlooking river 6 nice sites with tables. 2 covered tables

ontario-established.name: Wasani River rest

ontario-established.name: Rene Brunelle Provincial Park

ontario-established.name: Castor River

ontario-established.name: Happy Land RV Park

ontario-established.name: Wabigoon Lake RV Park

ontario-established.name: Camping du petit lac Simon

ontario-established.name: Guelph Lake Park
ontario-established.notes: Large Campground. The wash houses are not very new. Expensive. We paid 42 CAD for ins night.

ontario-established.name: Yellow Butterfly—Iron Bridge

ontario-established.name: Kettle Lakes Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
Super campground with all services including canoe rental.
We paid 41.53$ for a site without electricity.
5.00$ if you need power.

ontario-established.name: Wildwood conservation area
ontario-established.notes: All services quiet, lake, pool, protects animals

ontario-established.name: Driftwood Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
Vehicle Camping
Ottawa Campground is the larger campground with two thirds of the park’s campsites located here. There is a full-service, barrier-free comfort station that includes showers, flush toilets and laundry facilities. Many of the campsites are waterfront. All campsites are non-electrical and have a picnic table and fire ring.

All campsites in Brumm Campground are electrical and are geared toward larger trailer units and RVs. Pull-through campsites are available and each site has a picnic table and fire ring.

Group Camping
Two group campsites are available for larger, organized groups. Reservations can be made online or by phone.

Barrier Free
A barrier-free site is located beside the comfort station in Ottawa East Campground and can be reserved through the Ontario Parks central reservation service.

Boat Launch
A boat launch and small docking facility is provided for access to the Ottawa River.

Comfort Station(s)
The comfort station, located in the Ottawa East Campground is a modern facility with showers, flush toilets and laundry facilities.

Day Use
The day use area provides a small sand beach and grassed picnic area on the shores of the Ottawa River.

Flush Toilets
Both the comfort station and small washrooms located throughout the campground contain flush toilets.

Laundromat
A coin operated washer and dryer is located at the comfort station.

Park Store
Canoe rentals, ice, firewood and a selection of souvenir merchandise can be purchased at the park store.

Rentals
Rental canoes are conveniently located in the campground and day use area on the shores of the Ottawa River. Rentals include Personal Floatation Devices (PFDs), paddles and a boat safety kit.

http://www.ontarioparks.com/park/driftwood

ontario-established.name: Camping Sagitaire 2001
ontario-established.notes: Large Campground mainly for seasonal guests. Ok for a night but 35$ is too much for what you get.

ontario-established.name: Saint Laurence Park

Possibility to park a big RV, water and electricity available. Camping not extremely nice but convenient on the road to Thousand Island.

ontario-established.name: Carleton Cove

ontario-established.name: Finlayson Point Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: 117 sites, mid May, All ages, Tents, 1004 ft elev, 14 pull thrus, 33 electric only sites, 15/30 amp, tables, grill, water, toilets, showers, dump, laundry, firewood, playground,

ontario-established.name: Brangh's Seine River Lodge

ontario-established.name: Rushing River Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Amazing campsite on the waters edge. Site 112

ontario-established.name: Hattie Cove campground
ontario-established.notes: $30 fee for camping. Included showers and wifi at visitor centre.

ontario-established.name: Valens Lake Conservation Area Campground

ontario-established.name: South Baymouth Village
ontario-established.notes:
A small Campground, run by the Village. Very basic, but really ok! There are two hot showers and flush toilets, but no dishwashing facility.

It's normally 10 Dollars for a tent, 20 for a vehicle and plus 5 for water at the site. But I was told by a local, that they didn't collect this year - so it was free!

There are 5 sites, two of them might be suitable for big rigs.

Restaurants and Shops are nearby in the Village.

Great cell phone signal here.

ontario-established.name: Klotz Lake Camp
ontario-established.notes: This is an established campground. It is a little pricy for no amenities. We had the place to our self - we had a picnic table and were right by the water. It was a little late when we decided to stay here - on a side note we did, however, notice that just slightly west of this campground there was a little gravel parking lot with a couple garbage cans. Enough room for a couple vehicles. Just something to keep in mind if you do not want to spend $$ to camp!

ontario-established.name: Lebel sur Quevillon
ontario-established.notes:
The campsite was closed from the end of August, then we had a quiet night on the beach parking. 
Update: The  campground was open when we were there May 23rd 2022 for 2 nights.

ontario-established.name: Sandbanks Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Great beaches on Ontario Lake. Many sites are not directly on the beach but some are

National Park Campground , electricity+water, showers (~ 30CAN )
No WiFi or Cell Service but there is a very nice "Center decouverte" close by with wifi, coffee and very comfortable sofas. You can relax there after doing your hikes! We enjoyed it very much.

ontario-established.name: Glenview cottages and campground

Campground and rental cabins, pool, hot showers.

ontario-established.name: NET Camping Resort
ontario-established.notes: Established campground, we paid 48$ a night in the off-season for a very quiet and clean full hook up spot.

ontario-established.name: Grand Oaks RV Resort
ontario-established.notes:
Nice Campground located at a river. We booked a newbie offer with 20% off, so we ended up paying 170$ for 6 nights including water and electricity.

this resort is only open seasonally (may 1-oct 31)

ontario-established.name: Chippewa Park
ontario-established.notes:
Moderator Note: This place has seasonal closures.
......
Small park close to the lake with tables, baseball court, kids playground.
There are big parking lots and no signs that say "no overnight parking".
Plus: cheap gas on the way.

June 10, 2023 : 54$ for 1 night with services

ontario-established.name: Wild wood Golf and RV Resort
ontario-established.notes:
It is on a small well maintained golf course. There are full time residents in park models and lots of room for seasonal RV’s and over night travelers

63 Dollars a night for a Site

ontario-established.name: Elora Gorge Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes:
Full service and unserviced sites available. Sever km of walking trails around the campground, they even offer tube rides down the river. Extremely steep cliff faces, so watch you young ones. There are two bridges which allow access to the north side of the campground, be aware that these bridges are challenging enough for a pickup never mind a larger RV. There are some sites where you don't have to cross the bridges if you don't feel like attempting the crossing. The crossing is doable as there was some fifth wheel units parked on the north side. 

The town of Elora is a short drive, even a walk from the campground thru the day use area where there is restaurants and grocery stores, and other amenities. 

THIS CAMPGROUND IS A DRY CAMP GROUND. If they catch anyone drinking alcohol at any point they will kick you out.

ontario-established.name: Le Gîte du campeur
ontario-established.notes: 4 Wild sites near Lac Gaumond, Québec,Canada. Welcome R.V completly autonome, no services.Pedestryan trail, trout fishing, boat and canoë renting.

ontario-established.name: Esker Lakes Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
Provincial Park run by Ontario Parks.

Nice, quite, secluded park with only 100 or so campsites.

Offers full amenities, laundromat, showers, etc.

Great opportunity to view moose, bear and especially partridge. Opportunity to pick and eat wild blueberries in August is an awesome experience.

Campsites start around $40 a night, ~$5 more for electricity.

ontario-established.name: Wawa RV Resort and Campground
ontario-established.notes: Big campground with full amenities. pool, playground, laundry. Payed 35,- for electric for a small camper. Bigger ones are more expensive. Restaurants and fuel in town.

ontario-established.name: KOA Sault Ste. Marie
ontario-established.notes:
Expensive KOA, with well kept facilities, including mini golf and dog grooming salon. Prices start at 58,- Dollars.
Anyway couldn't connect to Wifi with two devices.

ontario-established.name: Willows Campground
ontario-established.notes: Very nice campground, RV, tents, hot shower, wifi, nice lake, fire pit, camping table, laundry. We paid 27$ + tx no services ( campervan). You can buy your firewood for 10$ ( big bag).

ontario-established.name: Voyageur Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Typical Provincial Park at Ottawa River, including dumping station. Showers were only slightly warm, maybe it's better at another building. The outlets for electricity are sometimes pretty far away from the sites, so a 10 m extension cord may be not enough.

ontario-established.name: Wild goose campground
ontario-established.notes: Nice camping near a lake. Very quiet and not expensive for : fire pit, wifi,camping table,hot shower and the view. We payed 25+ Tx ( no services).

ontario-established.name: George Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Nice campground on the lake. Several walking trails from the campground. In the middle of Killarney Provincial Park. Some sites are very private others less. We stayed at site 42 and had access to a big, flat rock overlooking the lake.
In summer season reservations are highly recommended, but there are about 10 non-reservable sites. Price for a van was about $37.

ontario-established.name: Camping de la montagne d'argent
ontario-established.notes:
Beautiful campsite, quiet and well maintained. Beautiful sandy beach by the red river.
---
Beau camping, calme et bien entretenu. Belle plage de sable au bord de la riviere rouge.

ontario-established.name: Birches Campground

Basic campground, 23$ per night (+11$ for a second vehicle, 2 vehicles allowed per pitch). Pitches are private with a lot of trees. The campground is right next to the lake and there are several hiking trails starting from the campground. Some washrooms are pit toilets (smells really bad) and some are flushing toilets (way better!)
There are no showers and no cell coverage either.

ontario-established.name: FaunENord Ecocamping
ontario-established.notes: Full service municipal campground near Chibougamau, QC on Route 167. (2 km to town). $32 for 2 services, more for 3 services, less for tenting. Picnic tables, fire pits. Nice clean showers and washrooms. Laundry available $1.50/ machine. Nice trail from campground near Lac Savauge.

ontario-established.name: Lake Embarras
ontario-established.notes: Stayed July 21 and the bugs were out pretty heavy. The sites are just off a nice beach with clear water. We were bothered by loud fisherman late into the night with lots of large RVs with expensive boats that are parked on that same beach. Nice place otherwise and has outhouse

ontario-established.name: Pickerel Park RV
ontario-established.notes: RV park for seasonal campers, but they accept overnighters, too. OK place, not unpleasant,  playground,  pool, lake with tiny beach. OK washrooms, toilets, laundry. We payed $ 48 for 2way 15 amps.

ontario-established.notes: This seems to be part trailer park, part seasonal campers. Accepts overnighters, too. Great quiet spot on a beautiful river, where you may swim. Pretty well kept, good wifi, washrooms rustic but clean and functioning. If you are short of something to read there's quite a library to chose from. Open grounds, little moskitos. Unexpensive, we payed 36 $ for a serviced site.

ontario-established.name: Earl Rowe Provincial Park

Not as quiet as some parks, can hear the road from the campsites but also next to a river so the sound of that is really nice. Definitely not as well maintained as some parks either, dog excrement was along the sides of some of the sites. Firefly show made for an awesome evening!

ontario-established.name: Crystal Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes:
$38 per site but a very nice place to stay. 

Private campground. Lots of grassy areas and our site was very level. We paid $50 for a pull thro with all services. The owners

ontario-established.name: Nipigon Marina and Campground

ontario-established.name: Plage Rouen Noranda
ontario-established.notes: a parking lot for RVs , 3 day maximum, picnic table, beach

ontario-established.name: Bronte provincial park campground

ontario-established.name: Barrage des quinze iles

ontario-established.name: Camping Lac Matagami
ontario-established.notes:
Excellent campground located on a magnificent lake.
Well maintained with all services.
Price for one day is $34 Canadian.

ontario-established.name: Mill Dam park
ontario-established.notes:
Nice park with Around 15 place for camping, camper or caravan.  Electricity, water, Child park and water game for child, pic-nic tables and restroom (no shower).  Really quiet and calm place.  
FREE CAMPING. Donation are accepted in a small box at the restroom.   It’s a public park, no personnel on the site. 

Near the bike path PPJ (piste cyclable du Pontiac)

ontario-established.name: Sandy Mountain Campsite
ontario-established.notes: Lovely, friendly wooded campsites with a pool, golf course, dumping and close to Kemptville and the nations capital, Ottawa

ontario-established.name: Beavermead Park
ontario-established.notes: City park by Little Lake. We slept in our van in the parking for one night with no problem. It was quiet until 7h30 am. There is a free beach nearby, and the park is overall really pretty. There is a campground next to the park where you could ask for a shower.

ontario-established.name: Sioux Narrows P. P.
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful quiet campground. Well kept. At beautiful Lake of the Woods. In my view nicest camping in the area. Canoe rental. Power at some sites. Spacious showers. --- Beau site de camping, bien entretenu, douches spacieuses, vue sur le lac, prix raisonnables.

ontario-established.name: Caliper Lake P. P.
ontario-established.notes: Another nice one. Well kept. Smaller shallower lake, relatively warm. Canoe, kayak, sub rental. Nice beach.

ontario-established.name: Camping Municipal Brownsburg-Chatham
ontario-established.notes:
Nice campground along Outaouais river. 
Possible to stay for the night only without services in the parking lot for $10.

ontario-established.name: Blyth fairgrounds
ontario-established.notes: Hundreds of sites, some shaded, at the fairgrounds in Blyth.  We were told by other campers to set up and that someone would come around in the morning to collect $30.  Walking distance to the Blyth theatre (award winning plays) and the Cowbell Brewery.

ontario-established.name: Brownlee Lake Park
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful campground on small lake. 2 km off Trans-Canada therefore quiet. Super clean, beach. serviced sites $35, unserviced $25 incl. shower plus tax. Wifi at office. Strongly recommended.

ontario-established.name: Agawa Bay Campground
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful Provincial Park campground right on the shores of Lake Superior. 3km of sandy/pebbly beach. There was heavy 1 meter to 1.5 meter surf and lots of wind the day we got there but was much calmer the next day. Lots of sites right on the beach and the whole campground is in a narrow strip between the beach and the highway, so the less windy sites are somewhat close to the highway. Decent amount of trees and some private spots. Flush toilets (but also pit toilets), free showers, potable water and dish cleaning stations. Ice and firewood available. ~$56 for the tent sites per night. We had data service for Telus there.

ontario-established.name: Parc national d'Opémican
ontario-established.notes: Provincial park.  Very beautifull but you can see the other cam site around you.

ontario-established.name: East Park Campground
ontario-established.notes: A really nice quiet and peaceful campground. Currently there are no electrical sites but in the near future there will be. There is a store onsite where you can buy some emergency items.

ontario-established.name: Camping de la Diable
ontario-established.notes:
expensive for electrical hook up @ $55. Laundry, swimming pool, games room. tenting sites for $45. good location to bike from. On side of river which would be great in good weather.  Some nice sites by river, others like a parking lot. 
worked for us to catch up on wi Fi and wash clothes.

ontario-established.name: Inwood Lake Park
ontario-established.notes: -with hook up $40-. -tents or no service $25-. (put it in an envelope) Next to a pretty sweet lake! Road noise: yes. I slept in my truck, payed $20 and it's absolutely worth it. You have to be out of the campsite at 12:00.

ontario-established.name: Fairview Park
ontario-established.notes: Nice little campground with tent sites, full hookup, flush toilets, showers... Not busy at this time so lot of space but might be busy in summer with not lot of privacy. Lovely river in the middle. 33$ for a tent site without water and electricity.

ontario-established.name: Ivy Lea Campground
ontario-established.notes: Nice campground. Some grass campsites some more into the woods. Washrooms and showers available.  Short drive off the 401. Main road nearby. Some road noise depending on the site you get

ontario-established.name: Lake Waswanipi
ontario-established.notes:
An 8 km gravel road from Highway 113 brings you to this beautiful place. There is a sandy beach with a boat launch, pit toilets, firepits and picnictables.
It's 5$ for a night.

ontario-established.name: Serpent River Campground
ontario-established.notes: Nice well kept campground with free hot showers. Free wifi near office, nice little trail to the river, lots of pull through sites. Well stocked store, some tent sites have water + 15amp, other primitive camping near the river. RV sites are only 30amp and no sewers but there is a dump station just outside the gate. Coin laundry on site. Close to the highway, you will hear highway noise. A bit pricey.

ontario-established.name: Penn Lake Park and Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Very clean and well-maintained campsite, seems always open. We arrived at 10:30pm.

Larger bathrooms, coin-operates laundry machines and 3 showers, including one accessible/family friendly.

Don’t need to camp here to use the facility - please leave the place better than you found it! They really deserve our gratitude and love.

ontario-established.name: Nicolston Dam RV Park
ontario-established.notes: RV Park in Ontario nestled on the Nottawasaga River Wind by the Nicol Family. Quiet and friendly, sides with 15 or 30 Amp and drinking water as well as no service sites. Laundry, showers, dump station, recycling, garbage, firewood ( 10CAD) & WiFi on sites

ontario-established.name: Grundy Lake Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Large provincial campground. Full amenities.

ontario-established.name: Lake Ste. Marie - Lac Ste Marie
ontario-established.notes:
Telephone: 819 467-5437 reservations. Launching ramp, places for travelers. $ 8.00 for parking. 
10 campsites, $ 35.00 for RVs. $ 25.00 for tents. 
Toilets, showers, electricity, Picnic table, fire pit, dump station, playground,

ontario-established.name: Davey Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes: it's a lot colder now so we are liking having power. many campground s are closed. this one open, nice manager, clean and heated bathroom, and reasonable price. we bought firewood too and had a nice evening.  Cute little lake here.

ontario-established.name: Rock Glen Family Resort
ontario-established.notes: Rock Glen is a member only resort that will allow you to stop in on your way thru if you traveling. They only allow a one night stay. If you are from a overseas country they will allow a longer stay. They are open year round.

ontario-established.name: Marie Louise Lake Campground - Sleeping Giant Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
200 sites available, almost half have electrical service. All have fire pits and picnic tables and close to vault (pit) toilets and water. Both comfort facilities have showers, restrooms with flush toilets and laundry facilities.
Sites vary in size to cater for tents, RVs (large and small) (dumping available), pull-throughs, group camping and 5 full service cabins also available. 
Canoes and kayaks available to rent and a boat launch is available.

ontario-established.name: Sandaraska park
ontario-established.notes: Nice, big camping, a lot of sites with and without hook-up, friendly staff and owners.

ontario-established.name: Sibbald Point Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Great campground. mix of powered and non powered sites.

ontario-established.name: Meldrum Bay Campsite
ontario-established.notes:
Big open sites right on the water. Amazing views!

The pin is for the camping area. It’s connected to the marina, I believe you have to check in with the harbourmaster to pay the site fees. 

As far I can remember the sites are fully serviced and there is a washroom with showers available. 
These are the current fees (for two people) according to their website:

Campsite with electricity: $40.00 per night.  
Campsite without electricity: $30.00 per night.
$5.00 per day for extra campers. 
Children under 16 are free.

ontario-established.name: Cedar Beach Resort
ontario-established.notes: Seasonal Campground for all camping types from tents to mobile homes.

ontario-established.name: Ingersoll municipalities campground
ontario-established.notes: Grass flat overnight spots, hydro and water at site. Bathrooms on location and a dump site available. Town has all amenities and auto part stores. Pay at site rates are cheap. Easy access just off main Highway.

ontario-established.name: Sturgeon Falls KOA
ontario-established.notes: Very nice spot by a river. Pull in water site Full service with patio, BBQ and dinette set

ontario-established.name: Mindemoya Court Cottages & Campground
ontario-established.notes: Cottage, Campground and RV resort located on crystal clear Lake Mindemoya, Manitoulin Island, Ontario, Canada. The resort offers over 18 acres of private groomed recreational area which includes a softball diamond, a volley ball court, horseshoe pit, bonfire pit and bicycle trails. The lake edge is clear and offer a brilliant sunset. Owners are friendly and kind. Out camp site had water and eletricity. Very good showers for a camping and clean bathroom.

ontario-established.name: Mountain Trout Camp
ontario-established.notes: Located 25 minutes from Tobermory, the MTC is at the edge of the Gillies Lake deepest cleanest inland lake in the Northern Bruce Peninsula. People are friendly even keeping social distance due the pandemic. Sites have electricity and clean water. Bathrooms are very clean and try he showers amazing! MTC offers a splendid sunset and there are many places to visit in a distance of 30 minutes from the camping. There are boats for rental and space for children ride bikes.

ontario-established.name: Selkirk Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
What You'll Like :
Quiet campground with grassed campsites
Wheeler’s Walk Trail with boardwalk across marsh wetland
Large day-use picnic area
15 minutes east of Port Dover
Monthly camping offered
General Information

ontario-established.name: Presqu'ile Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Many paid overnight sites, beautiful day stay opportunities right at the shore, beaches for swimming. Day stays included with Ontario Park Pass.

ontario-established.name: Bass Lake Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
Camping allowed May long weekend until Canadian Thanksgiving weekend.
Approx 10 minute drive west of Orillia, Ontario
2.8 km hiking trail
RV, car camping, group camping, picnic shelters and a day use area
Canoe, kayaks and paddle boat rentals and Park Store
Sandy beach on Bass Lake is great for swimming
Gas stations, groceries, convenience stores, restaurants, shopping and movie theatres within a five minute drive
Attractions within 30 minutes: Springwater Provincial Park, Discovery Harbour, Saint Marie among the Hurons, Wye Marsh, Casino Rama

ontario-established.name: Emily Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Great sites some quite big. Very nice sandy beach with boat launch on Pigeon Lake

ontario-established.name: Pog Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes: Second largest campground on Hwy 60. You can rent a boat, fish and there is a good place to swim. There are a few campsites that are not flat and you could have some issues on parking your RV or trailer. Tons of things to do at Algonguin Park.

ontario-established.name: Camp of the Woods
ontario-established.notes: Small established campground located on the banks of the Rainy River. Quiet, clean with great owner and staff.

ontario-established.name: Poplar Grove Campsite
ontario-established.notes: $47 per night. $975 per month. Spacious grounds. Fully serviced sites. Clean. Friendly management. 25 min to central Ottawa. Good shopping nearby. Great 11km walking loop. Extra fee for good Wi-Fi.  Showers/toilets closed due to COVID 19.

ontario-established.name: Happy Hearts Campground
ontario-established.notes: Nice campground just a little bit out of Tobermory. Nothing fancy but great for a stay for one night. Everything is clean and spots are big.

ontario-established.name: Aaron Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: The campground is in the Provincial Park Aaron. It works just like any other Provincial or National Park. You get to pick your own spot and they are not too expensive (Canada Explorer Pass does not apply here since it is Provincial). We stayed here one night and it was alright. There were no sinks to wash dishes which was unusual for parks like this. There's two very short hikes (around 1.2km each) in the park. The showers were still closed because of covid but bathrooms were available.

ontario-established.name: Oaster Lake Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Provincial park with nice sandy beach. Accessible for day use with standard day vehicle permit. Camping fees in the website link.

ontario-established.name: Pinecrest Trailer Park
ontario-established.notes: A trailer park right off highway 17 that has 4 tent sites right off the beach. It's $31 dollars for the non service site, they also have showers during covid.  Great place and would come back. They have a store at the office that sells junk food including ice cream!

ontario-established.name: west bay lodge
ontario-established.notes:
nice place face to the huron lake .
small but she found you a spot for 40 bucks 
the owners are so nice and kind 
safe and not far to the town 
the owner let me use the network on his front porch but no access on the campground
no shower because the covid-19

ontario-established.name: Riverlake Campground
ontario-established.notes: $54/day for RV spots, call ahead for overnight.

ontario-established.name: Camp Klahanie
ontario-established.notes:
Open May - Sept 
No restaurant, but they do have a store on site if you need some basic grocery items. Potable & non-potable water, dump station, showers, etc. Hydro & water nightly $51 - no hookups $40

ontario-established.name: Earlton RV's Courtesy Campground
ontario-established.notes: On highway 11, beside giant bison statue.  Flat gravel parking with picnic table.  At least 3 sites .  Water and electric available.

ontario-established.name: Woodland Park
ontario-established.notes: Camping full equiped with all the services for all types of camping gear. Verry clean, walking distance to Sauble beach village and beach

ontario-established.name: Kakabeka Falls Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful campground with large private sites, even for rvs. There are all the usual amenities of provincial parks, except the showers were closed due to Covid 19. Great platforms for viewing the falls and several hiking trails although not very exciting. At $60. including firewood, it was Very expensive considering we couldn't have a shower, which was why we stopped there in the first place.

ontario-established.name: Charlottenburg Park
ontario-established.notes: The campground is an Ontario Provincial park in Summerstown. It's a beautiful cozy green space on shores of the St. Lawrence sea way. it's children and pet friendly. price is reasonable. very quiet. seasonal only.

ontario-established.name: Sid Turcotte Park
ontario-established.notes: This is a nice campground in the downtown area of Mattawa near the hospital. It is clean and well run. There is a positive attitude here. The facilities are clean. Rates when here were $35.00 plus taxes for 15 amp site and water . Dump facilities available.

ontario-established.name: Cosmo Camping
ontario-established.notes: The 1000 Islands Camping Resort (now Cosmo Camping) is located in the heart of the 1000 islands on the 1000 Islands Parkway, midway between Gananoque and the 1000 Islands Bridge. North America's scenic playland is a cluster of more than 1,800 islands nestled in a fifty mile area of the St. Lawrence River between Ontario, Canada and New York State, USA. Personally, I was not impressed with this site or any of the other sites in that area,  but you are welcome to try it.  you may have a different experience.

ontario-established.name: Bala Sports Park - Muskoka Lakes Township
ontario-established.notes:
Clean washrooms with hot water, dog run, plenty of parking, accommodates even Class A motor coach. 
If you are into skate boarding, they have a free concrete facility for you enjoyment.

ontario-established.name: Round Lake Recreational Park
ontario-established.notes: Nice quiet camping at the recreational area. Picnic tables and covered gazebo. No other services/amenities.

ontario-established.name: Crosby Lake - Crown Land
ontario-established.notes: Crown Land campsites with a boat launch.  Four established sites and large open gravel area at shore for parking/ camping, boat trailer or RV spots.   Two first sites fit 30 ft trailers.  Access road is gravel and in good shape.  One star rating as it is Crown Land with no services, no cell service.

ontario-established.name: Sunny Lake - Crown Land
ontario-established.notes: About four established campsites on the north shore of Sunny Lake. Very tight short road into site off of a well maintained gravel access road.  One star rating is due to no services and very tight access road (200m).

ontario-established.name: Camping Lausanne
ontario-established.notes: Nice campground with everything.. nice cycle path.. lake etc..

ontario-established.name: Lac Philippe Campground (Gatineau Park)
ontario-established.notes: Public campground. Lots of amenities. Cost around $40 a night. Reservations are normally required, I was able to get a « first come first serve » site by calling ahead. (Comfort stations have sinks, laundry, electricity, showers)

ontario-established.name: Cliff Lake RV Camp
ontario-established.notes:
RV Spots: 14 full service sites, 30 Amp power, water, sewer & access to community TV hookup

Non-serviced site/Camping area: Large area for small or large groups with access to community Cook Shack (includes screened in eating area, fridge, stove, BBQ, dishwasher and TV room)

see web site for details, the site indicated that they will be open for the 2021 season

ontario-established.name: Tall Pines Camp
ontario-established.notes: stayed here for 4 nights to camp and fish, moderate rates, friendly people, we enjoyed our time here

ontario-established.name: Port Burwell provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
The 2.5 km sandy beach is one of most beautiful on the northern shore of Lake Erie.
An exceptional family friendly campground with large, well-treed, level sites as well as an outstanding play area for kids.
Family-friendly Discovery Drop-ins from July 1st to Labour Day.
Enjoy an amazing dog beach and pet exercise area with your four-legged friend.
The group camping area can accommodate big groups on sprawling, private sites.
An undiscovered birder’s paradise, experience the marvels of migration during the fall.

ontario-established.name: Camping Lac Schryer
ontario-established.notes: Camping with services. From large campers to little tent site.

ontario-established.name: Tottenham Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes: Small municipal campground. Book through website. Grassy sites for tents and RV's.  Water and power at RV sites.  Dump station available.  Firewood for sale.  All sites have table and fire pit.  There are playgrounds and a small beach area on the pond.  Disc golf field.  Rates from $24 to $33 a night. Weekly rates available.    No wifi but strong cell signal.  Short walk to main street with shops and a few restaurants. Access to trails. Access off 4th Line Road.

ontario-established.name: Assabaska Objibwa Heritage park
ontario-established.notes: Many campsites, quiet. Nice beaches and boat Launch. Hydro, sewer and water available. Mostly seasonal.

ontario-established.name: Camping gratuit St-Eugene de Guigues
ontario-established.notes:
Nice little municipal campsite.
about ten places, free without service, launching for boats, children's park, (swimming at your own risk) --- Beau petit camping municipal.
une dizaine de places, gratuite sans service, mise à l'eau pour bateaux, parc pour enfant, ( baignades à vos risques )

ontario-established.name: Turkey Point Provincial Campground
ontario-established.notes: Established Provincial Campground that has free day use Monday thru Thursday including showers, laundromat, water (and sani-dump, apparently).  Day use also gives access to the very nice beach for swimming.  We booked ahead for day use (no charge) but walkins maybe OK.  There is a charge for weekend day use and overnight camping.

ontario-established.name: Parc Municipal Parking

They play loud music and do karaoke, but they stop around 10-11pm, so it gives a nice ambiance until you to sleep. Ok

ontario-established.name: Harbour camping

ontario-established.name: Ryan's Campsite

ontario-established.name: Halte municipale Notre Dame de Pontmain

Camp sites with services (water and electricity) (8) and no service (18). The electricity on site is 30 amp and there's a dump station near the reception. The fee is $24+tx for a site without service and $32+tx for a site with 2 services. Wi-Fi available only near the reception.

ontario-established.notes:
Ontario provincial park. Electrical and non electric sites.
Quiet but dusty. Very clean. Large and small sites. Pet exercise beach

ontario-established.name: Badeswa (Mud lake)
ontario-established.notes: Established camp ground. $3 a person per night. Permits available at Pickle Lake municipal office. Boat launch.

ontario-established.name: Parc Provincial Marten River
ontario-established.notes: You can sleep here and fill up your water and it’s a beautiful place with a lake.

ontario-established.name: Lake Pinceau
ontario-established.notes: Nice camping spot suitable for any kind of camping. We stayed here for 1 night. Park has a 10 entrance fee plus 7 per night. It is located 14km after the park entrance on a gravel road (not to bad). There is room for multiple cars, but only one fire pit. Right by the lake. No cel phone signal.

ontario-established.name: Twin Lakes Camping
ontario-established.notes: Very large RV resort with man made lakes and lots of amenities. We were here at the end of the season so almost deserted. Full service sites, laundry , showers.

ontario-established.name: Arrowhead Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Large campground with large treed sites. Beaches, walks in the woods. No laundry or wifi. Weak cell service.

ontario-established.name: Mew Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes: Large level electrical sites. Electrical sites are further from the highway than the non-electrical ones. Treed sites. Small beach within campground. Showers and laundry. Sani-dump is down the highway.

ontario-established.name: McLaren  Campground
ontario-established.notes: Nicely treed, large level sites. Beach, laundry, sani-dump. Very weak cell phone signal. The showers need an update.

ontario-established.name: Nature’s Inn RV and Marina
ontario-established.notes: Simple RV and tenting park on the shores of Wabigoon Lake. Stopped here because HWY 17 was closed all day due to a collision. The couple that operate the park are nice. Facilities (shower and toilet) are quite old and dated, but clean enough. Paid $25 cash for a tent site for our campervan (no site services), which provided a great view of the lake. Sign in bathroom says sink water must be boiled before drinking - not sure about RV spot water hookups (we brought our own water). A great hiking trail across the parking lot - it’s not quite 2 miles, is flat and goes through forest and marsh areas in a big loop. That was an enjoyable find. This park is nothing special, but certainly better than spending even more hours sitting in traffic on a closed freeway! I’d stay here again.

ontario-established.name: Domaine Max & Lilly
ontario-established.notes: Camping, RV parking, limited services. Lake access, kayaks. Owner also has a short term rental suite. Animal friendly.

ontario-established.name: Long Sault, Ontario
ontario-established.notes:
Huge public park on Long Sault parkway, with picnic tables with possibility to prepare a little fire, on the beach, with a small information shelter. 

This is a Fee/ reservation location.

ontario-established.name: Camping Lebret
ontario-established.notes:
2 campsites on lake - 15$ per night - must reserve spot the sign says - managed by obikoba adventures - reservations at 819-761-4311 or aventuresobikoba.com 

You must reserve at 819 761-4311 and it is strictly forbidden to camp in the boat ramp for the safety of users

Amazing location easy for cars to access.

ontario-established.name: Calabogies lakeside camping & Rv resort
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful wild camping tent sites ,beach,washrooms,showers,store, and will accommodate  any type of rv. Hi speed internet with bell fibre coming spring 2022

ontario-established.notes:
Interesting holiday site, for camping, chalet, fishing, beach, swimming, camping, kayaking, boats ,Lots of people in high season

Site de vacance intéressant, pour le camping ,chalet ,pêche,plage,baignade,camping,kayak, bateau,mais beaucoup de monde en haute saison

ontario-established.name: Innerkip Trout Lake
ontario-established.notes: Campsite on Innerkip Quarry. Full site with power, water, and cell service.

ontario-established.name: Big Valley campground
ontario-established.notes: Owners are really laidback, community is friendly. 1/2 salt 1/2 chlorine pool, laundry ($3 wash, $2.25 dry) showers ($1). Seasonal, monthly, weekly and overnight sites. Also a few rustic cabins. Well water and advised not to drink but good for everything else.

ontario-established.name: PineHurst Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful natural campground and lake. It does cost $15 for a day pass. There is overnight camping available.

ontario-established.name: Ivanhoe Lake Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Nice ontario provincial park, with trail, canoe rental, beach with dog acces. Potable water available.

ontario-established.name: Mont Rigaud Ski Resort
ontario-established.notes: The Mont Rigaud ski hill offers 32 vanlife spots during they mountain bike season (May to end of October). Price is cheap, they give access to a shared fire pit, drinking water and toilets. The mountain offers hiking, mountain biking and rock climbing, as well as an obstacle course.

ontario-established.name: Lake Despair Lodge
ontario-established.notes:
A wonderful place, close to the lake. The Sitzes are in a small forest with shady trees. In the smalltalk Shop you may buy drinks and food. 
You also may use the Lodge's washing machine.
Fire pit, 30A electricity and City water at site

ontario-established.name: White River
ontario-established.notes:
Gass stop with some camp sites and a general store.
Slip for boat launch.
site is on the Indian Reserve, so Gas is generally cheaper.
We paid 10cents less than in Marthon a few miles back.

ontario-established.name: Six Mile Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Very lange campground, more than 300 sites close to the Six Mile Lake. Some with eletrcity. We had a Regularien site without any Service C$ 43.75 with park fee. On some sites you hear the traffic on HWY.

ontario-established.name: Carol's Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Large Campground close to the beach. Narrow sites with full Service. Free WIFI on sites.
C$45 incl. tax.

ontario-established.name: Killbear Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Large Campground with spacious sites, some with electricity near a wonderful sandy beach of Huron Lake. C$ 53,68

ontario-established.name: Algonquin Pines Campground
ontario-established.notes: Very nice campground, more than 80 spacious sites in a large pine forest. Most of them with water and electricity. Free WIFI, free showers, C$ 62. Laundry and dryer each C$ 2.75

ontario-established.name: Tobermory Village Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Quiet and clean family camping and RV sites, close to the national park and village of Tobermory. Big camping, a bit princier (52-68$/campsite), but calm with a variety of remote and more accessible sites.
Wifi at the main building.

ontario-established.name: Glengarry campground
ontario-established.notes: Ontario government run Campground, really beautiful right on the side of the St. Lawrence River. Minutes from the 401 highway. All the facilities, $39 for a tent one night.

ontario-established.name: Cache Campground
ontario-established.notes: Large campground on the lake. Couple of kilometres in from highway 144.

ontario-established.name: Rideau River Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Provincial Park with all the amenities you would expect. Friendly staff, clean new bathrooms and showers. There were a lot of mosquitos the night we were here.

ontario-established.name: Camping de la marina
ontario-established.notes: Three campsites in the town of Temiscamin near Lake Temiscamingue. There is water, electricity, toilets, showers. Place to discover.

ontario-established.name: Maple Ridge Family Campground and Restaurant
ontario-established.notes:
Large Campground suitable for big RVs,  also tents. Nice Owner. Just off highway 6, close to Bruce Peninsula National Park. 
We arrived on July 3. They had lots of sites available. The owner told us that it was fully booked the last weekend because of Canada Day. Clean, hot showers, Pets welcome, 75 $ per night, electricity, water, fireplace, dump station,

ontario-established.name: Ferris Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Typical provincial park that handles RVs with the associated amenities.  You can check the website I have included for more details and hours of operation.  The cost for dump and refill was 12 bucks.

ontario-established.name: Camping Municipal Lac St-Paul
ontario-established.notes:
Nice little municipal campground.
A lot of trees, large place for RVs.

ontario-established.name: Lazy Rock Campground
ontario-established.notes: Established campground. Very well setup. Nicest bathrooms and showers I've seen for a campground. Right on a lake with Wi-Fi, boats to rent, 2 docks (fishing and swimming). Sites are close together, but not bad. We stopped for 2 nights and we're enjoying it very much.

ontario-established.name: Loon Lake Resort
ontario-established.notes: We came in at the end of the day, there was nobody at the gate. So I ask someone about camping and suddenly everybody wanted to help, they found me a spot to pitch my tent. It has to be the most friendly place we ever encountered. The cost was $40 a night for a beautiful camping site clean and quiet. Utilities include washer and dryer shower washrooms. There is also access to a beach and a swimming pool. I would qualify the place more as a trailer parked on the camping site.

ontario-established.name: Camping des Cèdres
ontario-established.notes: Everyone is welcome, even the dog. They have their own beach.

ontario-established.name: Backcountry campingspot on Lookout Island
ontario-established.notes: Nice backcountry camping spot on Lookout Island. Only accessible by water. Beautiful sunset, fireplace and level ground for a 3 person tent.

ontario-established.name: E.M. Warwick conservation area
ontario-established.notes:
Campground.  I saw mostly tents.  
www.ltvca.ca 
Day use area and overnight

ontario-established.name: Darlington Park
ontario-established.notes: Provincial park near the highway.  50 minutes from Toronto.  Clean, large lot.  The electricity a bit far from the sit so I could not plug in my 30 amp but only 15 amps because I had to take an extension cord.  At night the train passes by the Hours and shouts.  This is disturbing.  Some sights seen on Lake Ontario.  It's splendid.  around $45 for 1 course.  There is a Park Store on site and the dump.

ontario-established.name: Windsor Campground
ontario-established.notes: Good campground place, a little noisy with the 401 road. Wifi available in the laundry.

ontario-established.name: Cardinal / Ottawa South KOA Holiday
ontario-established.notes:
Your standard KOA. 90 CAD for a 20/30 amp site with water (standard).

Activities, pool, playground etc.

ontario-established.name: Stop Along the Way Campground
ontario-established.notes:
This is their first year operating and they’ve done no advertising. A small family bought a house on what used to be a campground and decided to reopen all the RV hookups (full service spots!) and offer a place to stop while you travel. 

They offer spots with electricity and water and have a few with sewage dumps. They have place for RVs, tents and trailers. 

They offer longterm and one night stays, are super relaxed and have toilets and showers available. 

It’s basically in their backyard. They have at least 20 spots. We drove in without a reservation and they gave us a spot right away.

ontario-established.name: Cecile's Camping
ontario-established.notes:
A nice place for one night. About 10 sites only. Close to the Rte 11.
 Full hook up. Green meadow or  gravel, no shade. C$ 40.
Ablution did not work. Wifi did not work on our site!

ontario-established.name: Latibule Resort and Campground
ontario-established.notes: Nice and calm campground close to a lake. There are sunny and shady sites most of them with 2 services. Ablution are clean and smart. Only one shower. Fire rings and tables but no internet. Reception is 4G.

ontario-established.name: Providence bay tent and trailer park
ontario-established.notes:
Campground for tenting or RV’s
Near providence bay beach, with showers washrooms and a store for wood and ice.

ontario-established.name: Lac des milles lodge
ontario-established.notes:
This beautiful resort is located on the northwest tip of lac des mille lacs about 160km west of Thunder Bay. 

This resort is run by a lovely family. They have cabins and a campground. The grounds are beautifully ket and if you are Into fishing, you are sure to be satisfied.

ontario-established.name: Two rivers lake campground
ontario-established.notes: Provincial campground. Pine forest campsites packed in with people in the summer.  When we visited in late august, they had a water shortage which meant no safe water fill ups and no showers. Pit toilets reeked. Not ideal for this region.

ontario-established.name: Rock Lake Campground
ontario-established.notes: Smaller campground with lots of shade.  Doesn't seem to be big rig friendly but great for a camper van.  Rock Lake has good swimming and there is good water on site along with standard campground services.  Firewood from the camp store was wet.

ontario-established.name: Scott's Campground
ontario-established.notes: regular everyday campground.  30amp, 50amp, tents,  electricity water and dump avail.  pool (heated).  wood $10 for a blue recycling bin full.

ontario-established.name: Fanshawe Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes: Perfect day use spot. Water available as well as public washrooms. Trails for biking or hiking (all levels) as well as boat launch for small motorized or kayaking/ canoeing. Offers overnight sites but book online ahead of time to ensure availability. Camp area offers pay-per-use laundry, dump station and free showers but seasonal sites are for RVs only, no tent or van conversions. (Nightly or weekly is ok for any camping: tent, van conversion, RV).

ontario-established.name: Marina Chibougamau
ontario-established.notes:
Multi service including camping for all types of vehicles and cabins. Access to Lac Doré from there.

Multi service incluant camping pour tous les types de véhicules et chalets.
Accès sur le lac Doré à partir de là.

ontario-established.name: Camping Ange-Gardien
ontario-established.notes:
Nice place near Hull. 2-3 services. Pool. dump station.
....
Belle endroit près de Hull
2 ou 3 services  ,piscine ,d’épandeur eau ,station vidange

ontario-established.name: campers corner campground
ontario-established.notes: Family camp ground .with heated indoor pool. Friendly staff, and quiet spaces

ontario-established.name: Bell Falls Family Campground
ontario-established.notes: Lovely family owned place, with history back to WWII. Hot showers and running toilets. Mostly seasonal trailers here but spots for tents or campers for overnights. Small falls on site.

ontario-established.name: Mine Mill CAW Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Right next to Carol’s. $45/night for 30 amp pull through spot. Potable water in sites. Free wifi. 
Gates to site close at 8pm, you will have to ask for a fob key and deposit $20 if you want to go in and out.
No privacy but okay for one night. Some long term trailers set up.
Right on Richard Lake. Beach, soccer field, dog beach also.

ontario-established.name: Norm’s tent & trailer
ontario-established.notes:
Beautiful campsite on the water's edge! $29 for the night without service!
—-
Beau camping sur le bord de l’eau! 29$ pour la nuit sans service!

ontario-established.name: Wesley Clover Parks Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Great campground under trees. By the highway 417, so we hear trafic. Wifi at the office. Large and private sites.
Be advised. There was a 50$ refundable security deposit taken on my credit card. It was never refunded and no answers to my email and phone calls. The campground is closed for winter.

ontario-established.name: Avonmore Oasis Camping
ontario-established.notes: Great open spot surrounded by trees, fire pits, pond, camping benches, portapotty, showers and running water. RV’s/camper vans and tents allowed. Owner super helpful and easy going. No wifi but there is a fine phone signal.

ontario-established.name: The Pinery Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes:
This is a typical Ontario Parks campground.  Very nice, great beach, trails, this one even had a store.  Evening programs some nights, canoe rentals, etc.  This park has many hundreds of sites, some electric.  Expect to pay around $40C per night.

My only complaint is that the showers were on the cool side (in mid-October),  however, most campgrounds are closed by this time of the year, so I am glad that I got a shower.  One of the other shower buildings had hotter water. Bathrooms and showers were exceptionally clean.  Sites all had plenty of privacy.  

Overall a great park and campground.

ontario-established.name: Bingemans
ontario-established.notes: Multipurpose recreation center with a water park, bowling & a big outdoor stage, plus a campground

ontario-established.name: Rockwood Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes: Tranquil preserve offering limestone cliffs, a recreational river, caves, hiking trails & campsites.

ontario-established.name: Shawville, Quebec - Mill Dam Park
ontario-established.notes:
Beautiful park with about six full service sites for $20/night.  Free tent camping for three nights (see photo of sign).  Toilets. Dump station and "spring water" available.  Dump station is $5 by donation. 

Lovely splash pad for the kids, on a small creek.  Picnic tables.   Worth the stop.

ontario-established.name: Samuel Champlain Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: Beautiful campground with sites on the water.  Small store for items and check in when entry booth is closed.  $43 CAN for a site without power/water.

ontario-established.name: Awenda Provincial Park
ontario-established.notes: incredible place to stay that's far enough north to be wild and green, but not too far where you feel like you've driven forever from the GTA

ontario-established.name: The Old Homestead Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Full service campground with many small and large overnight and seasonal sites. Close to beautiful town of Bayfield with beach, browsing, restaurants and shopping. 
The Old Homestead offers quality family camping at a unique trailer park facility. The park is proudly owned and operated by the Keller Family for over 30 years.

ontario-established.name: Jellystone Park
ontario-established.notes:
a family oriented campground suitable for all sizes of RV overlander or road only vehicles.  pets are allowed and it has a general store for most of your needs. close to niagara falls and safari niagara. good enough atmosphere staff were all friendly  ... has a pool bouncy pillow larger attractions as well (some require extra payment) but for our four kids there was plenty for them to do and keep them occupied when we were not sight seeing ;) they also have cabins, yurts, and trailers for rent as well if that is more your style. some of the sites are tight but cheaper than a hotel and better fires.. the wood sold here colst 11.30 CAD and was just under a cubic foot of good hardwood. close to a major highway but it is a place for the kids to burn off some energy and you get some rest.  would come back..

we have had a minivan with a 1959 sportscraft 15 foot overall trailer. we were the tiny one of the bunch by far.

happy camping

ontario-established.name: Twilight Resort
ontario-established.notes: Small Campground with some cabins at the lake. As the office was closed, I called the attendant. He told me that the rate is 58$ plus tax. We should take a spot and he would collect the fee in the evening. When he finally arrived, the fee came up to 97$ inkl. tax. This price is way to expensive so we decided to move on. It's a pitty, because the view over the lake is great and there is a good pebble beach.

ontario-established.name: Solitude Nature Reserve
ontario-established.notes: Amazing free campsite! Beautiful nature preserve with walking trails open to the public. Also 6 campsites (2 drive up, 4 walk-in tent sites) that are accessed thru a locked gate.  Contact the park, at https://solitudenaturereserve.com/location/  to reserve your site and get the code for the lock. The sign at the park says it is available for weekend camping but we contacted and asked to camp on a Sun and Mon night and that was ok. Our site was huge, plenty big enough for our 2 vans (we were traveling with another couple). There were 2 picnic tables, a fire pit, and a composting toilet at our site. Beautiful.flowers all around, nice morning walk on the trails. No payable water.

ontario-established.name: Rocher Rogue Campground
ontario-established.notes: Found this place via Google Maps. Cash only. We were charged $35 per night. Rustic campsites. Beautiful view of the water at some of the spots. Some of the van/trailer spots filled with semi-permanent trailers. Good Rogers/AT&T signal.

ontario-established.name: Ferguson Farm Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Wonderfull clean and well mantained. 
Good for all types from tents to big rigs. Very friendly owners, beach at the lake and good fishing. Wide grass area to stay, mostly flat.

ontario-established.name: Kingston Mills (Parks Canada)
ontario-established.notes: Parks Canada allows to pitch a tent anywhere, 5$/person, with access to a bathroom. Gps point put at the information building, which closes at 7pm. You can swim in the canal. Train passes really close to parking lot. We went by the lake, opposite side of the road (in a tent) to get farther from the train

ontario-established.name: Camping lac du cerf
ontario-established.notes: Nice place to relax. Small camping next to a lake and little beach for kids

ontario-established.name: Shangri-La Niagara campground
ontario-established.notes: Paid $56 for a site without services, one of few campgrounds without a 3 day minimum stay. Lots of seasonals. Hot showers and flush toilets included in fee. Bathroom is rustic and adequate. Wifi usable sporadically around play area.

ontario-established.name: Chukuni River RV Tent and Trailer Park
ontario-established.notes: Pull through sites 30 amp Showerhouse , docks , fish cleaning shack, close to town, boat launch ,

ontario-established.name: Fifty Point Conservation Area
ontario-established.notes:
Fifty Point Conservation Area on Lake Ontario, a magnificent 80-hectare park with superb marina facilities in Stoney Creek. It’s the place to be for a swim in Lake Ontario, family camping or a picnic for groups of any size.

Visitors can also enjoy a fabulous lakefront view by walking our promenade or while relaxing at conveniently located benches and shaded areas.

https://conservationhamilton.ca/conservation-areas/fifty-point-conservation-area/

ontario-established.name: Balsam Lake Provincial Park. Dumpstation.

ontario-established.name: Harmony resorts Grand Valley

ontario-established.name: Happy Green Acres

ontario-established.name: Toronto West Campground
ontario-established.notes:
Lots of long term, but have several pull thru sites with full hookups including 50amp power, water and sewer.

Sites are very long, plenty of room for 43' towing jeep, plus more space. Some sites they back to back in the one pull thru site and there's still plenty of room.

If you have a mounted Starlink , most sites have large trees on both sides, which is great for shade, but causes major interruptions to Starlink.

Managers are very friendly and helpful!

Pets are welcome.

ontario-established.name: Camp park Resort
ontario-established.notes: Huge camp ground with tons of things for the kids to do. Can fit all different sizes of RV’s , Tenting, with tons of washrooms, and laundry facility. Restaurant on the camp grounds. Fire pit picnic bench on your site. Reasonably priced to stay here also. Large sites here also.

ontario-established.name: Laurel Creek Conservation
ontario-established.notes: Good cell phone signal.  Walking trails and kayaking available.  Some low income families living on campsite for the summer.

ontario-established.name: Cedar Valley Resort

Beautiful place in the woods

The owner started our campfire.
Propane, clean washrooms, hot showers, play area, trout fishing and more.
$35 no service

ontario-established.name: KOA Camp ground

ontario-informal.name: Kenora

ontario-informal.name: Parking Lot - Niagara Falls
ontario-informal.notes: Very large parking lot in the center of Niagara Falls. Just some minutes per feet to the falls. Very quiet during the night. With 20 CAD/24 hours might be the cheapest option.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Supercenter
ontario-informal.notes: Very friendly staff when we asked if it is ok to stay. Very quiet and zero dollars. Great and very fast WiFi if you are parking a little bit closer to the building - we used to work on our blog. Great place!

ontario-informal.name: Canada Auto Parks
ontario-informal.notes:
Moderator Note: Please confirm that it is OK to stay overnight in your vehicle.
.....
Parking lot in Toronto Downtown - it is a 20-30 minutes walk to the CN-Tower or just 2 blocks away from the next underground-station. Not the most beautiful place on earth but in the center and surprisingly quiet during the night - the workers on the nearby construction site waited until 9AM (!) to start with concrete drilling and other noisy things. We didn't ask if it is ok to stay in the car for the night and just did it. No facilities. We paid 65 CAN for 2 nights. Close to the CN-tower there are other parking lots as well so there are perhaps other options to stay downtown.

ontario-informal.name: Melgund Lake
ontario-informal.notes: Super nice camping spot at a small lake. We watched the beavers working on their dam while having breakfast. Fire ring. Lots of bugs. Large spot which could fit a couple of campers.

ontario-informal.name: Penn Lake, Marathon
ontario-informal.notes:
Now open June 7th. 
The campground at the Penn Lake in Marathon was still closed for the season, but we were allowed to stay at the parking lot of the day use area and they opened the restrooms for us. We could us the showers at the swimming hall in town.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart

Spaces are car-sized and NOT level.

ontario-informal.name: Bruce Mines - Bobbers Restaurant

ontario-informal.name: Hearst

ontario-informal.name: Ottawa - Walmart

ontario-informal.name: Rest area

Pit toilets no water.

ontario-informal.name: Bayfront Park

ontario-informal.name: Mission Island boat launch
ontario-informal.notes:
A grass parking for boat lover with wild goose and deer.

This is a public place for people to put their boat in water.

ontario-informal.name: Helen Lake Rest Area

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Supercentre Thunder Bay

ontario-informal.name: Palgrave forest trail parking lot

ontario-informal.name: Bendor amd Graves Tract

ontario-informal.name: Arnprior Marina

ontario-informal.name: Gemmil Park

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Kingston super centre

ontario-informal.name: Fort Erie

Small parking lot for vans and small rigs like my 22 ft for free or large parking lot of boat ramp for 10$.
Washrooms.  Playground for kids. Water and washrooms available.

ontario-informal.name: Arnprior R. Simpson Park

ontario-informal.name: Parking municipal

ontario-informal.name: Esso

ontario-informal.name: Private residence
ontario-informal.notes:
Hello!

ontario-informal.name: Uppsala Curling Club

ontario-informal.name: The Cell Tower - Rd 655

ontario-informal.name: White River Tourist Information Centre
ontario-informal.notes:

esso gas station with overnight truck stop.  
 Country style coffee.

ontario-informal.name: Dufferin Island Park

ontario-informal.name: Blind River Community Center

Big parking lot next to the river and the marina. Toilets in 2 minutes walk at the tennis court. Very quiet place.
Hot showers and washing machines available at Blind River Marina.

ontario-informal.name: Parking

ontario-informal.name: onRoute
ontario-informal.notes: Bathroom, water, snacks available 24hr.  Lots of parking.  No stress.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Woodstock
ontario-informal.notes: Very quiet Walmart parking lot. Park near the shop Payless Shoes Source.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart
ontario-informal.notes: Great Walmart lot just outside of Hanover. Typical road noise during day but quiet at night. Big grassy area on east side of lot for anyone traveling with dogs. Currently no “no overnight parking” signs.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Fort Francis
ontario-informal.notes: Walmart carpark - pretty standard fare, but right on the edge of the city so nice and quiet.

ontario-informal.name: The Home Depot 99 Cross Ave

ontario-informal.name: Mohawk Slots Casino
ontario-informal.notes: You can stay overnight on the huge parking lot. Register with security. Unfortunately no shade, but tons of free play and free food vouchers if you make a players card ;-)

ontario-informal.name: Flying J
ontario-informal.notes: Parking near the highway, not too noisy. With showers (not free) and toilets.

ontario-informal.name: ONroute Trenton South
ontario-informal.notes: Stop on the highway with Fuel, washrooms, restaurants, WiFi.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Smiths Falls
ontario-informal.notes:
Walmart Smiths falls.
Near road 15 so a bit noisy.
Take time to visit the water lock (sluice).

ontario-informal.name: Flying J
ontario-informal.notes: Truck parking with a new gas station, almost no people but there is truck noise.

ontario-informal.name: Pizza hut Dryden
ontario-informal.notes:
Overnight parking far behind the restaurant. I asked the manager and he said we were welcome. Obviously we ate at the restaurant. 
Canadian Tire store next to the restaurant. Train tracks opposite the restaurant, nice little town, there is a Walmart not far also.

ontario-informal.name: Cineplex
ontario-informal.notes:
We went to the movies and asked to stay in the parking lot for the night. No issues.
Just a far away background noise of the motorway.
Tuesday is a promotional night for the movie tickets.

ontario-informal.name: Tim Horton parking lot
ontario-informal.notes:
Big sign welcoming rv's.
Restaurant is in Perth on hwy 7. Coordinates will be off a bit because we were driving.

ontario-informal.name: Lodge Lake Park (before was:Highway 17 Rest Stop with Beautiful Lake
ontario-informal.notes: As the title says there is a beautiful Lake with lily pads and a rest stop beside. Picnic tables, toilets, lots of room for cars and a separate area for big rigs.

ontario-informal.name: Parry Sound
ontario-informal.notes: At the Harbour. Gravel parking lot of the Island Queen Cruise. Overnight is permitted by this company, costs 10 $. Night between 11 p.m and 6 a.m was very quiet. There were noisy freight trains at 11 p.m and 6 a.m. It's a nice place. There is a sign about the overnight parking rule - photo enclosed.

ontario-informal.name: Brambleberry Farm
ontario-informal.notes: Brambleberry Farm is a Pick your own fruit farm located 20min north of the 401 between Toronto and Kingston.  The farm store has fresh picked fruit and vegetables and drinks depending on the season. you can pick your own fruit price is by weight of amount picked. prices vary on type of fruit picked. eg. Strawberries,Raspberries,Blueberries,Black and red Currents, gooseberries and cherries.

ontario-informal.name: Shorelines Casino (Thousand Islands )
ontario-informal.notes: free spot to overnight. casino parking lot. fairly quiet but it is close to Hwy 401. RVs parked at far end of parking lot.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Renfrew
ontario-informal.notes: Nice quiet place.  Huge parking lot.  Ask the customer service and said there was no problem.  Dump station on the other side on the street at the visitor center. We parked near Canadian Tire and used their free WiFi until they closed at 11pm.

ontario-informal.name: Cloyne General Store Parking Lot
ontario-informal.notes:
This is just a parking lot beside the Cloyne General Store. We were running out of options in the evening and asked the very kind shopkeeper of the Shell station if we could just park our self-sufficient class B camper in the large lot outside.  He was kind enough to say yes while accepting no responsibility for anything that might happen. (In a small Ontario town, nothing is going to happen).

They are open until 9pm. It’s like a quiet truck stop without trucks nor showers. 

I would definitely ask for permission and in exchange for kindness, buy something and help his business; it may help this spot to remain permissible.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Stockyard
ontario-informal.notes: Walmart Supercentre open until 11pm. One night okay, Tim Hortons, Subway next to the parking lot. Possibility to take buses. It's nice to ride to downtown.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Orangeville
ontario-informal.notes:
Large common parking lot of Walmart Orangeville. Didn't see any signs porhibiting overnight parking.
Stayed here for a couple of nights without a problem. Can pick up the Canadian Tire wifi from quite far away.
We parked near 24 hour gym so no one bothered with us.
Parking lot quite well lit during the night..

ontario-informal.name: Green spot next to baseball field
ontario-informal.notes:
Nice quiet green spot near the backsite of community center with baseball, hockey and football field.
Only small oneway road nearby.
Two simple toilets available.

ontario-informal.name: Manitowaning Welcome Center
ontario-informal.notes:
Nice place. Close to the road but ok for 1 night. Some grass, 2 pit toilets (really clean!) and even a sink to wash your hands and free wifi ! 
The Center and the book store are open from 10am to 4pm from Tuesday to Saturday.

ontario-informal.name: Chibougamo
ontario-informal.notes: Small parking of the water department of the town. Near the lake with beautiful view. Some noise of the main street. Used by the employees, did not stay too late even if nobody asked us to leave.

ontario-informal.name: Rivière Rupert
ontario-informal.notes:
3.2 Km from Route de la Baie-James.
4 campsites next to the river.
Level sites with fire ring.
Cellphone is not available here.

ontario-informal.name: Nipigon Panorama Lookout
ontario-informal.notes:
This wasn't exactly on the co-ordinates or I mis-read but in any case it was close....the co-ords told me it was across the street but obviusly the water side of the highway is what you want.
Area is a little dirty and the water is shallow so no fishing.
The day we arrived it was foggy and raining, as you can see in the picture but it was very attractive and although quite open...very private.
We enjoyed out stay here.
Just a note that further along the shore, as seen in the picture, there is a sandy beach which might allo0w swimming when it's warm.
Lots of room for several big RV's

ontario-informal.name: Rotary Park
ontario-informal.notes:
Parking lot. Toilets, picnic tables, a gentle river to swim in. Busy during the day, quiet at night. No “no overnight parking/camping” signs. A local also said it’s pretty relaxed around here so people likely won’t mind. 
I wouldn’t tent camp and I think a camper van is going to be fine.  
Got full bars of LTE internet on Telus. 

You can hear car traffic in the distance.

ontario-informal.name: Litchfield Route Stop/Rest on highway 148
ontario-informal.notes: it is located on a local highway, friendly large green area with toilets, drinking water and picnic tables. you can sleep overnight. low noise as cars don't pass by frequently. starry sky (no light pollution). great place.

ontario-informal.name: Lac Duncan km574
ontario-informal.notes: The site is okay for one night but le road is very bumpy (8km) on site there are picnic tables, fire pit and toilettes. A nice lake vieux and boat ramp. Poor network (in and out).

ontario-informal.name: Parking for big rigs
ontario-informal.notes:
15$ per 24h until 5am only, you have to pay twice if your RV is on 2 places.
$5 on PH and weekends.
Very close to the city center, 15min walk with kids.

ontario-informal.name: Stardust Drive-In Theater
ontario-informal.notes: Drive-in theater we pass by accident. Went in and asked if we could stay overnight. Manager said it's all right. A lot of people fall asleep and leave the next morning. So we watched a movie and stayed over night.

ontario-informal.name: Cabela's Parking
ontario-informal.notes: Parking at Cabelas store. We stayed on the left side with sign "RV parking" which has shade in the afternoon. Opening hours: Mo-Sa  9am-9pm, Su, 9am-6pm, Toilets and WiFi during store hours. Some street noise from highway in the distance otherwise very quiet.

ontario-informal.name: on route Napanee
ontario-informal.notes: rest stop with restaurants, fuel, washrooms and wifi

ontario-informal.name: Camping @ Newton Street Art Barn
ontario-informal.notes:
A beautiful country property that has been opened to all types of overlanders (including  big rigs). We came here initially to visit the Art Barn. There is a 15-20 minute walk through the forest to a creek. There are dogs living here who are very friendly. Please call prior to arrival to arrange camping! Clean bathroom and shower as well as potable water available. Accepting donations for camping fee. Highly recommend! 
Debbie (705) 427-2119

ontario-informal.name: Marathon Centre Mall Parking Lot
ontario-informal.notes: I was told by a person working at the Mobil gas station and a 2nd person working in The Independent grocery store that RV parking is permitted. It's right next to the OPP detachment office and I wasn't bothered. A couple 18 wheelers were parked nearby. One ran its engine all night.

ontario-informal.name: Husky/Esso 24/7 Truck Stop
ontario-informal.notes:
Another Husky Truck stop / Travel center

This places are amazing!
Located from BC (Chilliwack) to Ontario (Kingston) close to the main Highways.
Recognizable by a huuuge Canadian Flag next to it.
Shop (with toilets, laundromat and showers) is open 24/7.
Also have a restaurant and usually free wifi (not always tho).

Before you use the showers: go to the counter, sign up for a husky rewards card, download the app and subscribe to the newsletter. 
You instantly get 200 rewards points only for that! 
Also you can find other Husky Truck Stops / Travel Centers with the app!

A shower (if you bring your own towl) is only 50 points (or ~8$)! 
(If you need a towel it is 100 points or ~10$).

The showers are AMAZING!
Super clean, you have no time limit and get a whole private bathroom. (You can even bring your phone and powerbank in to charge meanwhile).

Laundry is usually coin system and around 1,25$ for washing and 1,25$ for dryer (1h).

Even tho it is no problem, I would not recommend to sleep here (as it gets very loud next to the street and because some truckers leave their engine running the whole night).

Big rigs would fit, places are meant for the truckers tho!! No problem for small vehicles.

ontario-informal.name: Besides Motel Super 8
ontario-informal.notes:
566 Lakeshore Drive. Just on the north side of Super 8 Motel. 
No more home on that lot. Access to the lake on the other side of the road

ontario-informal.name: New Liskeard - Walmart
ontario-informal.notes: Typical Walmart. Close to the highway but wasn’t overly noisy. Some big rigs and a couple other RVs while we were here. Walmart hours were 7am-10pm. As it’s a smaller town, the lot is a bit smaller than the ones you’d find in a larger city. Toilets inside during opening hours and some fast food places nearby that may have wifi.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart Brockville
ontario-informal.notes:
Hello
One more Walmart for night. 
Lot of places, lot of Wi-Fi, lot of shops, and also, lot of noise..!!! :)
Not more noisy than other Walmart or some RV park...
Have a sweet night 
Thank to Walmart for this place.

ontario-informal.name: Walmart
