Attention, tree branches hang down, even with our 2.4m Toyo we had to bend away so they do not hang on the roof 2 branches.

ontario-wild.name: Level-sur-Quévillon - NICE
ontario-wild.notes:
Cute sleeping place right on the river. Has some black flies and near road, but hardly any traffic. Beautiful sunset, relaxing water rapids sounds makes you feel alone..
Phone service not so good, but ok.

ontario-wild.name: Marten River - OK
ontario-wild.notes: Sleeping place a bit off the road in the bush. Had hell of a lot of mosquitoes, otherwise ok as an alternative to the super expensive Provincial Park Camping ($ 38!). Only few 100m from here is the car park to splash down to the canoe in the Wickstead Lake or Marten River Lake.

ontario-wild.name: Vor Kenora - OK
ontario-wild.notes: Sleeping place a bit off the road. Needs 4x4, but was only ne short distance. You can hear road and airport still good. Had millions of mosquitoes at nightfall.

ontario-wild.name: Vor Lake Superior Prov Park - OK
ontario-wild.notes: Roost near the entrance to Lake Superior Prov Park. Well hidden from the road. Little traffic, but you can hear the truck's good when they rush past. For this you can go in the morning purely Prov Park.

ontario-wild.name: Kaministiquia River
ontario-wild.notes: Dead end of a gravel road, close to train tracks, but there was no train at night.

ontario-wild.name: Boat Launch - Gravel Area
ontario-wild.notes: free, next to the road but quiet- follow the road for the boat launch and park there. quiet and no signs saying no camping.

ontario-wild.name: Dogtooth Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Hidden pull off to dogtooth lake, scenic, and free.

ontario-wild.name: Budd Lake - Highway 101
ontario-wild.notes: On Budd Lake. Near Highway 101. Not a lot traffic. No cell service with Telus. Some intermittent H+ service by the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Heron Bay
ontario-wild.notes: Quite place on the River. A bad small paved road (from the 627) goes to the old town site. But there are no longer any building. The steep hill down is maybe not for any car. But there a lot of place around to stay on gras.

ontario-wild.name: Pancake Bay - Lake Superior
ontario-wild.notes: A hidden place next to the street with 4 or 5 options to find a nice view directly to Lake Superior. The street you can hear a little bit. Despite we had a rainy day we had enjoyed the view and a great lazy day at this place. If the weather is well, you can go swimming in the lake. Few great spots to go fishing too. There is a loop at the end of the road for turning around.

ontario-wild.name: Alona Bay - (Lake Superior)
ontario-wild.notes: Small flat place in the wood above the lake at Alona bay. Take the paved road near the senic outlook to Alona bay, there is space for bigger RVs or drive some meters down a dirt road to a small flat pace, good for one car, maybe 4WD good to drive  down to the place. Steep path down to the pebbled beach and great view over the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Luther bird sanctuary
ontario-wild.notes: We took the dead end road beside the bird sanctuary and parked in a nice field with many flowers and many more mosquitos. very quiet and level. We had Internet with T mobile.

ontario-wild.name: Rest place At Highway 17
ontario-wild.notes: nice picnic area, no sign for no overnight, good view over the lake, quiet at night

ontario-wild.name: At Highway 50
ontario-wild.notes: it is a gravel place near Highway, like a small rest area with a picnic table and garbage bin, good for a night

ontario-wild.name: Small Rocky Beach - Just Off Hwy17
ontario-wild.notes: One campsite. Large swimming area, can be busy. Stone/Pebble Beach, some sand. Great view!

ontario-wild.name: Closed Road
ontario-wild.notes: Several nice spots along the closed road. Sign says enter at own risk

ontario-wild.name: Grouse lake & Teapot lake
ontario-wild.notes: Small treed site off of logging road at Grouse lake. Gravel parking lot with boat launch at Teapot lake.

ontario-wild.name: South of highway 11
ontario-wild.notes:
Very quiet place for a night. There is space on the rock even for larger vehicles. 

No RVs , no place to turn, tents only

ontario-wild.name: Godson Lake
ontario-wild.notes: This is a camping area on Crown land, free, several sites, very popular with boondocking anglers. Pit privy, and fire pits.

ontario-wild.name: Rouyn-Noranda
ontario-wild.notes:
Behind the end of paved road in a small forest, dirty gravel parking, quiet.
Good for one night. Not far away from Walmart.

ontario-wild.name: Secret Lake Wild Camp
ontario-wild.notes: Nice and peaceful place on your private Lake! Just follow a very old unmainted Road in to the Forest, then torn right and drive over the Rocks to the lake...! not easy to level the Car. Just possible with small 4x4 Cars/Campers and high clearance!!

ontario-wild.name: Riverside Wild Camp
ontario-wild.notes: Very Beautifull place above the River. Firepit and lots of Moskitos...;-) Just for small Cars/Campers because of low hanging Trees and narrow road!

ontario-wild.name: Port Colborne
ontario-wild.notes:
MODERATOR NOTE: WARNING! Thefts and vandalism reported in this location. Please use caution. 


Parkinglot / Park at the marina. Boatramp near by. Quiet at nicht. Nice breez from the lake. Big Rig could be a problem if it looks like a RV.

ontario-wild.name: Forest clearing Camp off Highway 11
ontario-wild.notes: Forest Clearing at dead end track 100 metres from Highway 11. Can't be seen from main road.

ontario-wild.name: Point North, Trans-Tiaga West
ontario-wild.notes: Old road and clearing on hill. Nice level site and quiet. Tried to camp at the point but too crowded

ontario-wild.name: Pont Ferme. End of the Road
ontario-wild.notes: End of a long gravel road next to a stream. Fairly rough with an unsafe bridge at the end so doubt much traffic. Very quiet

ontario-wild.name: Towerview
ontario-wild.notes: 2 flat spots at the end of 4wd road on hill. Next to radio tower

ontario-wild.name: Ghost Town Joutel
ontario-wild.notes: Former site of the mining town Joutel. lots of roads but no houses. take your choice.

ontario-wild.name: Wildcamping at creek
ontario-wild.notes: Place for wildcamping next to a creek. It's still pretty close to the highway so you may hear the traffic a little bit.

ontario-wild.name: wild, nice,
ontario-wild.notes: wild, nice place. 4x4 need. near local road but quiet

ontario-wild.name: Dans la nature
ontario-wild.notes:
The area is been used by fishermen and workers. 
I took the dirt road and at the 1st intersection with a private road there is a small area where you can park in the forest just before the private road. The neighbors were okay to let us stay. Tent okay. 4WD recommended.

ontario-wild.name: Crown land site
ontario-wild.notes:
There is some spot at this location. This is crown land close to the park Algonquin. You will need a high clearance vehicle to access the trail.

Roughly enough space for a JKU to pass between the trees, trailers needed some magic.

Be careful in the hunting season!

ontario-wild.name: Minnow lake - Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
Crow Land camping spot on side of a Small lake stock with lake trout.
Must have 4x4 vehicle

ontario-wild.name: Shiner Lake - Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Shiner Lake is a Crown Land camping spot with multiple fire pits or sites available. Very easy access for any vehicle.

ontario-wild.name: K&P Trail - Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
There is a few places along this trail which goes from Kingston to Pembrook were you could set up for the night. It's recommended checking on the Crown Land website to be sure you're not set up on the privet land section that this trail crosses.  It's a very nice drive :)

Ontario Cround Land Map
http://www.gisapplication.lrc.gov.on.ca/CLUPA/Index.html?site=CLUPA&viewer=CLUPA&locale=en-US

K&P info
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%26P_Rail_Trail

ontario-wild.name: Timber Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Ther are 2 very nice Crown Land ( wild camping ) spots each with access to the lake. They are close to the road and easy access. There is another spot a few hundred meters east which is not as nice but has a boat launch.

ontario-wild.name: Greater Madawaska
ontario-wild.notes: This is a very cute discrete camp spot just off a gravel road trail. We have stopped twice at this campsite and have loved it every time :)

ontario-wild.name: Calabogie Power Line
ontario-wild.notes: This is a nice off-roading trail with a few challenges nice spots to stop for the night. 4x4 with a minimum of 10" clearance is recommended.

ontario-wild.name: Wabun Lake
ontario-wild.notes: There is a sign posted no camping right before you get to the boat launch. HOWEVER, there are several campsites on the road leading to the boat launch, before the no camping sign, and there aren't any other signs that I could see. A kind person gave us their campsite as they were leaving and said that he got fined for camping near the boat launch last year, but that you were fine so long as you didn't camp anywhere after the NO CAMPING sign.

ontario-wild.name: Griffith
ontario-wild.notes: This location has a few spots to set-up and has water access not too far away. This is a great cute option for a night or two.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: There are 2 very nice clearings, each with a nice fire pit on this trail. A great large isolated place to rest up. Don't go further than the one I have marked on the map the trail after that one gets tighter and unpassable by vehicle fast. Nice trails to take a hike nearby.

ontario-wild.name: K & P - Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes:
This is a small unofficial boat launch on the side of the K& P trail. It has a great view and place to park 2 to 3 vehicles. Its very exposed but if there is a nice sky worth stopping for a night. 

I personally would not stay longer than a kick overnight because it's not during the day there normally is a lot of action on that section of the rail and would not be quiet.

ontario-wild.name: Deer Lake Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes:
Great gravel parking lot with no amenities. 

Signs say no camping within 66ft of water and no camping (*not overnight parking)

Moose, frogs and mosquitoes!

Leave space for boat trailers to turn around!!!!

ontario-wild.name: Prince Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
A small place at the lake.
There are some houses around but we asked and the house just near the place is inhabited, the place is a public square and one of the neighbors told us that there was no problem staying here .
There are many mosquitoes and black flies but the sunset is worth it.
The water was not too cold in May to swim and it is even possible to fish.

Ok for little van, this is not a uge place

ontario-wild.name: La pointe
ontario-wild.notes: Petit spot de campement rustique sur les terre de la couronne

ontario-wild.name: 180 superior lake view
ontario-wild.notes: Garbages, no toilet and no water, but amazing 180 deg view on the superior lake. A little noisy on the day but quiet at night.

ontario-wild.name: Matheson
ontario-wild.notes:
Small lakeside boat launch with picnic area. No signs indicating that overnight camping is not allowed. Another camper in a tent was setup on the grass. Near the main road so a little noises but not bad. 


Please be respectful This site is a memorial to the hundreds of people who perished in The Great Fire of 1916

ontario-wild.name: Parc de la source
ontario-wild.notes:
Quiet place for one night
Not Many choice in this area

ontario-wild.name: Halte pont rouge
ontario-wild.notes: Picnic area where we slept one night. Quiet despite the road nearby. Beautiful view of the red wooden bridge

ontario-wild.name: Hammer Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Hammer Lake boat launch. Gravel parking lot near the highway. it's a little bit noisy, but on nice lake.

ontario-wild.name: Place on the water
ontario-wild.notes: Nice public beach. Trees, beatiful views.

ontario-wild.name: beach waves
ontario-wild.notes:
nice place to watch the waves very quiet you have to get out of the highway at the sunset shore sign.
---
belle endroit pour regarder les vagues très tranquille il faut sortir de lautoroute a la pancarte de sunset shore avec un original

ontario-wild.name: Roadside pull off
ontario-wild.notes: Large spot next to a not so busy road. Close to the old nipissing road, good spot for lunch or an overnight stop.

ontario-wild.name: crown land site
ontario-wild.notes: busy in fall during hunting  season.    boat launch up the road.  peterborough crown game  preserve  west side.   stay on crown land side.  back up spot down  the road before the dump on right.    black bears and  cougars are in the area

ontario-wild.name: Near Highway 17
ontario-wild.notes: A good place for one night , 100 km before Thunder Bay if you are going to East Canada. Near Highway 17 so a little noisy. No commodities. Free. Not plowed, very unlikely to access this place unless it is summer.

ontario-wild.name: Spanish wild beach
ontario-wild.notes: Serpent Rivery Territory, permission from tribal elders needed to stay here. Beach very hard to find and inaccessible, just for 4x4, the track is vegetated closed, but we do it with a Sprinter. Lonely, quiet, small, gravel and sand beach, water not very cold in the edge, the best of which we have known

ontario-wild.name: Metro grocery store
ontario-wild.notes: located between car dealership and residential area, slight inclination to the parking lot, a few light post on parking.

ontario-wild.name: Arena, sport center
ontario-wild.notes: parking lot across arena, slight a for to parking, adjacent to school yard and river.

ontario-wild.name: Lower Nishin Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Small parking lot on a boat ramp at the Lower Nishin Lake. Good to sleep for two campers Vans

ontario-wild.name: Louse Creek Air Stip (Abandoned)
ontario-wild.notes: Crown Land, massive area on abandoned airstrip. Road in is fine, last bit is a bit of a slope but okay for my Class B.  Go down the far end for more privacy.

ontario-wild.name: Dirt  Road
ontario-wild.notes:
Maintanance way to a mobile transmitter. Only to sleep. About 300m from the highway.

Wirtschaftsweg zu einem Mobilfunksender. Nur zum Übernachten. Ungefähr 300m vom Highway entfernt.

ontario-wild.name: Rawn Reservoir
ontario-wild.notes:
Spot for one camper. Maximum Sprinter size. With view of the lake.
On the lake turn right. On the left site is a boat ramp.  There is cell service

ontario-wild.name: Small space on the lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Small space on the lake. Narrow access. Maximum sprinter size. No boat launch. No sign No overnight. Place for one camper van Beautiful view of the George Lake. The spot is below the Highway, is not to seen. 

Kleiner Platz am See. Schmale Zufahrt. Maximal Sprinter Größe. Keine Boots Launch.  Kein Schild No Overnight. Platz für einen Camper. Schöne Sicht auf den See. Der Platz liegt unterhalb des Highway, ist nicht zu sehen.

ontario-wild.name: Montagne du diable
ontario-wild.notes: up we go..by 4x4 with our trailler. hard road really need 4x4 but what a view once your up... on the way theire is some place where you can stop and camp too.

ontario-wild.name: McNulty Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Great Off road camping spot for relaxing, swimming & Fishing. Once off the road it’s will only take you 20min to get to the lake. ( U most park on top of the hill, not a direct lake access, but very small walk )

Strongly recommend a 4x4. I did the trail with my stock Jeep JK with no problem you just need to go slow and pic your line properly. When I went all the obstacles were marked with Trail tape :)

ontario-wild.name: Outskirts of Longlake
ontario-wild.notes: A small turn off from the highway, mostly a rock cap with room to set up camp. Three trails seem to lead off into the bush from here, we weren’t bothered at all during our stay. Some noise from the highway, nothing exceptional, but a good spot to spend the night.

ontario-wild.name: Nogies Creek Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
Moderator Note: Users report this is Crown Land and camping is permitted if you are a Canadian Resident or have a Permit. 

Small gravel parking lot surrounded by trees on Crown Land next to a bridge over Nogies Creek. Room for any size vehicle. Tents could be done on the edges of the lot or a little into one of the trails. Northbound, the route is all paved except for the last ~3.2kms which are gravel. Quiet spot with very minimal passing traffic.

ontario-wild.name: Wheatley Harbour
ontario-wild.notes: A gravel parking lot at the end of the road that is directly beside the beach. The harbour is just across the inlet. There is a portapotty and a garbage can. The beach is nice and is popular with locals during the day. The lot is big enough for any size vehicle and there is some shade on one side.

ontario-wild.name: Pitopiko rest area
ontario-wild.notes: Clean Rest area near a small river close to the highway still good for one night stop.

ontario-wild.name: Arnott Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Effing beautiful, clear and refreshing lake in between lots of muddy, brown lakes.
Only two or three cars fit here. No noise at night.

ontario-wild.name: Halte Routière
ontario-wild.notes: rest area on route 117. washrooms, picnic tables, some covered. Two parking areas, with the furthest one having an area big enough for 3-4 rigs.

ontario-wild.name: Halte Routière 113 N
ontario-wild.notes: a picnic area/rest stop with dry toilet, boat ramp, picnic tables and room for 3-4 RVs .

ontario-wild.name: Forest Access Road
ontario-wild.notes: It’s far in the bush, some traffic in the fall due to the hunting season, but a nice little spot with a hand made fire pit.

ontario-wild.name: Tat River
ontario-wild.notes: Great place for an overnight stay. Access to the Tatachapica river. Some highway noise.  Quiet spots further down the logging road on the right at entrance

ontario-wild.name: Old log yard
ontario-wild.notes: Old. Log storage. Yard. Lots of room for any size rig. Perfect for an overnight stay and 2 mins from watershed restaurant. Good food, gas and bathrooms.

ontario-wild.name: Duke lake
ontario-wild.notes: Good road, about 5mins off Hwy. large site with lots of room for campers. Great site for overnight or a couple of nights. Right on the water. 10 mins from the watershed restaurant and esso gas station.

ontario-wild.name: Bear pond parking
ontario-wild.notes: This is a parking use for the 4wheeler during hunting season. easy to get in al 4 seasons.

ontario-wild.name: Boyne Valley Provincial Park Camping
ontario-wild.notes: Parking spot by the trails, no signs saying no overnight parking.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Marlene
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land campsite next to this lake. Fairly quiet but next to a dirt road. Tent camping possible as well as a small trailer.

ontario-wild.name: Petit lac cayamant
ontario-wild.notes: Tough to reach sandy spit with free camping on crown land.

ontario-wild.name: Old CP Track - Adelard
ontario-wild.notes: This trail leads you to an old CP track bed just off the road. Lots of room for any size vehicle. Due to loose graveal, I recommend a 4x4 vehicle

ontario-wild.name: Old Lumber - Adelar
ontario-wild.notes: This is a great place off the highway ( 7 to 10min of trail ) Lots of options once you arrive at the clearing. If you continue north once you arrive at the clearing you will arrive at the river. ( We recommend Small to Midsize vehicle with 4x4. The trail is very simple and stock friendly )

ontario-wild.name: Old CP Track - Head, Clara and Maria
ontario-wild.notes: Just off the highway, this trail is an old maintenance trail to the CP track. You cant drive on the track bed because they put cut outs but there is room to park. Has a view of the Ottawa river. Maybe noisy since you are close to the road.

ontario-wild.name: Off TransCanada Hwy
ontario-wild.notes: There are a couple of spots for tents all around. The gps coordinates lead to a big opening with 360^ view of the forest. We can hear the cars. ---  Il y a quelques spots le long du chemin pour tentes ou véhicule. Les coordonnées gps mènent à un plateau avec vue 360^ de la forêt! On entend un peu la route.

ontario-wild.name: Beside CP track.
ontario-wild.notes:
Large lot beside old CP track. Looks like local youth meets here too.

Near a gas station with restaurant and store, maybe toilets, didn't go there.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes:
look on satellite to have a better idea of how to get there
it look like a old road unused there's still pavement...  I think they use it to access the pipeline upper... 
there's a pond near
there's grass so probably ok for a tent
good stop for a night

ontario-wild.name: logging road with lake
ontario-wild.notes:
farther on the logging road on the middle of a bucherie..… there is place to park car or van or little RV or a tent or whatever you are traveling with!!! there is lake quite close with clear blue water and beaver... perfect for kayak and beaver tail degustation! wonderful place to admire the devastation of wood cutting!!! 

there's "thé du Labrador" to.... 

pass the sand pit... 
keep left at the fork...
continue for couple min...
there you are!!!
check satellite for more info

ontario-wild.name: Rongie Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Lake side of the highway. Part of original road. Level part has road noise, quieter behind the rock.  Trailers may need to back out. Beautiful view and lake access

ontario-wild.name: Rongie Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Even better site on old road to creek. Paved far enough traffic is quieter than water. Best swimming hole

ontario-wild.name: Sand Bay Rd
ontario-wild.notes:
Up behind day use there is a sand pit and roundabout for big size rigs. Separate from no overnight area. 
Big rig ok in the gravel parking.

ontario-wild.name: gravel pit
ontario-wild.notes: a place for 4-5 véhicules, off route 117, next to bike path. No services, but good to crash.

ontario-wild.name: Dog Lake
ontario-wild.notes: A free site on public land on the beach at Dog Lake. Much nicer than the Silver Falls campground located nearby and it is free instead of $31.50CDN. May be soft sand. We backed in off the road with our large truck camper on a 4x4 dually. Water is clear and clean.  Good beach for swimming. Some cottages nearby and are used to having people camp here. A nice breeze today so no bugs. We needed to use our cell phone booster to get cell service.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Dumont
ontario-wild.notes:
Back country camping overlooking the lake. Possible to drive on the lake. Lots of spots. Beware sometimes the locals will use this spot to party. 

Don't trust your GPS I got lost in the bunch with my truck

ontario-wild.name: Parking and Trail to Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Safe and quiet parking, day and night, on this small parking lot. At the left of the parking, there is a little trail going down for 2 minutes to the parking lot below, then 5 minutes walk to the Falls.

ontario-wild.name: Carden Alvar Provincial Park
ontario-wild.notes: Parking lot at the beginning of a trail with WC. Some mosquitoes. Humid in June. Very poor cell service. Open sky for starlink

ontario-wild.name: White Duck lake
ontario-wild.notes: A little spot for van or little camper close to boat landing near the lake. Good for one night to break a long day driving. Pit toilet old. Don’t park in the middle of the way! There is plenty of wild camping spot along thé road 101.

ontario-wild.name: KP trail parking
ontario-wild.notes:
Gravel parking lot at the end of Dalton street.
We parc there for the KP Trail.
We bike the 8km to down town. 
Sleep here and leave in morning. 
Good for 1 night.

ontario-wild.name: Car park near Puzzle Lake Provincial Park
ontario-wild.notes: Flat gravel lot near Stone Mills township (Lennox & Addington county).  No signs prohibiting camping.  No lighting in lot.  Low traffic on adjacent road.  Tents could possibly be pitched but we were in a van so I am not 100% sure

ontario-wild.name: Large Field
ontario-wild.notes: Wild camping in large field. Area full on the weekend of the "Festival Western" the rest of the summer is free. Quiet place. OK for 1 night.

ontario-wild.name: hydro service trail
ontario-wild.notes: Hydro service trail, easy to hide the car. Suitable for tent.

ontario-wild.name: Rivière-des Outaouais
ontario-wild.notes:
Small, beautiful place close to an established campground. This place is very close to the river and sadly also very close to the road. 
Lot of fishermen use this place to launch their boat during the summer months.
There is one picnic table and no one is going to bother you if you spend the night there.
None or very poor cellular connection. Easy way in and out.

ontario-wild.name: Dozois Dam
ontario-wild.notes:
Not so quiet because of the road, but nice place to spend a night or two if you don’t want to camp a little farther north.
Great boat ramp just close by.
Beautiful lake in front and rivers on the two sides.
Great place to explore by boat or kayak.
Even good cell connection.

ontario-wild.name: Tower Rd. crown land
ontario-wild.notes:
This is a wild camp area with no amenities. Crown land camping on a hydro line access road. 

Tower road ends at the transfer station. Take the hydro access trail in. Good for 4wd rigs or ground tents, no RV or big rig access. Keep in mind that you are close to the transfer station. I have never had any issues with the wildlife there.

ontario-wild.name: Moon River
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land camp area. Wild camping with no amenities.  Good for an overnight stay if you're travelling. Just off of the highway. Some flat areas for ground tents, good for rig camping,  if you drive in a bit it is 4wd, if you park at the entrance of the trail it is for all size vehicles. A short trail hike to some great fishing. Some locals like to use this spot for a dump at the entrance, just a heads up. Been many times and never been bothered. Hunting season is active here.

ontario-wild.name: Riviere Louvicourt
ontario-wild.notes:
First road across the bridge.
There is room for a few campers.
There are no facilities but a picnic table is available.
Close to the main road but since it is a 50 km zone, there is little noise.
Good cellular phone coverage.

ontario-wild.name: Road 113
ontario-wild.notes: Spot just out of the road 113 for Chibougamau on the right side. At the beginning of a secondary road. Not easy to be out of the trafic in this area.

ontario-wild.name: Rivière Opinaca
ontario-wild.notes:
Located at KM 411 on James Bay Road
View of the river.
This is a place to sleep not a campsite.
There are picnic tables and some fire rings.
Room for about 10 campers.
No service.

ontario-wild.name: Louvicourt tower
ontario-wild.notes:
A lot of place for wild camping around here. Place for big rig and tent. 
Take the Telebec Louvicourt trail and drive 100m
Plusieurs place et petit chemin forestier pour camping sauvage.
Prendre le chemin Telebec Louvicourt et faire 100m

ontario-wild.name: Réservoir La Grande-1
ontario-wild.notes: Large boat ramp with easy access and beautiful view of the water.

ontario-wild.name: La Baie park
ontario-wild.notes: Small area to park. near the ottawa river. nice city view and you can meet some ducks. no bins, no toilets, no water. ok for bigs rigs. no "no camping" signs

ontario-wild.name: Chisasibi
ontario-wild.notes:
Hotel parking lot
 Recommended place for overnight parking by a local policeman.
Well lit and hydro is available on parking lights.

ontario-wild.name: Chippawa
ontario-wild.notes: Small area with grass and gravel. No "no overnight" sign. Close to the river. no shadow. it is close to the road but quiet. it is very close to the Chippawa boat ramp where you can not camp overnight. there is toilet over there. 200m walking.

ontario-wild.name: Trans Canada. North of Wawa
ontario-wild.notes:
We came in and stayed the evening with our 26 footer and there was enough room ( with a little bit of wiggle )
The water, as seen in the third photo, was right out our window through the trees.
The second picture is taken from the water....the boat launch and it shows our RV on the right with a small back-up entrance at the left and at the top is highway 17...not far away but very quiet due to all the trees.
A very private spot with room for one more camper a little smaller.
It was a VERY windy night but it was so well protected we felt almost nothing.

ontario-wild.name: the giant firepit
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice wild camp at the lake, not for big rigs. Huge Firepit, shady, nice view over the lake

Fyi, the name is overselling. There's just a regular size fire pit.

ontario-wild.name: Scenic wildcamping near a lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Small area with lake view on a gravel road. flat. place for one van or two if you are friends. right under electric cables. nice view and quiet. fire pit. no toilet
Horse fly seasons a little rough

ontario-wild.name: Lac Murray
ontario-wild.notes: Super beautiful camp spot. Only accessible from south.

ontario-wild.name: Near Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Unknown Lake next to HWY 599. Crown Land wild camp, next to lake, surrounded by large sand dune, fire pit.

ontario-wild.name: Mawley Campgrounds
ontario-wild.notes: Formerly municipally maintained camp ground. Now Crown Land. Camp site with fire pits, pit toilets. No other amenities.

ontario-wild.name: Olsen Drive rd
ontario-wild.notes:
Quiet place to stay overnight. 
Turn onto Olsen Drive Road. You will see a long flat building, there you turn right and follow the wide gravel track. On your left side you have a lot of space to park your car. 
For more privacy just follow the gravel curve (left) because there you are surrounded by plants and trees 
Solid ground with rocks, that’s why the place is not too comfortable for camping.

ontario-wild.name: Sherwood road
ontario-wild.notes: There is few small spots along the road to camp. There is a nice place a little bit farther than this coordonates. No "no overnight" signs. Gravel road. Just good for one night because is not so flat everywhere. Quiet road. No toilet. Locals are friendly and come to pick blueberries

ontario-wild.name: Hawk Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Big parking lot near the road, railway and quad trails. Some noise from the road but still acceptable.

ontario-wild.name: Parc de la Baie
ontario-wild.notes:
Large gravel parking lot behind Parc de la Baie. Across the street from a lovely bike and pedestrian path along the Ottawa river. 

Nice restaurants nearby. View of Ottawa.
---
Parking calme et tranquille pour la nuit. Restaurant sympa à côté. Très belle vue sur Ottawa. Marche piétonnier et quai tout près.

ontario-wild.name: Timmins Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: By the road before Timmins. Sandy ATV playground with space by a pond for camping with fire pit. road and railway noise but not in the night.

ontario-wild.name: Tiger Lily
ontario-wild.notes:
for us the best place in whole eastern Ontario. Small rigs and 4*4 only. for tents due to rocky surface difficult. entrance at 
 44.61016° N, 77.99906° W

ontario-wild.name: Chip & Chap hill
ontario-wild.notes: if you don't like all the boat launching action over the street, here you can have your solitude and peace. you still hear the road but much less than on the other side . a lot of chipmunks came to say hello.

ontario-wild.name: Burwash Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Great camping spots all around this area. No fixed spots, free wild camping. Will fit any size camper. Crown land so maximum of 21 days camping.

ontario-wild.name: Darling Long Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Access is along a maintained road but high clearance vehicle needed. Site is a bit rocky, but there are a few tent sites. Decent water for a swim.

ontario-wild.name: Hunter's Point (Private property)
ontario-wild.notes: At the point of the site.  This place is own by a very nice lady.  She was more than willing to let my family of 5 in 2 SUV to used her land and use the access to the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Medicine Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Medicine Lake is set back from route 17 behind George lake.  The access road to Medicine Lake is a 2 lane oiled and well traveled road easily traveled by a big rig.  Medicine lake access road 2 leads to a large solid  gravel area in which a big rig can turn around in. It has multiple fire rings and appears to be an area that locals use for fishing access and ATV play. There is evidence of camping, but no one was here when we arrived. There are many mosquitoes. We heard boats on the lake until sunset and there was light road noise from the highway. No signs about camping or anything else.

ontario-wild.name: boat launch @ Smooth Rock Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot by the River.  picturesque picnic table on the dock. Some trees for shelter, south side of highway. No signs forbidding overnight parking.

ontario-wild.name: halte rivière rupert
ontario-wild.notes: Large parking with table picnic and bathroom and garbage

ontario-wild.name: Gagnon Road Wild Camping
ontario-wild.notes: Nice quiet spot near the road. No water near but few trees around

ontario-wild.name: baie James
ontario-wild.notes: you have  2 spot with table picnic and garbage  and large parking too ...cell signal available

ontario-wild.name: beach public
ontario-wild.notes:
a lot of place to park for the night  and if you want you can go swim at the beach....To cool for me :) 
cell Phone service available

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land Game preserve
ontario-wild.notes: open camp site at the trail head of a level 3 trail?

ontario-wild.name: Pal Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Lots of options here in the forest roads around Atikokan. I chose this spot to be super out of the way (some areas are ATV or horse trails) and near a lake. Dirt road access, reasonable size dirt clearing for parking, reasonably flat. No amenities.

ontario-wild.name: Cataraqui Tailhead parking
ontario-wild.notes: Small parking lot for the Cataraqui trail. Suitable for up to 30 ft RV. No services but beautiful location in the country. Some traffic in the evening and morning but quiet at night.

ontario-wild.name: Roadsde pullout
ontario-wild.notes: Tried to find the lake site nearby but couldn't find the turnoff, instead camped here. Very quiet roadsde pullout although did hear maybe a few hunting gunshots in the early evening? Probably similar quality to "okay for sleep" further west on the road but I didn't check that one out.

ontario-wild.name: Burleigh Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Trent Severn Lock 28 parking lot. The day fee to park is $2. There is a small market restaurant and pub across the road.

ontario-wild.name: Communication Tower Access Road
ontario-wild.notes: Access road to reach a communication tower in the wooded area on the outskirt of the city. The road itself is not gated, only the tower is. At the beginning of the road there is a sign saying "Use at your own risk" with no other indications or restrictions. The road is accessible from Sandy Beach Rd and is made of well compacted gravel. It is about 300 meters long which is far enough from the main road to be dark (except for the red lights from the tower) and quiet.

ontario-wild.name: Wilson Lake Road
ontario-wild.notes: Large campsite right off the main dirt road. Close to highway. Full cell reception. Lots of room for tents or RVs/Trailers. Small boat launch and access to the lake. A few stone fire pits. Although high voltage powerlines are nearby, the nnEMF readings are reasonably low and significantly lower than most people's bedrooms. Maximum RF measured 7.40 microWatts/Sq Meter (using Safe and Sound Pro II Broadband RF Meter). Maximum AC Magnetic Frequency measured 16 nT. Maximum AC Electrical Frequency measured 2 V/m (using GIGAHERTZ SOLUTIONS ME3830B meter).

ontario-wild.name: Water Reservoir Access Road
ontario-wild.notes: Public access road that goes around the town's water reservoir. It is wooded on both sides so it's dark, being an untraveled access road there isn't any traffic, its far enough from the town and the highway to be quiet, and it is very wide so vehicles of all sizes can easily park here. Big rigs can pull in from one side and drive straight out the other.

ontario-wild.name: Camp Site
ontario-wild.notes: Ok spot.  Round spot on the side of the road but hidden by trees. Not very clean tho

ontario-wild.name: Trail Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: A huge parking lot for the close by Grey Country CP Rail Trail. Super quiet. We've slept there for one night. Nobody bothered us.

ontario-wild.name: Forest field
ontario-wild.notes: Place for one night, 200m-300m. from 17hw, nice for night, little noisy, but no signs no overnight camping.

ontario-wild.name: Maitland public beach
ontario-wild.notes: Free parking by the public beach. Very quite and nice place. There are houses around, so not making noise is a point to consider. We have had a wonderful night with the sound of the waves without a problem. (low season)

ontario-wild.name: parkslot view on fort wiliam reserve
ontario-wild.notes: Quiet parkslot at river with view on fort William reserve. Here is an pit stop, very clean rn.

ontario-wild.name: Logging Road
ontario-wild.notes: wild. not far from hwy28.  no facilities. quiet

ontario-wild.name: Wolf River Camp Area
ontario-wild.notes: An amazing area to overland with a fair amount of space with room for a nice campfire. Since it’s right by the river, it’s also an amazing place to fish too. The entrance is messy. if you have a very large over-landing vehicle I don’t think you’d be able to make it through the trees. If you can’t fit, I’d recommend parking at the entrance. The entrance is a bit hidden so the best way to enter is heading west and it is on the left just before the Wolf River Bridge. If you can visit this place you definitely should because it is probably the best place to camp for hundreds of kilometers.

ontario-wild.name: Island lake
ontario-wild.notes: Nice camp site by island lake close to hwy  with an outhouse close by more of a camp site for 4x4 trucks or suvs not rv friendly

ontario-wild.name: Jacks Lakes
ontario-wild.notes: it looks like a boat launch area, no visible sign of no parking or no camping.

ontario-wild.name: Small forest glade
ontario-wild.notes:
Small forest glade near gravel road. The place isn’t in the provincial park. Keep your eyes pealed we saw Wolfs at evening.
Hidden

ontario-wild.name: Government Dock /Chatham Kent
ontario-wild.notes: free boat dock, camping, fishing, locals fish river.  Along Thames River

ontario-wild.name: Hilltop with telecom equipment
ontario-wild.notes: Wild camp at the top of a hill with some small telecom towers and dishes nearby. Accessible with 2wd. People from the telecom company came to do some work in the morning and were friendly. Make sure to not block the road for their big trucks. Otherwise very quiet with minimal background noise from the highway and factories in town. Lots of wild berries when we were there.

ontario-wild.name: Near Ganawaska forest
ontario-wild.notes:
A nice little spot near the ganawaska forest. For  any access to forest you need a daypass. Nice offroad trails for hiking, Moto-Cross or ATV. 
Some ATVs in the morning.

ontario-wild.name: Cleave lake
ontario-wild.notes: Great site.  Lots of room for any size vehicle, probably accessible by RV but I will let someone else evaluate that.  Road to site is in excellent condition, some potholes and washboard but really excellent overall. Be bear aware.  Some other sites along the road to this one, but I found this to be the best one.

ontario-wild.name: Menet lake
ontario-wild.notes: Great site, lakeshore is approximately 30 feet from camp site.  Final approach requires decent clearance, I was fine in a stock xterra.  There is space to leave a car before the turn into the site, and then carry your tent/gear to the site, which is approximately 50 feet away.  I’ve tried to show the rocks and pull out space in the photos.  Lots of mosquitos.

ontario-wild.name: Public Parking
ontario-wild.notes: I spend a quiet night! Good, if your children like to play. Lots of traffic in and out. People doing burn outs with their vehicles and loud music. Didn’t feel safe.

ontario-wild.name: Outside Frontenac Park
ontario-wild.notes: Amazing parking spot, beautiful, and just across a little walking bridge from Frontenac Provincial Park. Tons of hiking trails, campsites can be booked online. Or you can just park here! There are pit toilets if you hike to the nearest campsite (although they belong to the campsites, so be polite!). The campsites are beautiful, overlooking the lake with tent pads and fire pits. Take all your garbage with you. The parking spot is outside the Park so it's not under their jurisdiction. It's surrounded by private land and cottages, so you're probably fine to stay as long as you like if you don't disturb anybody!

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Off Devil Lake Road, Crown Land that leads to Faye and Bruce Young's place (you'll see their name where you turn off the road). But they're just on the other side of the crown land. People use it in the winter for hunting. Not far from the side entrance to Frontenac Park. No amenities, just beauty and nice local folks.

ontario-wild.name: Grand-Calumet
ontario-wild.notes: By the river near the boat ramp.  Quiet spot.  Stayed overnight.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: This place is close to a lake where it is very calm in the morning. You can drive through a small entrance with a grassy path to the lake. We parked backwards so we woke up with a Lakeview! It is dark, you're hidden and it's quiet. Definitely a must! It is after the bridge, you see an 'old' gravel parking lot. People must use this to bring canoes in the water. There are some potholes, but we have low clearance and managed to drive around it.

ontario-wild.name: Ottawa River - Boat Launch - Acre Road
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice spot. 
Established boat launch. 
Some locals dropping by to fish and launch boats and canoes throughout the day but quiet at night. 
Cell service is spotty, had to walk a bit on the side of farmers field to the North, go out on the rock point or go back on Acre Road a half a kilometre.

ontario-wild.name: Bark Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Lots of sites along this lake, unfortunately most are taken by RVs that seem to stay there permanently.  Most likely area to find a site is right off the highway.  Beautiful aside from the annoyance of some of the best sites being held permanently.  Any car could reach these.

ontario-wild.name: Crown land free camp site
ontario-wild.notes:
Crown land free camp site in the woods, very quite and clean. Not too far from the road 101. Easy acces for big rig too. 
A lot of mosquitoes in June. No facilities and no phone coverage. 
Please take your rubbish home !

ontario-wild.name: Crown land free camp
ontario-wild.notes:
Beautiful place near the river, easy access and a lot of space for big rigs. The road isn’t too far but it’s really quite. There are some fire rounds but be sure there is no fire restriction. 
No phone signal (Roger). No facilities. Keep your rubbish with you please

ontario-wild.name: Old quarry
ontario-wild.notes: This is a pretty great location. We parked just off the road but you can drive down into the quarry where there are a vast number of places, and all pretty flat too. Bonus is that there is a bit of 4g signal on public Mobile. And the other bonus is that there aren't many bugs. Nice place!

ontario-wild.name: Parking area
ontario-wild.notes: A massive place for many band and tents on a large gravel parking area next to the highway and not far from Matagami town centre. There is w water point very close towards the centre. When we were there there was a temporary toilet and sink. The south days 48hrs parking. All good!

ontario-wild.name: Les Cenelles
ontario-wild.notes: Small opening in a small trail.  It's large enough for 2-3 SUV.  No cell service.  A fire ring already existed in that spot. The main access trail is part of a off-road spot. Can be busy during the day but very quiet at night.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Nearby camping was full, but this place was ok for a night. The road is very quiet after 11pm and the bugs were far less than other places too. Amazing sunset.

ontario-wild.name: Semi-working quarry with lots of space
ontario-wild.notes: We found this by accident, the quarry is still working but there is a large flat area that you can camp safely on, away from any machinery and very quiet. No noise from the road at all. Pretty good for a night.

ontario-wild.name: Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Stranger Lake - Construction currently, hard packed parking, boat launch below waterfall/ rapids, caught a few fish. Camped overnight

ontario-wild.name: Deception Bay, boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: Small turn around, locals come in to launch boats. Will stay the night, seems okay locals have said nobody will bother us. Close to hwy

ontario-wild.name: Lac Sauguay
ontario-wild.notes: Free established sites along the walking trail. One right at the parking lot, another that is in poor condition along the trail, and the furthest (this one) is worth the walk. Some traffic noise, tent platform, privy, picnic table, fire ring.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes:
Super quiet place. No traffic noise. Not nice but good for a one night stand. Few mosquitoes! 
High Grass. Not for big rigs.

ontario-wild.name: Gov’t Dock Beach Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Like 10 or more parking lots. The street to this place is a bit like a unpaved road, but it's worth it. You have like 150 metre beach and it's very quiet. Another car with a roof tent was also here at the same night.

ontario-wild.name: Aubrey Falls Provincial Park
ontario-wild.notes:
ADMIN NOTE: Entry seems to be at an established campsite (in the provincial park?) marked on the map. Please confirm status of this site.

Just off Hwy 129 and Peshu Lake rd. Water access and room for large RVs amonst local seasonals

ontario-wild.name: Off hwy 129 just north of Aubrey
ontario-wild.notes: A nice spot just off the hwy. there may be a few locals with seasonal campers. Just find a spot and put your feet in the water. No cell service without booster

ontario-wild.name: Cedar Lake - Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Short drive down from the highway on a gravel road. No signs saying no camping, nice view of the lake. Fish were jumping, some cottages nobody bothered us. Better suited to class B RV’s, short turn around area, overhead wires, not big rig friendly

ontario-wild.name: Perrault Falls - Rest Stop
ontario-wild.notes: Usual rest stop, no signs saying no camping, beside a lake. Spent the night with no problems, spoke MTO person in morning and there is no problem staying.

ontario-wild.name: Logging track
ontario-wild.notes: There is enough space for 1 or 2 small Vans or tents on this logging track. just at the junction with the main road. Very quiet. Decent 4g signal on PublicMobile.

ontario-wild.name: Old Highway
ontario-wild.notes: I think this is a part of the old highway, it is well out of sight of the main new highway and fairly quiet. Great for a night. There are toilets a short walk away at the rest area at Little Joe Lake

ontario-wild.name: Parc provincial Mashjimonje
ontario-wild.notes:
Site to access also the park's walking trails. We spent the night there without problems. No sign prohibiting spending the night there. Watch out for mosquitoes !!! You must have excellent mosquito nets or you will not be able to sleep


Site pour accéder aussi sentiers pédestres du parc. Nous y avons passé la nuit sans problèmes. Aucun signe interdisant d’y passer la nuit. Attention aux moustiques!!! Vous devez avoir d’excellents moustiquaires sinon vous ne pourrez dormir.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: beautiful spot to come with van or car or tent clear water good swimming fire pit green sand rock nice sunset has everything dream place to stay few days

ontario-wild.name: Lac metabeskega
ontario-wild.notes: Little place, very quiet, close to the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Beaucage
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice spot with picnic tables, garbage, toilets and a view on the lake.
A bit noisy because of the highway next to the spot !!

ontario-wild.name: Overnight parking
ontario-wild.notes: There is an overnight parking next to a dental office parking lot and there is also a carwash. We slept there with no problem and no police checks.  It is indicated overnight parking. the place is noisy until around 9:30 pm / 10 pm because there is traffic but night is very quiet until around 7:30 am.

ontario-wild.name: Sitches lake boat (canoe) launch
ontario-wild.notes:
Really nice spot just off the hwy on sitches lake. bugs weren't too bad.  The turn off is onto a tiny dirt road going down the bank of the hwy, steepish but probably fine for most vehicles.  

we camped in the "boat launch" and it was great, but just be mindful of anyone loading and unloading boats.  


Road noise, but minimal traffic.
2 bars of cell service

ontario-wild.name: Lookout Road
ontario-wild.notes: Pull off along side of the fire tower lookout road. This spot has no cell service but the tower parking lot about 1 km up to road has both strong cell and free wifi.

ontario-wild.name: Mcarthy Lake Rd turnoff
ontario-wild.notes: Large flat gravel areas just off the highway

ontario-wild.name: Just off Highway 108
ontario-wild.notes: Large gravel area just off the highway. Only minutes to TC17 or Elliot Lake.

ontario-wild.name: Crown's Territory Trail pit
ontario-wild.notes: Allowed to camp here by law. Follow the trail from the highway

ontario-wild.name: Skootamatta lake
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land camping. Easy pull on for any vehicle. Right on the lake. Not huge. But enough space for a couple of tents.

ontario-wild.name: Higway 17 close to Ignace
ontario-wild.notes: On the side of the highway. Lot of space, noisy but ok to spend one night without being disturbed

ontario-wild.name: Ausable River Cut Trailhead
ontario-wild.notes: Level parking lot on the side of highway 21. Pretty noisy even at night but really close to Pinery Provincial Park entrance (3mn). Lot of space and no "no overnight parking" signs. Located at the beginning of a little trail and 200m from a canoe launch into the river.

ontario-wild.name: Logging area
ontario-wild.notes: This is an area that has been logged some years ago, so it is fairly open. Easy access on gravel road. A few sites for small to medium size campers, not recommended for large rigs. Not great scenery but a quiet spot to spend the night. No Rogers cell service. Not many bugs. We camped about 1/2 km from highway.

ontario-wild.name: Vermilion Bay
ontario-wild.notes: Large spot close to the train. It seems to be a public place, no signs.

ontario-wild.name: Steephill Dam Road
ontario-wild.notes: Gravel parking lot at boat launch and dam. Nice view of lake. Locals going fishing at night so it can get dusty. Not many bugs when we were there. Ok for one night with any size rig. Rogers cell service low but ok.

ontario-wild.name: Obi’s Landing
ontario-wild.notes: Located on the Whitesand/Winston Road. Small parking area next to Lyne lake. Fairly flat and has a fire pit. Easy access to launch boat or canoe/kayak. Gravel road was very rough coming in, potholes and washboard. Rogers cell service about 2 bars.

ontario-wild.name: Greenstone Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Two spots near the entry off highway 11. First one near the highway but very quiet at night.  The main sounds are from the flowing river which can be loud, but beautiful.  Second spot a bit further up is at the edge of the lake and is equally beautiful.

ontario-wild.name: Papineu Creek
ontario-wild.notes: nothing special right by the road. small gravel area by the bridge over the papineu creek. can access creek.

ontario-wild.name: off highway by Whitefish falls
ontario-wild.notes: Pull off from the highway with no signs prohibiting parking or camping. No facilities or privacy but a nice view and a bit quieter than some other stops in the area. I think an RV would fit here but I'm not sure. Not ideal for a tent

ontario-wild.name: Lower Twin Lake
ontario-wild.notes: just a pull of by the road, which is a nice drive. lake access and fire pit. pretty loud during day because of the road.

ontario-wild.name: Pull out / lookout
ontario-wild.notes:
Just a small pull out on the side of the road. Pretty quiet at night but from 7am a lot of cars passing through. Nice view of the St. Lawrence river. Not the best spot but better than nothing.
I noticed also Rockport community centre 500m further with a big parking lot and no signs, if you want to give it a try.

ontario-wild.name: Marathon Road side rest
ontario-wild.notes: Small area but plenty of room for a couple of vehicles. No signs saying “no camping”, OPP and ByLaw enforcement have driven by but no stopping. Picnic table, no pit toilet. Some noise from the highway but gets quiet overnight. Close to gas station and convenience store.

ontario-wild.name: Round Lake Road
ontario-wild.notes: Lots of places to camp along this road. Nothing great but ok for a night.

ontario-wild.name: Pipe Lake
ontario-wild.notes: We camped beside the boat launch on the beach. There is also a campsite in the bush a short distance away. We enjoyed having the lake to ourselves for a few days. No cell service.

ontario-wild.name: Camp 314 Road
ontario-wild.notes: Just a small gravel road with a few places to park. Good for a night. No Rogers cell service. Some road noise but you could go further off the highway.

ontario-wild.name: Bala
ontario-wild.notes:
No "no overnight" parking signs, there's a public washroom just up the street open all night. Off the main road.
OPP came by at night to check on us - he said he was making sure we weren't "the kids that come here to drink". He even saw our empty beer from dinner and said nothing. Wished us a good stay. No worries at all, and OPP confirms there's no bylaw at night anyways.
Beautiful view to wake up to.

ontario-wild.name: Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land 21 day camping allowed, looks like fire pits and fishing

ontario-wild.name: Boat launch near river / Descente de bateau proche rivière
ontario-wild.notes:
Boat launch off highway in front of river.
Large flat parking with pit toilet.

Descente de bateau 
Terrain play avec une toilette

ontario-wild.name: Wawa Sandy Beach 2
ontario-wild.notes:
With the new' no overnighting' signs right at the main Sandy Beach parking lot, we found this roadside parking 100m away. You're parked by the road so you hear the occasional car in the evening but it's quiet at night. From here you see the lake and hear it too. You can back in with a large rig, just don't hog the whole carpark or they'll put 'no overnighting' signs here too. Use the main toilets. There's a path to the beach from here. We slept as good here as at the other spot before the signs went up.
No internet connection.

ontario-wild.name: south coleman lake
ontario-wild.notes:
nice spot need a small tent 
a place for one car on the gravel road.

ontario-wild.name: Painswick Park
ontario-wild.notes:
nice clean park with large open gravel parking lot on a quiet road with an adjacent busier road.  
park has tennis courts , large jungle gym , open fields. great place to stop with kids and animals. stayed the night in an RV with out any worries.

ontario-wild.name: Boat Launch Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Big boaters parking. can stay overnight. not very level and fairly populated area but the lake is nice.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land WeyerHauser rd
ontario-wild.notes:
Waterfront camp site with a fire ring. 

Track entrance is narrow but short and the sun sets over the lake. Aces.

ontario-wild.name: Narrows Lock Picnic Area
ontario-wild.notes: Nice quiet spot near the lock. Nice open grassy area with a couple of picnic tables, barbecue stands and fire pits.

ontario-wild.name: Concrete Flat in Sand Pit
ontario-wild.notes: level concrete flat for a van or two in something that looks like an ATV sand pit. very quiet and discrete. easy to reach.

ontario-wild.name: Chaîne des Lacs
ontario-wild.notes: Nice Camp spot near a boat ramp. Acces road is narrow and a little rough. No services at all, dry toilet near. Few picnics tables. Nice place to stay a day or 2.

ontario-wild.name: Sliver Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Very nice sand beach on Crown Land.  Room for several campers.  Access road is very rough, you need good ground clearance.

ontario-wild.name: Large space by lake / grand espace sur le lac
ontario-wild.notes:
Large area with boat launch near lake
Can hardly hear the traffic
Entrance is on the west side (south bound 117)
--
Grande place au bord d’un lac avec descente pour bateau
On entend presque pas la route
L’entrée est côté ouest de la 117 sud

ontario-wild.name: Malivoire abc
ontario-wild.notes: Conservation area. trails, quiet, has pit toilet. no 'no overnight' signs. good for a nights sleep

ontario-wild.name: Crab lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Right of the highway, garbage pail, short walk to lake (100 feet). Fire pit.

Their will be noise from the highway.

ontario-wild.name: Teapot lake roadside
ontario-wild.notes:
SEE PICTURE!
Enough space for maybe 2 cars or a van on a small patch right on the side of the road next to the lake. 6x6 flat area dug out for text on hill.
Very quiet spot with the occasional ATV passing by.
Boat ramp further south with more room.

ontario-wild.name: Boat launch au lac Blouin
ontario-wild.notes: Big parking lot next to boat launch, suburb of Val d’Or.

ontario-wild.name: Battery Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Recharge your good vibes at Battery Lake. Oh that sweet, sweet crown land. I came by bicycle, don't think you could drive. Worth pedalling all those gnarly hills for the sweet view, benches and fire pit. Pack out yer trash kids!

ontario-wild.name: La Halte du pont couvert
ontario-wild.notes: Official site for fishermen to leave their trailers while they go fishing on the river.

ontario-wild.name: Campbell’s Bay, Qc
ontario-wild.notes: Parking along à gravel Bike path (route verte), in front of a play park and splash pad. Picnic tables situated in the park. Access to the Ottawa river via the municipal dock right by the park. Small convenience store within walking distance and a microbrewery a short walk away for locally brewed beer and german inspired food. Quiet location with lots of great views

ontario-wild.name: riviere Whisky
ontario-wild.notes: Small place just before the bridge. At the edge of the water, sandy bottom. Fire pit on site. Adjacent trail, perfect for Ebike. Boat descent on the other side of the bridge, very busy. Near a dump site and water.

ontario-wild.name: Private Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: We found a driveway leading to an old fishing boat launch with a pull off tucked behind the trees, across the highway from the abandoned Gloria’s Motel. Beautiful lakeside spot on a lake called “Dunc Lake” with a miniature beach and fire pit. We arrived at 12am. Used some deadfall to have a quick fire and watch the stars, before sleeping in the van and heading out early in the morning.

ontario-wild.name: Path Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Very large parking lot beside lake. right off the road.

ontario-wild.name: English River
ontario-wild.notes: Access road to pipeline; big open area down a grassy road. Close enough to English River (3 min walk), you can see it from the best spot to park. There's a little fire pit, shade and a few trails nearby. Big rig friendly if you don't mind a few pinstripes on the way in. Full reception.

ontario-wild.name: Waverly Beach Park
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice little park. No mention of an overnight stay ban. Very nice little place. Accessible toilets. Perfect out of season.
---
Beau petit parc. Aucune mention d’interdiction de passer la nuit. Très belle petite place. Toilettes accessibles. Parfait hors saison.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Trails to crown land. On the way to another location down Troutspawn road (dirt road). this is the large area by the road right off the highway. no signs or anything. highway has some traffic.

ontario-wild.name: Lookout Heights Place
ontario-wild.notes: Lookout over lake and city with nice views. Large paved parking area, trash bins, park benches, surrounded with trees. Not so quiet place to overnight. Good cell coverage, Verizon.

ontario-wild.name: Off the Highway
ontario-wild.notes: Plenty of space to park off the Hwy less than one Kilometre. Communications type tower. Room to turn around and park. Full bars of cell service. Please respect this site is very clean, trash free and quiet.

ontario-wild.name: Abandoned motel
ontario-wild.notes: Not great but you can park behind this abandoned motel.

ontario-wild.name: Coldwater River
ontario-wild.notes:
Running late one evening we saw this from the highway and turned around to check it out.
Beside and looking under a bridge this is a very private Trout creek ( although called the Coldwater River)
Found on the Westbound land just before the River you can see in the pictures how close it is.
Below the level of the road it was very private and quiet with a view of the river from our window.
Beside is the Coastal hiking trail.
We saw 2 fishermen and no other campers.
Room for 3 van campers or 1 26 footer as we had.
Private and pretty and obviously a spot for the Trout fishermen.

ontario-wild.name: Grant Ferris Fishermans Park
ontario-wild.notes:
Large parking area with toilets and picinic/bbq space. Path for access to the river.

Grand stationnement avec toilettes air de Pik Nik et Bbq. sentier pour accès a la rivière.
Aucune indication et interdiction.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
Easy access and close to the main road.  Expect some road noise.

Pretty much this whole road is crown Land.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land Camping
ontario-wild.notes:
The coordinates will take you to the entrance.  

This is crown land, about 30 minutes from Resoule Provincial Park.

At the end of this"drive way" is the camp site. There isn't much of a turn around so if you have something bigger than a pickup truck, I suggest you just back in or find a different spot. 

There is only space for one rig, unless you are traveling with friends then you can park in tandem.

There is a bit of mud, I wouldn't suggest parking anything big here if it is wet.

If this spot is taken, try the next entrance which is just 10 seconds to the West. (I didn't investigate the other site but it looked similar on Google maps.)

ontario-wild.name: Forest Road
ontario-wild.notes:
It's a pullout on an old forest road.  There are probably better spots further in but didn't want to completely destroy my passion.

Only enough space for vehicles. No trailers, RVs, or giant vans as there is no easy turnaround.

ontario-wild.name: Wolfe Lake Road clearing
ontario-wild.notes: Simple but effective. Big wide open area on the side of a gravel road that appears to be just used by hunters and ATVs. Tons of space, mostly flat and very quiet. No facilities but modest Telus coverage. Works for us since the other options north of Sault Ste Marie were either right beside the highway and or closed.

ontario-wild.name: Long Lake Boat Launch - Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
MODERATOR NOTE: Please check local and country laws to confirm wild camping is allowed in this area. 

There wasn't too much Crown Land in this area but I found one parcel.  There is a sign that is labeled Rideau Valley conservation authority boat access area that makes it look like it's private land.
I have checked the Ontario Crown Land Atlas and this is labeled as general use Crown Land.
Nevertheless be careful when parking here. I parked at the very bottom and there's a spot between the trees, therefore I could not be seen from the road. I drive a full size pickup truck and it was tricky to get in there. The land is on a bit of a hill so I recommend four-wheel drive. I would stick to pickup trucks, smaller vans, and probably nothing bigger. I also recommend not blocking the boat launch as there may be fishermen in the mornings.

The spot would not be suitable for large RVs Class A nor Class C.

ontario-wild.name: Street parking
ontario-wild.notes: Nice quiet place on a street, not in front of any house, one side of the street is beside a wooden fence and behind there's a building with only a small window and the other side of the street there's a building with no window.

ontario-wild.name: Logging road
ontario-wild.notes:
Trans- Canada pipeline / logging road. close to road. road noise. lots of space. best if you have 4x4 and some clearance. 

nothing fancy but good for 1 night

ontario-wild.name: Michipicoten canoe route
ontario-wild.notes: Large turnaround by the river. Follow the narrow road off the turnaround thru to an opening further away from the hwy. Further down the narrow road (keep right) you'll see a large clearing with a fire pit, as well as access to a sandy beach area. Access on the narrow road would be risky for larger non 4x4 vehicles, but the main turnaround by the hwy is fine for a small trailer and any sort of car. 3G reception (no LTE with Rogers).

ontario-wild.name: Shabomeka Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land on a lake, near a trail that goes around the lake, with campsites along the route

ontario-wild.name: Lac Fiset
ontario-wild.notes: Can the Jeeps and others that are parking on the site..like near the campfire stop..site is rutted..ground is very soft, lets please keep it nice for all..best spot to park is on the road..that area just off the road leading to the site is a mess...and someone got stuck recently and left with huge ruts..good thing I have a spade..the site is nice, but hilly so very limited place to put tents.. 2-3 man tents only..road is not suitable for anything but a lifted 4x4..I have 9.3 inches of clearance and still hit twice..was going too fast..lots of noise from the ATV's there is a trail close by and they pass by the site as well frequently..

ontario-wild.name: Trail junction
ontario-wild.notes: Near main route.  There was 6-7 trucks passing that night.

ontario-wild.name: Beaver Dam
ontario-wild.notes: Small trail cut by a beaver dam.  Large enough for an SUV but fairly close of the route.  Very quiet in late fall.

ontario-wild.name: Skootamatta Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Little area off the road small parking by the lake. Access to water. Very quiet. Good for a night.

ontario-wild.name: Rivière Rouge
ontario-wild.notes: Cute place between a small gravel road and Rivière Rouge for 1 or 2 VR. Transcanadienne Highway is across the river, so we can hear traffic but it’s not really disturbing. Access to the river (fishing?) and a small fire place was already there. We stayed one night without any trouble, the gravel road is not busy at all.

ontario-wild.name: Little Fire Pit
ontario-wild.notes:
The "giant fire pit" was taken so I had to drive farther in.  I found a spot that is easily accessible, no 4wd needed.

There was already a fire pit here but looks like it hasn't been used in a while.

Unfortunately, there is no lake view.

It's open though, good if you have solar panels.

Site includes some used asphalt shingles and chain link fencing!

ontario-wild.name: By the Bridge
ontario-wild.notes:
Sweet spot that I found on Crown land.  It's pretty tight.  There isn't much room to manoeuvre either.  
I'd say trucks and smaller vans only.  There is no way that a trailer would fit, you'd be blocking the road.  Also, the spot isn't level.

You will be rewarded with a nice view of the lake.

Keep in mind, you are right by the trail so there is no privacy.

ontario-wild.name: Layby
ontario-wild.notes: We found this nice place, it's a pull off the main road, which is very very quiet. We stayed in Nov 2nd and there were only a handful of vehicles that passed us all night. There is no signal at all on any network. But very peaceful.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: I think this is the old highway into town which is now decommissioned. It was very quiet when we were there but there is a little bit of rubbish around. Ok for a night.

ontario-wild.name: Smiths Falls - Lower Reach Park
ontario-wild.notes: Big municipal park just south of downtown. Lots of space and a pond for reflections.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Nice crown land spot right on lake. Basically no traffic. Seems quiet. Lots of spots to set up camp. Road to get here is quite rough (I would recommend 4wd or 4×4) and entrance to this spot is tight. would not recommend bringing an RV.

ontario-wild.name: Riverside
ontario-wild.notes: Neat place, quiet, off road. Nice place to spend the night away from city.

ontario-wild.name: Brush Fun Park
ontario-wild.notes:
I'm not sure what this lot is used for, however, I am sure that it is Crown land.

There is plenty of brush clippings on the side, so maybe something to do with logging.

Also, this area is clear and a bit hilly, so it looks like ATVs have fun here.  

You could probably come here with a trailer. I think there would be sufficient turn around space.

There was a trail that leads in the direction of the lake, but I didn't want to scratch my paint too badly so I skipped it and parked on the hill.

We're two minutes drive from Lake St. Peter Provincial Park.

Also, bring your friends, there is plenty of parking here for several rigs.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Can fit three RV's, spotted on Google Earth.

ontario-wild.name: Pigeon River Conservation Area
ontario-wild.notes: Just before the entrance to the Pigeon River Conservation Area, is a small un-level shoulder that can fit 1 larger vehicle, or 2 small ones. Do not drive into the conservation area to sleep. Good spot for one night, as it is on a poorly maintained road that is not used very often. Speaking of which, Gray Rd itself is quite rough and bumpy, unless you have a jeep 4x4, DO NOT drive Gray rd coming off Hwy 35, there are parts that are completely washed away. Access Gray rd from Century Farm Rd by first taking Hwy 7A or Ballyduff Rd. For cars or small SUV's there are also a couple of tiny pullouts along Gray rd right next to the stream, but these spots are very small and right next to the road. Gray Rd is not well maintained in winter and may be hard to drive if snowy.

ontario-wild.name: Gray Rd. Shoulder
ontario-wild.notes: Gray Rd is a poorly maintained road that has a small shoulder area that could be used for a night, but not for a large RV. The spot is right next to a small bridge and Pigeon Creek. DO NOT take Gray rd off of Hwy 35, instead, access Gray rd off of Century Farm Road, unless you are feeling lucky and/or have a jeep 4x4. There are also a couple very tiny pullouts a hundred feet or so up Gray Rd, right next to the stream that can fit a car or small suv.

ontario-wild.name: Centre Lake Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes:
Great place to swim ,camp or fish. Great lake for canoeing to a campsite.
You may camp anywhere on the lake, providing you are within 150' of the shoreline. You should remove any trace of camping when you are done and insure that your campfire is 100% as there are root fires that can develop otherwise.

ontario-wild.name: Fairy Vista Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot at the start of Fairy Vista trail. You can park here and no issues at night for parking. No "No overnight parking" signs.  Nice spot to wake up to. Close to a water treatment plant, but you just hear vehicles driving on the roadway.

ontario-wild.name: By the lake
ontario-wild.notes: Nice quiet place by the lake. Pull in by the side of gravel road, walk about 30 metres to the lake and firepit. Enough room for a couple tents but uneven. Very quiet no traffic.

ontario-wild.name: Mont Chaudron
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking at the foot of Mont Chaudron, at the start of the path to go up there. little corner of paradise very very quiet, far from the road, to spend as much of the night as you want. The track to get there is dented but it goes smoothly with a normal car. Very good 4G connection. Take care of the place, take your waste, and give it lots of love! =)
--
Parking au pied du Mont Chaudron, au départ du sentier pour y monter. petite coin de paradis très très calme, loin de la route, pour passer autant de nuit que vous voulez. La piste pour y accéder est cabossée mais ça passe sans soucis avec une voiture normal. Très bonne connexion 4G. Prenez soin du lieu, emportez vos déchets, et donnez y plein d'amour ! =)

ontario-wild.name: Lac des Soeurs
ontario-wild.notes:
On the shores of Lac des Sœurs, a large car park that is very easy to access for all types of vehicles. Small beach for swimming, walking path in the forest. A few shaded areas for camping. Popular place, family but remains rather quiet. Sorry no photo, but ask google.
--
Au bord du lac des Sœurs, grand parking très facile d'accès pour tout type de véhicule. Petite plage pour baignade, chemin de promenade dans la forêt. Quelques coin ombragés pour camper. Endroit fréquenté, familial mais reste plutôt calme. Pas de photo désolé,.mais demande à Google.

ontario-wild.name: Lake loop
ontario-wild.notes:
MODERATOR NOTE: No vehicle access!

Very small waterfront clearing with two picnic tables and a fire pit. Accessible by mountain bike trails, by hiking or biking. No room for big tents 2-3 person tents max. I accessed by bike and camped with a hammock tent in October 2020. No cost for camping, 10$ per day to access VELO MSM trails, paid by honour system/donations.

ontario-wild.name: Pretty River Rd
ontario-wild.notes: This lot is maintained by a snowmobile club and is large enough for RVs. Very quiet but cell coverage isn't great. No fires permitted. Stayed two nights with no issues.

ontario-wild.name: Raw block
ontario-wild.notes: Tree planting block. 2k from  the road. nice round-about in middle of the block! The access however is pretty rough. recommend a 4x4.

ontario-wild.name: Serviss Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Several informal spaces on a gravel road along the lake shore. Ministry of Natural Resources signs at each end stating max 21-day stay. But when I visited in the first week of May, most of the spaces were occupied by "permanently-sited" trailers, without occupants.

ontario-wild.name: Stationnement Belvédère
ontario-wild.notes:
Rotary Tower Tourist Site, Large parking lot that can accommodate large RVs.
.....
Site touristique de la tour Rotary, Grand stationnement pouvant accueillir VR de grande taille.

ontario-wild.name: 4x4 secluded spot
ontario-wild.notes: drive up the dirt road with 4x4 to get to a sweet open area with a fire pit. for climbers check Dorion tower on mountain project, 20m tower 5.6 Trad and super close by

ontario-wild.name: Parking Area
ontario-wild.notes:
Large, unpaved parking area across from the former Aylmer Farmers’ Market. On the ridge north of the ball park overlooking Steen Park, with a scenic view of one of Aylmer’s two disc golf courses. 

Many amenities nearby. 

Narrow entry points to parking area may require wide turns to get a larger rig into the lot. 

No posted signs indicating no overnight parking. The Park itself is closed from midnight to 6:00 AM

ontario-wild.name: Jones road
ontario-wild.notes: Jones road climbing basecamp. sandy campground at the base of Jones road crag. next to a couple lakes, beautiful spot.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: side of lake, sandy beach, couple of fire pits

ontario-wild.name: Beach
ontario-wild.notes: This is another place by Lake Superior in the event that the official rest area or the other spot by Lake Superior has already been taken! it is a narrow road down. travelled in a class B campervan. a bit noisy from trucks. but beautiful view!

ontario-wild.name: Moss forest
ontario-wild.notes: a little bit of a drive up an old trail. 4wd or AWD recommended but not needed.

ontario-wild.name: St-Donat Wild Camp Spot
ontario-wild.notes: Campspot in the wood. The road to get here is made of rocks and sand. We came here with our Santa Fe (SUV). You dont need a 4x4 but I dont recommend to come here with a small car. 1 bar LTE only. Fits 2 SUV or pickup truck

ontario-wild.name: Off Hwy 522
ontario-wild.notes: Gorgeous private, off road small spot to pull over and park by quarry/make a fire. Stayed overnight. Off highway 522 just outside Grundy provincial park

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: By the lake next to the other spot. perfect. beautiful viewing . peaceful !!! keep it clean :) Be careful you don't get stuck in the sand and when going back up the hill to get back on the highway. take it really slow. No signal.

ontario-wild.name: Sand Pit
ontario-wild.notes: This is a nice large sandy camping area on Crownland. Far from this camping area but in the same sand pit is a spot for gun/archery shooting. Dead firewood around and I build camp fire area last year.  Accessible with regular car but I came with a Jeep.

ontario-wild.name: Open Area
ontario-wild.notes: Unfortunately somebody left an old BBQ here but other then that it's a nice open spot. In the middle of nowhere but very quiet and has a fire pit ring with dead wood around for fire.  Could be accessible with regular car probably but I would recommend 4x4.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: Awesome spot  on the lake but need good off road vehicle. Space for 2-3 trucks.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful but horrible night. Very nice spot. but I won't recommend !! A LOOOOOOOOOOT of moskitos !! Impossible to keep calm there. We left at 6 am after a crazy night.

ontario-wild.name: Road Side Bluff
ontario-wild.notes:
A spot just off the gravel road at the top of a rise. 
Suitable for larger units or maybe even two small ones. 
We are an F350 with a truck camper pulling a 16 foot trailer, and we fit. 

If you hike to the top of the rock bluff, there are excellent views of the sunset.

ontario-wild.name: Gas Line Side Road
ontario-wild.notes:
Small access area just off a gas line access road. We drove down the gravel road until it turned east and then backed onto the small siding area almost in the centre of the gas line clearing. 

The gravel side road is in good condition and there is room for one or two units here. There is also some room down the road a little further beside the trees of to the side of the road. 

The highway is quite a ways away and you can barely hear the traffic. We sat outside with our fire ring and enjoyed the sunset.  If you were tenting, there are many places to pitch in the grass. We are driving a truck and camper pulling a cargo trailer and had no issues with space. 

A local did stop in to let us know that they had seen bears in the area and to be bear-aware with our food and belongings.

Three bars of LTE cell service.

ontario-wild.name: Turkey Lake shore
ontario-wild.notes:
A great spot but popular with the locals. There are multiple sites here that are large enough to for pretty much everything, unless they are taken...  big rigs (class A) might have issues turning around if others are here.  We arrived on a Friday and there were two units already here, both 28-30ft RV trailers pulled by 4x4 pickups. We took a lakeside site with our truck and camper pulling a 20 ft trailer and there were two other sites about the same size.
