There are fire rings and a rocky beach at this location and one of the locals told me there is another area further down the road by the lake with a sandy beach that is usually used by “Jeeps”. 
We could have stayed here a few nights, or maybe even a week but we did not have time. 
NO highway noise at all, just the sound of waves against the shoreline and the loons on the lake. Spotty cell service with only one bar, but you had to be close to the lake to get it.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot by the lake. During the summer, gets busy but lots of other spots on the way to this one that are usually free.

ontario-wild.name: Rush Bay Rd
ontario-wild.notes:
Great spot for an overnight. 
Large wide open area that may have previously been a gravel/sand pit. There are a few places to park and also a decent road that leads into the bush a ways to a large grassy area, about another 100 meters away. 

The site is exposed to the small road but quite a ways from the Trans-Canada highway, so you can barely hear the large transport trucks. The side road heading from the highway is paved. The site we parked at was crushed gravel but there are other areas of sand and dirt. 

Three bars of LTE.

ontario-wild.name: Asphodel Library
ontario-wild.notes:
Moderator Note: Please check that parking is legal. Public libraries in Canada do not usually allow overnight parking. 

A few parking spaces next to the village library. Parking spaces (not pull thru) could likely accommodate up to 25 ft. Pull-thru spot on the other side of the road can accommodate up to 30 ft. Library normally closes at 7 pm and is closed all day Sunday. Has wifi and a small public park with playground, basketball court and picnic tables.

ontario-wild.name: Front Road Waterfront Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: Quiet place, the odd car drives by at night. There are not any “no overnight” parking signs.

ontario-wild.name: Beaver River Access
ontario-wild.notes: Lane way into a small turn parking lot. Mostly used for access to Beaver river. Small campfire spot. Right on the River. Crown Land

ontario-wild.name: Trailhead parking area for ATV/Snowmobiles
ontario-wild.notes: LOADS of space, enough for many Class A's, drive thru. There is a turn around at the mine up the 6 if you pass it. There is better access to the area from the north side which will enable a drive out south, or you will need to exit north to the mine to turn around if entering from the south as the north entrance is too sharp to exit and go south from. Quiet, despite large trucks passing by, sheltered from the road by the bank and trees, wetlands beside for beaver sightings. Be sure to park well off the drive area to allow those using the area to park trucks and trailers, and there is room for 3 abreast at its narrowest point.

ontario-wild.name: Research street
ontario-wild.notes: Industrial area. Quiet most nights. Not much parking enforcement. Close to stores and Home Depot.

ontario-wild.name: Notre-Dame dirt parking
ontario-wild.notes:
Pretty much the only place in town where you can legally park overnight, as the city bylaws explicitly say no street parking. Sign states “parking at own risk”, I’m guessing this is because of how soft the dirt becomes when it rains. I stayed 1 night and have a Honda CR-V and was fine.

There is an RV dump station about 50m down the road (well indicated with signs), a public bathroom at the dock (5 min walk) and 3 free wifi access points around town: the dock, the town rec center and the town gym (all within 1km of this spot and all seem to have a solid connection, no password required). I’m not sure if I should add these as amenities as they aren’t technically on-site, but if you’re reading this, you know they’re there 

There’s enough space for 5-6 regular-sized vans or 1-2 medium campers, but again, be careful not to sink in the dirt.

Please leave this spot cleaner than when you arrived!

ontario-wild.name: Otter Rapids
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot overlooking the Abitibi River, fire pit there, lots of room for just about anything you can tow. No signs saying anything about no camping.

ontario-wild.name: Island Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Great spot right on the base of island falls dam, good fishing a few fire pits around great view.

ontario-wild.name: Mazukama Falls Trailhead
ontario-wild.notes: Large dirt parking lot across from trailhead. Just a few hundred meters off the highway, parking lot alongside a dirt/logging road. No 'no overnight parking' signs, hard to believe anyone would bother you here

ontario-wild.name: Wawa Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Great little spot to the right of the boat launch when facing the water. There is a trail the locals use through the bushes so don't be surprised to see someone walking up. Tried fishing but no luck. Great little town with everything you need in walking distance.

ontario-wild.name: Logging road
ontario-wild.notes: The logging road to the west is way too rough for my loaded down touring bike and the canoe launch just to the east is not suitable for throwing down my tent, very boggy or too many rocks. I saw this road between those two sites. Much better road and several good level spots for my tent.  Pretty flowers too!

ontario-wild.name: Departure lake
ontario-wild.notes:
the entry to this spot involves a bit of a ditch, might not be suited for low vehicles. I barely made it with a Dodge van.

huge open space on the lake, a few firepits, no network (a bar here and there), very pretty spot.

the coordinates are of the spot itself, you would need to find the road entry (sorry I didn't add these coordinates)

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes:
Right in between the bridge and the craft shop exit the highway by the dirt road next to the big rocks. The road goes behind the rocks and leads (keep your left) to a viewpoint of the river passing under the bridge. 
There are traces of firepit there and a little of trash :( perfect for a stop. I cooked there and left at sundown before or the mosquitos. 
If you wanna drive to the end of the road, you need a small car. If not, it's a 3 minutes walk, just park behind the rocks.

ontario-wild.name: Cell Tower
ontario-wild.notes: Well protected campsite just east of cell towers and west of Hwy 651. No view or lake but a good spot for a night. Excellent cell service. Very little highway noise.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes: Nice campsite on a lake. Narrow road going in with some low branches but then it opens up to a nice large camping area. No cell service. Very remote.

ontario-wild.name: Wolf Lake Dam
ontario-wild.notes: Large area at the end of Wolf Lake. Some campers might be here for the season but there is still space available at the end of the road or by the Dam. Arrived on a Sunday and by night time we were the only ones here (locals mostly staying for the weekend only). Lake access.

ontario-wild.name: Gravel Pit Stop
ontario-wild.notes: It is a gravel pit. Very large and empty and on Crown land. It is a wide open space with gravel and there are no amenities but there is space to park any size of vehicle. It’s on the way into Killarney and it is pretty much somehwere to stop. If you drive to the back of the pit and park it is a good ways away from the road so quiet although the road is not very busy anyways. The area is pretty flat for sleeping. It does get very buggy at night.

ontario-wild.name: Madawaska River
ontario-wild.notes: Amazing spot on the Madawaska River, a little tricky to get in, high clearance and 4x4 are not a bad idea, the road to get there is extremely bumpy and there were some large puddles along the way. We made it in a 2wd Ford e250 without any issues.

ontario-wild.name: Lake Superior
ontario-wild.notes: A little turnoff of hwy 17 between  Schreiber and Thunder Bay. Safe spot to park your car and lot's of space to set up your tent along the sandy beach area. An RV or two can fit on the side of the road.

ontario-wild.name: P'tit Train du Nord
ontario-wild.notes: Nice place to stay at night. There is lots of space, tables and a toilet a few meters away when you cross the road. Can be a little noisy at night since it's just beside the highway but I had no problem sleeping.

ontario-wild.name: Parc des Stations Montcalm
ontario-wild.notes:
Spent one night here while biking the corridor aerobique. 
I had messaged the town and they said I could park overnight at the Parc des Stations.
I stayed one night in my RAM Promaster and had no problems. Nice and quiet. 
It will only fit a vehicle that can park in a regular spot, so no big rigs.  There are flush toilets at the rest stop not too far from here.

ontario-wild.name: Amherst
ontario-wild.notes: Spent one night here while biking the corridor aerobique. I had messaged the town previously and they said it is allowed to park at this spot overnight (278 McLaughlin). It was nice and quiet, no problems. At the rest stop down the road there are bathrooms with flush toilets and you can fill up your water as well.

ontario-wild.name: Hwy 113 Sandy Clearing
ontario-wild.notes:
Sandy clearing on E side of Hwy 113.  Lots of space, a few small trees and brush, sandy soil, little grass.  No signage of any kind.  Some highway noise, but not bad as road is not very busy.  Nice bird sounds, only a few bugs.
Edit / update:  Sandy soft ground could be a challenge here. Easy to sink into the sand and get stuck.  We failed at our first exit path but found another way, fortunately without getting stuck.  Beware!

ontario-wild.name: Wanapitei river bridge
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land camping just north of a bridge crossing the Wanapitei River.

ontario-wild.name: Sturgeon River
ontario-wild.notes: Old Gravel Pit just before the removed bridge that used to cross the Sturgeon River. Lots of room, short walk to rover for water or crossing to hike to Ishpatina Ridge.

ontario-wild.name: Lac des grèves
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful lake and a rustic camp, sable and possible go with RV.

ontario-wild.name: Abandoned Old Mine
ontario-wild.notes:
Abandoned mine with many areas to camp.
Easy access by sand road.

ontario-wild.name: Tiger Dunlop Road
ontario-wild.notes:
The Tiger Dunlop trail is a stunning trail and path way. Slept overnight. It was quiet and secluded off the road spot to rest camp and picnic. No portable toilet. But you can get privacy. 

Great tuck away off hwy 21 it’s called tiger Dunlop road no services but it’s a quite place to park overnight. Beautiful trail with access from here. No one bothered us overnight quite spot to picnic and sleep.

ontario-wild.name: Rock bay
ontario-wild.notes: Wild site for camping. 4x4 or moto required for access. Many sites at least 4 or 5. Many fire pits. Access to the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Rawn Reservoir Open Area
ontario-wild.notes:
The site marked 'Rawn Reservoir' is nice but small. This area is nearby doesn't have water view but is a much bigger, flat open area. Lots of room but it's a dirt track to reach here. No 4x4 required, it's an easy drive, OK for normal cars but might be a bit iffy for RVs with very low ground clearance. 
No facilities. Free.

ontario-wild.name: Wildcamp open area
ontario-wild.notes: Nothing special but a pleasant peaceful spot for a good night's sleep. A clearing in the trees at the side of the little-used trail. Flat area good for 2 or 3 vehicles if you are friends. Easy dirt track to get here, but there is a sign saying it's not maintained, so condition may deteriorate over time. No facilities. Free.

ontario-wild.name: Plage municipale du Lac Simon
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot to stay in the beach parking up the hill, little bit noisy during the evening but calm starting from 8pm, nobody around !

ontario-wild.name: Rabbit lake
ontario-wild.notes: Great secluded parking lot in front of a trail head and behind a rowing club and tennis court

ontario-wild.name: Passerelle Ulrick-Cherubin
ontario-wild.notes:
Very large parking lot near the « passerelle » crossing the Harricanna rive.  Nice view on the rapids and 2 minutes from down town.  Very quiet and nice view.  
----
Très grand stationnement près de la passerelle et piste cyclable qui traverse la rivière Harricana.   Vue sur les rapides et à 2 minutes du centre-ville.  Très tranquille et superbe vue.

ontario-wild.name: Lac 4H
ontario-wild.notes:
small paking beside 4h lac.
pit toilet is discusting.
lac is good for swimming. 
acessible by car or small van, not for big rig.
known place by locals
was very quiet during our stay, but there is a big fire pit so expect some company.
to get to this place, I used Google map with satellite view to see the road.
.

ontario-wild.name: Silver Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Nice sand beach on Crown Land. Room for many campers. Entrance road is very rough, you need good ground clearance.

ontario-wild.name: Amable du Fond River. D&W stop.
ontario-wild.notes: Gravely/sandy look-out over Amable du Fond River. Right next to the road, leading to Kiosk Campground in Algonquin Provincial Park, but this spot is outside the park boundaries. Room enough for a few vans or a  large rig. Nice view of river, but no easy access to it, with about 30 feet down a steep slope. Only 1 sign present which says " D&W STOP. PLEASE KEEP CLEAN. THANK YOU"

ontario-wild.name: pedestrian trail parking
ontario-wild.notes: Very quiet place in the night, 6 or 7 place for small rv.  Near of bike trail and pedestrian trail.

ontario-wild.name: Cedar lakes
ontario-wild.notes:
Further up the logging road (carp road) is a nice little site on a lake! A bit of a swampy smell and not very level, but it's a really beautiful, private/isolated spot. Fire put established. Weak Roger's signal. The road in is very easy but the site isn't suitable for big rigs. A little bit steep heading into the site. 

I think there are plenty of other spots up ahead, and it's a great spit to explore considering how well the road is maintained.

ontario-wild.name: Halifax road logging area
ontario-wild.notes:
at the entrance of the road, you'll see a large handwritten sign pointed east that says Halifax Road. there are plenty of pull offs and side roads to explore. coordinates may not be exact as they were entered manually (cell coverage is very sporadic). several areas with established firepits are available. lots of small lakes are around, but we were unable to find a spot by one. some areas have really terrible bugs, and some have none at all. not terribly scenic but very green and very quiet. there was lots of garbage when we arrived. as this is crown land, there are no garbage bins. try and pack our some garbage you find left behind.

logging is still active in this area so use caution. the road is in fantastic shape and high clearance/4x4 is not required. not suitable for RVs as some turns are narrow and tight. regular campers will have no issue. tents and pets aren't suitable for this area since logging trucks are still active.

ontario-wild.name: Beach spot
ontario-wild.notes: Down the road from Havilland Beach. Large gravel lot for boat access into the lake, BUT through the trees there is a path just wide enough for van to back into….giving you access to your own private beach!

ontario-wild.name: Glade Across the Tracks
ontario-wild.notes:
Three or more spots here... I pinned the entry off of hwy 17.
On the west side before the rail crossing there are two good spots not far from the highway but not too noisy.
Across the tracks is a dead end public road next to a large pasture.  Lots of flat places to park on the side of the road opposite the pasture.
The rail crossing is unsignalled and crossing them is a bit bumpy...  I think a light vehicle or RV would have no problem... just go slow...
No signs or postings if any kind.
Rogers Cell Signal enough to post this description,

ontario-wild.name: Big Rock in Clearing
ontario-wild.notes:
Far enough off the highway that it's quiet...  Trail head is the first left on Tower road.  I pinned the GPS location sitting on the rock.  enough cell service to add this  location...
Light vehicles and vans can get here... small RV's can turn around...  SUV's can go further down the trail.
Check if there's a local fire ban before making a fire...
No signage of any kind...
Please don't make a mess...

ontario-wild.name: Gravel area
ontario-wild.notes:
There's a large gravel area here... big enough for the largest vehicles to move around...  kinda noisy next to the highway...
No signs of any kind... 
A couple of formal ATV/Snow mobile trails tie in here

ontario-wild.name: Halifax Road rocky pit
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot on a very well maintained, active logging road. Road is suitable for most campers, but not RVs. Tent camping and pets aren't suitable for this location due to active logging trucks. This spot is nicer than the pin ahead, but cell service is not available.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes:
Moderator Note: Please check signage. There are conflicting reports about whether or not camping is permitted.
.....
Nice camping spots. Allowed for less than 21 days in a row. Free and about 15-20 minutes drive from the main road. Big rigs won’t do it

ontario-wild.name: Flat Rock #22
ontario-wild.notes: Flat-rocky area off the 45. Obvious local activity but quiet when we were there - 2WD. Some noise coming off the road but dies down pretty quick. No signs that would indicate no camping. Few bugs but nothing crazy

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: By Pickering nuclear plant dead end road . Dead end by water along walking/bike water trail awesome trail lots along trail quiet at most part no signs to say no parking. parfait pour dormir beaucoup de va et viens mais la nuit tomber super tranquille !

ontario-wild.name: logging road
ontario-wild.notes: great spots on a river crown land a few campers already set up camp there so we continued on down to explore but looks like a great spot.

ontario-wild.name: Buckhorn, Ontario
ontario-wild.notes:
Sunset crescent on the bottom of the locks at the end of the road , 
small parking lot, some vehicles with empty boat trailers along the edge but we found a spot and it emptied in the evening 
Rest room up the hill at the controls of the locks hrs vary 
Along side of Hwy 36 
Restaurant up on other side of bridge / lock a walk but not bad 

Tent camping allowed if you want to pay for it through the boat lock system. They charge a minimum around 15$ and you get a code for the washrooms. (After hours seems like no one checks, just no washrooms)

ontario-wild.name: Nassau Mills Lock # 22
ontario-wild.notes:
Trenton waterway Nassau mills rd lock # 22 .
Coordinate are not as shown. not on Hwy 29 it’s on Nassau mills on the other side of water, between Peterborough university and Lakefield at lock # 22  not at all far from the university 
Large parking lot, lots of benches on the water, picnic tables, boats parked also for the night

ontario-wild.name: Colbourg  Ontario at the end of Durham rd
ontario-wild.notes:
Board walk along waters west side of Colbourg, 
next to back side of legion village ,  and beside the soccer field 
Colbourg ecology garden is at the end here too

ontario-wild.name: Little Savanne Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Off of HWY 17, there is a boat launch site. Full reception OK for big rigs. There is a another more private spot if you take the road to the left with a fire pit, it’s right next to the train, although I did not hear it. Full reception. No signs whatsoever.

ontario-wild.name: Beach
ontario-wild.notes: An easily accessible spot on the beach for smaller vehicles right off the highway. Not the most private spot since it can be seen by houses and the highway. Once you get off the highway onto Havilland Shores Road, there is a larger area of sand looking out to the beach where you can find a path. Once on the path, the entrance to the spot will be on your right. Don’t go too far because there is a private property. Please remember to clean up after yourself to keep this spot beautiful. Happy camping!

ontario-wild.name: Hydro camp
ontario-wild.notes: Nice established place in hydro easement. Room for two campers. Talked to a gentlemen that has been there several days. Close access to water. Just south of Alexander Dam

ontario-wild.name: Forest Service Road
ontario-wild.notes: Just a small clearing off the side of an FSR. Road in is smooth gravel, the only part my low-clearance 2WD car struggled with was getting up over the berm on the side. Take it slow and at an angle and you’ll have no problem. Nice views of the river and sounds of trees rustling.

ontario-wild.name: Open meadow
ontario-wild.notes: Close to the road. Log trail . Middle of nowhere

ontario-wild.name: Gare Labelle
ontario-wild.notes: Free parking close to hiking trails. Next to "le train du nord" trails. Bathroom and restaurant close by.

ontario-wild.name: Outside Vermillion Bay
ontario-wild.notes: Up a dirt road 3 km. 2 wheel drive and low clearance ok. Camped at a T junction big enough to turn around a truck and trailer. No other traffic while we were there. Flat. Could also camp at pipeline right of way ~1.5 km from highway. Quiet and surrounded by forest.

ontario-wild.name: White Lake Boat Launch and Lot
ontario-wild.notes:
Large parking lot and boat launch for White Lake. Gravel lot with some grassy area. ATV and Dirt bike trails all around. Lots of space to park anything. We stayed here a few times and always lots of space.

 Free firewood down the road where power company cleared trees and left lots on the ground.

Free water and dump station at provincial park down the road.

ontario-wild.name: Boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: Excellent camp site on the water. Lots of parking for vans / RVs. Down and to the left gets you to a beautiful spot on the river.

ontario-wild.name: Vermillion River Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Free parking on the Vermillion River. Tons of space for a big rig. Light traffic in the mornings with boaters coming in, but mostly empty at night. Trash can available. Good for one night — better than a Canadian Tire in Sudbury.

ontario-wild.name: Clearing
ontario-wild.notes:
Large clearing big enough for lots of vehicles.  Accessible from the North East Corner of the rest stop.

Highway is far enough away so that it's not noisy

No amenities.  Bring what you need and remove what you bring.

ontario-wild.name: Off Main Road
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice spot just off the "main road"
Easy access with a regular 4-door car.
Black flies and dragon flies central. Watch for turtles all along this road.

ontario-wild.name: Forestry Clearing on Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes:
Wide open forestry clearing on a hill.  Forestry roads are a bit rough but brushed back wide.  Ground clearance helps but if you go slow a light vehicle or large RV can get here.

I tented here in September and could hear the highway a bit.  There were no bugs.

This is a big sky location.

The wood chips keep the mud and mess under control.

Nothing here... bring what you need and remove what you bring.

Allowable Crown Land Usage applies.  Forestry vehicles have right of way on the roads and stay clear of any forestry work going on.

ontario-wild.name: Trail head to clearing
ontario-wild.notes: 150m NNE of my geo pin down the quad trail, you will find a nice clearing for a tent site.

ontario-wild.name: Old Logging Trails - Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land.  Numerous suitable spots.  Small lakes accessible.  Cell signal spotty.  Busy during hunting season.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: There's a very short lane into the woods here. 20 meters in there's a spot to park a van, tent or small RV on the left.  The path curves right and continues only 20 meters further to a small lake.  Sorry, no pictures I, arrived in the dark and left in the dark.  I got into  Chapleau late and this was the best I could find after dark.  It worked in a pinch for a 6 hour snooze.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land Campsite - Florana Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
large campsite inside the Chapleau Wildlife reserve.  It's next to a lake and accessible by light vehicle (be ready for wash outs and go slow).  Allowable Crown land usages apply.

Wild camp... bring what you need and remove what you bring.

lots of critters around... large and small

No cell service

CBC on 89.9FM

ontario-wild.name: Ellie Beach
ontario-wild.notes:
Small sandy beach Crown Land lake side campsite.

Room for one vehicle or small/medium van camper.  There's an additional site to the east that is not on the beach as well.

Nice spot...

Allowable Crown land usage applies.  Bring what you need and remove what you bring.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes:
Couple of spots along a road parallel to the train track (and the highway). 

A bit noisy (close to highway) but good for the night. Preserved , the nature is beautiful,  lac on the other side of the train tracks (no direct path. kind of wild).

3.4 Mbits on fast.com

we had a 33ft RV.

ontario-wild.name: Watershed before Gogama, ON Large Clearing
ontario-wild.notes:
Large clearing away from the road a bit.  This area is brushed back generously and has lots of room for the largest of vehicles or camper trailers to turn around.

Good for a nights rest

Wild Camping - Bring what you and remove what you bring

lots of cell service

ontario-wild.name: Cockshutt Bridge River access
ontario-wild.notes: Large parking lot with river access to the grand river. Portable toilet and picnic tables available. No signs prohibiting parking overnight. A bit of noise from road traffic at night but otherwise quiet. Locals use this spot to launch canoes and kayaks and leave their cars in the lot. A pebble beach next to the river where you can swim or fish. You could probably pitch a tent on the gravel shore. Be respectful and leave space to not block the boat launch and you won’t have a problem staying here. Closed 01 December to 01 April.

ontario-wild.name: Clear Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Small spot near the junction of 144 and route 8

a bit close to the highways but there'a a fire pit and room enough for a van or small trailer.

Bring what you need and remove what you bring

CBC on 99.9fm

ontario-wild.name: Street Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Bayfield, Ontario, west end on Howard. Quiet neighbourhood, other roads around say no parking hours through the night, stairs lead down to beach people coming and going walking dogs down on beach, but at dark no traffic, not really busy area, road bikes to a park and marina

ontario-wild.name: Dead end road
ontario-wild.notes: Road ends at a small turnaround. I see big rigs parked there overnight all the time. Just don’t block the small construction entrance with the chain/lock across it. Limited turn around area so if you have a trailer you’d be better off backing in. Some walking trails into the field, no amenities but quiet. Construction site close by so maybe some early morning noise, there is washrooms on the construction site within walking distance

ontario-wild.name: Crown land
ontario-wild.notes: Great little spot. Can easily fit couple of vehicles . Right by the lake. Gravel road in good condition

ontario-wild.name: Wilson road
ontario-wild.notes:
Good for 1 RV. Truck turn around area far past the wilson cottages. Sufficient space for a full RV. Easy turn around, very level. Good for a quiet night.
We did not like the crowded site nearby so we drove on a bit and found this spot.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: amazing spot along troutspawn lake road. established firepit, a little tricky to get down the steep sandy and slightly uneven ramp but if you can, it's worth it! Large enough for several vehicles. not much cell coverage. if you can't make it in, there are two firepits established on the main road. the road is extremely easy to travel!

ontario-wild.name: Timber lake #2
ontario-wild.notes: specific location of 2nd site, details already provided in other post.

ontario-wild.name: Marmora Mine
ontario-wild.notes: Marmora Mine Lookout Parking. Gravel lot, also has ATV trails nearby. No washrooms, or any other facilities. LTE reception is good.

ontario-wild.name: Rest area
ontario-wild.notes: Rest area off Highway 11 N. Beside the rest area is a day use picnic area by the like - Klotz Lake

ontario-wild.name: The Quarry
ontario-wild.notes: Large abandon and flooded quarry. Not posted, locals camp for extended stays. Caution on the entrance. Lots of ruts.

ontario-wild.name: Rainy Lake Scenic Lookout
ontario-wild.notes: parking lot mostly used by photographs and for boat trailers parking

ontario-wild.name: Trewartha Creek, near Thunder Bay, ON
ontario-wild.notes: Found this flat place to sleep through online Backroad Mapbooks. It was dark when I arrived, and I wasn't sure how long the road is, so I only drove about 1 km down dirt road. Can hear traffic, but it's not so loud. Slept well.

ontario-wild.name: Parking lot outside of rouge beach park
ontario-wild.notes: Parking lot, no signage. By the go train so there’s some noise but not bad. Outside of the rouge park but close enough to walk to. Good for self contained overnight camping with lots of parking for small and large vehicle

ontario-wild.name: Quad trail
ontario-wild.notes: Quad trail off of highway 28 just past the bridge on the left hand side coming out of Bancroft. Made a little campsite about 400yards off of the highway. Made it in no problem with my Tacoma. Wouldn’t recommend anything bigger.

ontario-wild.name: Former Granite Blast Site
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful old granite quarry with flat ground. And cell service , two track remote road to get in but no need for 4wd. Big turn around space. Great spot for bouldering. Lots of shot gun shells, and active hunting.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Just a gravel lot next to the road, quite near the highway

ontario-wild.name: Close to Onaping river, North Ontario
ontario-wild.notes: Only for 4x4. good for one overnight stay. Close to hwy but nestled  in woods.

ontario-wild.name: Lac-Pythonga
ontario-wild.notes: Great little spot to stay by the lake. Also close to the highway, so may have some road noise. No amenities so please take your garbage with you.

ontario-wild.name: Silent Valley Side Loop Parking
ontario-wild.notes: This is a small parking area for a side loop of the Bruce Trail. It's at the end of a dead end street with very few houses or farms around. Space for about six or seven vehicles. No amenities, no "no parking" signs that I can see. Very quiet at night. Good Fido cell service.

ontario-wild.name: Log Chute Trailhead
ontario-wild.notes: This is a trailhead parking lot for the nearby log chute trail. It is just a gravel lot, no facilities, but is well off the main highway (35) and is quiet. There are picnic tables, garbage cans and an outhouse 200 m down the road at the log chute area. A sign in this lot says there's a 72 hour parking limit.

ontario-wild.name: Off Aylen Lake Road
ontario-wild.notes: If the access point just up the road is busy, this does in a pinch. Crown land just off the paved Aylen Lake Road, the approach to an old and unused logging road. You can still hear and see the road from here but it's fairly tucked away. Not very level or large so I would only bring one vehicle back here, no room to turn around.

ontario-wild.name: Glebe Park
ontario-wild.notes: A dirt parking lot for Glebe Park, the sculpture forest and the local museum. There are no "no parking" signs and it is very quiet back here, almost no traffic because the road dead ends at the park. There is an outhouse in the park as well.

ontario-wild.name: Crownland
ontario-wild.notes:
A wonderful crownland camp site near Bon Echo provincial park with lots of room for a couple tents. It has a little campfire area set up and a log seat, right on the edge of a lake. Also has a “take some leave some” pile of wood under a tarp, but make sure to try and leave some if you take!! 

How to find it: You’ll arrive at a dirt road with a sign that says “Skoot Damn” on it, and if you park up on the sides of that road to keep it clear, you’ll find the site by walking down the hill and turning right when you see a path in the forest.

ontario-wild.name: Lions Lookout
ontario-wild.notes: It seems you can park overnight ONLY from Saturday night to Sunday. Good for Cars and Campervans. Pet Friendly. Go all the way to the top. No signage at all about parking on the lookout.

ontario-wild.name: Churchill Park
ontario-wild.notes: Residential area, overnight street parking ticketing not enforced. Be respectful. Excellent proximity to Churchill Park (field for dog to run, seasonal public restrooms, splash pad, jungle gym & Royal Botanical Gardens hiking trails). Walking distance to shops, restaurants & groceries in Westdale Village. Walking distance to McMaster University.

ontario-wild.name: Fisherman's Parking
ontario-wild.notes: small parking area, dirt surface, room for a few dozen cars.. OK for mid sized rigs etc but longer vehicles may be unable to turn.. no facilities but there is a Tim's within walking distance.

ontario-wild.name: Lock 22 - Nassau Mills
ontario-wild.notes: Two large parking lots with benches overlooking water. No “no overnight' parking” signs. Stayed one night, traffic was not bothersome, quiet night. Beautiful area to catch the sunset and space for dog to run.

ontario-wild.name: Mallory onRoute
ontario-wild.notes: 24/7 onRoute. Bathrooms with outdoor pet station with potable water spout. WIFI, Tim Hortons, NY fries, A&W as well as Canadian Tire Gas. Brightly lit parking lot but plenty of space to stay the night.

ontario-wild.name: By the water Owen sound bay
ontario-wild.notes: Good for van or small RV. Room to turn around right at waters edge. We had no trouble in the fall.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land Campsite and Boat Launch on Opikinimika River
ontario-wild.notes: Multiple campsites on both sides of the highway. Some people camp here regularly in season and have kept the land clean.

ontario-wild.name: Crown Land Campsite and Boat Launch at Firth Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Primarily a boat launch to access the lake. Shouldn't be a problem to camp overnight. Not ideal for large rigs.

ontario-wild.name: Dead End Luskville Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Nice place for one night or two. Not a campground. But if you drive down to the dead end there is enough room for a campervan to park up for the night right next to the entrance to the trail to Luskville Falls. No amenities, bins or toilets so you need to be self contained. We had a 170 extended Sprinter, no space for big rigs though. No signs saying you cannot park there for the night. Quiet in the day and night. Not sure if its much busier in the Summer. Trail is a really nice hike!

ontario-wild.name: old Hwy 99 trail
ontario-wild.notes:
MODERATORS NOTICE:We could not confirm if overnight parking is allowed in this place.

Nice parking spot next to a biking trail. I think you can sleep in your vehicle if you had to.   Secluded spot.  Lcbo and variety store not far of a walk.  Lots of trails south east.  Steps from steel city but still small village feel.  
4G coverage

ontario-wild.name: First street
ontario-wild.notes: free parking from 1800-0900 Monday to Friday, and all day Sunday.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Blais
ontario-wild.notes:
Translation:Free camp with access to water. Can fish here. Descent for rowboat.Pets are allowed.

Accès à l'eau. Peux y pêcher. Descente pour chaloupe. 

Droit aux chiens.

ontario-wild.name: In the forest
ontario-wild.notes:
1/2 kilometre from the highway, nice spots for one night (maybe more
night) we don’t hear the sound of the highway.
No service.
Middle of the forest.
Better with a 4X4.

ontario-wild.name: Strathclair Dog Park
ontario-wild.notes: Two partly level parking lots by the dog park. Nobody bothered us. No amenities. Close to the road, but sheltered from the noise. It gets quite busy from the morning on with cars going to the dog park. Out of respect, I'd say that no more than two rigs/cars.

ontario-wild.name: Two Creeks Forest Conservation Area
ontario-wild.notes:
Conservation Area parking lot. 
South Nation Conservation

ontario-wild.name: End of the road
ontario-wild.notes: Cottage country end of the road turn around. Very quiet. There’s a dirt road that continues up and around into what appears to be a hydro cut. Would likely need a 4x4, I didn’t follow the dirt road. At this time a construction company is using part of this road end for vehicle storage and a dirt pile, but they’re not here after 4pm. There are no “no parking” signs.

ontario-wild.name: Concession 11
ontario-wild.notes: Dead end of a street ( actually, more an elbow at a bend in the road) near Grey County Rail Trail

ontario-wild.name: big dirt parking near beautiful lake view
ontario-wild.notes: Flat and dirt parking lot with couple of workers cabin around but further on the left you can find a nice quiet place near lake with fire pit.

ontario-wild.name: Quiet Sandy Beach
ontario-wild.notes: Quiet small sandy beach pull-off right off the road. Not much privacy and some road traffic but no "no overnight parking" signs and a nice view. Easy to access, maybe not for a class A motorhome but our Class C (ambulance conversion) had no trouble.

ontario-wild.name: Pier 4 Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: Parking lot next to small park with playground for kids. Just a short walk to the beautiful Bayview Park. Lots of picnic tables and you can charge your devices at the end of the pier (left side of the park at the "gazebo"). People start coming early in the morning and leave late, but overall very quiet and way nicer than the Bayview Park parking lot.

ontario-wild.name: Halte municipale
ontario-wild.notes: Perfect little spot for lunch and no signs forbidding over night stays, next to road though and noisy. Picnic tables and dry toilet

ontario-wild.name: Township Road 60
ontario-wild.notes:
Quiet spot right at an old bridge that has been closed for years. Used to be able to walk across now it’s all fenced off. Still a nice spot to park for one night or to hang out for the day. Lots of locals and fishermen frequent the area so be respectful. There is an unmarked trail to the side of the bridge but not sure if it’s private property or not. Limited turnaround room, vans and smaller rigs will be fine but I wouldn’t bring a trailer. Approx 2km of fairly decent gravel road to get here. I advise coming in from the East off of Katherine Street North - it is more level than the other side of the bridge. Remember bridge is closed so pick your approach! Couple small fire rings along the river. Keep it clean and respect the locals or it will get closed really quickly!
 There's a snowplow turn-around for bigger rigs. Blink and you'll miss it.

ontario-wild.name: Lions beaver lake park
ontario-wild.notes: Located at 5783 County Road 41, on the southwest corner of Beaver Lake in Erinsville.  Includes: waterfront parkland, swimming, picnic tables, picnic shelter, dock, playground equipment, toilets, boat launch and two parking spots.  Maintained by the Tamworth and Area Lions Club.

ontario-wild.name: nice secluded spot on the lake
ontario-wild.notes: accessible by short moderate difficulty 4x4 trail to spot on a lake

ontario-wild.name: Lac Simon
ontario-wild.notes:
Rest stop with picnic table on the road surrounding Lac Simon (sign reads "2000 LS). No "no overnight" signs. Room for 2 or 3 small RVs. Beautiful view from top of mountain. Very quiet.
--
Halte routière avec table à pique-nique sur le chemin longeant le Lac Simon (une pancarte indique 2000 LS). Aucune interdiction d'y passer la nuit. Assez grand pour 2 ou 3 petits VR. Très tranquille. Superbe vue au lever du haut de la montagne.

ontario-wild.name: Wilson's Flat Access Point #4
ontario-wild.notes: Gravel Parking at a hiking trail beginning in Grand River. Easy to drive on. No "no overnight" signs.

ontario-wild.name: River Road Pullouts
ontario-wild.notes:
Just North of all the tourist craziness is a short road to the right if you’re heading north called river road right by the power plant. There are 6 picnic tables and pull outs along with three trash cans. On the other side of the road from the picnic areas is PowerPlant Property wetlands that are fenced off. For around 4 hours deer, turkeys, 3 foxes and other cool wildlife came to the fence line to feed. So if you sit in the area quietly it’s like a nature show. 

No bathrooms
4 bars of lte
Quiet at night
There is no signage saying you can’t sleep here at night. The only signs here say not to go into the wetlands. I was here with two other Vans and had a very peaceful night.

ontario-wild.name: Nice Picnic area next to the road
ontario-wild.notes: Great, large picnic area next to the road so it is a bit loud, but great for an overnight stop. Beautiful lake with otters, and we had a visitor from a fox. No amenities

ontario-wild.name: Gouin Reservoir
ontario-wild.notes: Wilderness camping is permitted on any of the islands in this reservoir, there are plenty of beautiful sand beaches. I will point out a specific one I stayed at and had a great experience. Good walleye/pike fishing.

ontario-wild.name: Beach
ontario-wild.notes: Nobody else here, sunrise view, lot of space for campers or tents.

ontario-wild.name: boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: A launch I stopped at for the night to get some rest. park off to the side to allow use of the boat launch. Not a long term spot, but definitely a nice quiet one!

ontario-wild.name: Naiscoot river Boat launch area
ontario-wild.notes: As you cross  the bridge over the Naiscoot River on Hwy 69 South. A sharp right  turn, boat launch close to Hwy. We arrived in a long weekend and parked away from the launch area . We are Class B. 2 bars cell service.

ontario-wild.name: Shrubby Trail
ontario-wild.notes:
We found this spot when we were trying locate a nearby pin which ended up being inaccessible for a van our size. The main logging road is in great shape and is nice and wide. any sized vehicle can make it. there were several spots before and beyond this pin, but they appear to be rarely used (no established fire rings). plenty of wood to burn and small side roads to explore. 

we tried to see if we could reach the river but the trail got pretty soft so we turned around. 

where we stayed was about 25 minutes from the highway.

very quiet, some cell service. enough room for large vehicles or multiple vehicles. enjoy!

ontario-wild.name: fitzroy
ontario-wild.notes:
Translation: The park campsite was closed, we camped in the parking lot at the entrance.No camping prohibition sign.Another vehicle was present.

Le camping du parc été fermé, on a campé sur le parking à l'entrée.

Pas de panneau d'interdiction de camper.

Un autre véhicule était présent.

ontario-wild.name: by the rapids
ontario-wild.notes: if you don't mind the sound of the rapids a nice place for a night. non camping beach nearby with fire pits perfect for a picnic. more places further down but currently blocked by a tree.

ontario-wild.name: K&P hut
ontario-wild.notes: Little snowmobile hut with self made toilet in a pull off from the trail. right by the lake with access. neighbours on the other side of the lake and some ATV traffic.

ontario-wild.name: Belanger Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Very busy place during the weekend with locals fishing or swimming and teenagers camping and drinking. 
Beautiful spot during the weekday when it is quiet.
There is one easy spot for a camper van near the road and water, 
There are 2 more spots great for 4x4 overland rig near the pin (past a big mud hole ).

Keep it cleaner than when you arrived

ontario-wild.name: Nature et calme
ontario-wild.notes:
Free camping, fire pit, very clean and quiet.
We saw turtles and chipmuks.
---
Free camping, coin pour le feu, très propre et calme.
On a vu tortues et chipmuks.

ontario-wild.name: Teapot Lake Pull Through
ontario-wild.notes: Big spot that can fit large trailers. There are two fire pits, a big one and a small one. Right on the lake and there is also an outhouse. The site is a little muddy because people usually ride ATVs around here.

ontario-wild.name: Sanddam Road
ontario-wild.notes:
Crown land. Been here for 3 nights and no one’s bothered me. I’m close to the road that leads to the dump (it’s far enough away so you don’t smell it.). Weekdays you do hear the dump trucks going by but it’s quiet by about 4 pm. There are several spots to camp, some nicer then this but I get 1-2 bars of cell here and none further up the road. 
A few ATV trails lead off this area but it’s been quiet, just the occasional one.

ontario-wild.name: Spicy Water
ontario-wild.notes: camp site down a hill right on the water, fire pit and boom box. Not suitable for 2WD going down hill to site, but room to park at top, 50 meters away.

ontario-wild.name: pile of sticks
ontario-wild.notes: pull off that leads to a big pile of logs.

ontario-wild.name: Central and Eastern Timezone Park
ontario-wild.notes: Large overnight area, right off Highway17, brand new washrooms with plugs to recharge.

ontario-wild.name: Trent University rowing club
ontario-wild.notes:
Huge gravel lot with view of the Otonabee River by Trent University. 

Large enough for any size rig 

Lots of use by other groups/people. Not private. 

Would be good as a place to sleep overnight.  Good for canoe launch.  

No signage for any rules. 

Tent and camp fires would be risky, but possible.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes:
There's a patch of level ground right next to this small lake. You're only about 30m from the TC but traffic is pretty minimal at night.
The lake is shallow and warm, there's a bar or two of Telus coverage and, overall, it's quite peaceful.

ontario-wild.name: nogies canoe access point parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: large gravel parking lot off bass lake rd. no water, no toilet.

ontario-wild.name: No Exit Street /near Hwy 11
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot off the highway 11. It’s at the end of a no exit street. Entry point doable with a 4 x 4 or higher vehicle. No trailer. Open flat area with ample space. Perfect for one nighters during commute.

ontario-wild.name: grouse lake
ontario-wild.notes: beautiful high ground for 2 or 3 class b or smaller plus room for tents. we got our aluminum boat in by elbow grease but no problems for canoes or kayaks as there is a path/ramp. several great spots all along this road. road in is long 30-40 mins but not bad. no fish biting or jumping. atv's come through once in awhile

ontario-wild.name: sainte Agathe nord
ontario-wild.notes: on the Side of p'tit train du nord cycle path small beach ans small like on a private land not occupied ni mention of prohibited you have to go on left of the Fence. Bring bug repelent as close to water. fireplace in the Sand. good overnight place

ontario-wild.name: Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: Paved, shaded parking lot in front of the Frankford tourist park. Parking in front of municipal camping

ontario-wild.name: Riverside
ontario-wild.notes: 2 open sites next to each other.  Second site can be reached by an SUV through a really short but also tight trail.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Pomponne
ontario-wild.notes: Near a boat ramp.  Big flat area with some trees.  Very good place for a group.

ontario-wild.name: Boat ramp
ontario-wild.notes:
The boat ramp was closed at that time for the fisherman.  There's a 5 degree decline, so be prepared to level your vehicle.  It is also at 15 min from the road with a random passage of trucks.    After 2000 hrs, no one passes on the road.
You are 12 km from the village with gas.

ontario-wild.name: Pointe au bouleau
ontario-wild.notes: Excellent place to spend the night, for the more adventurous, you can go down just below with your camper to get closer to the water. there is no indication that camping is prohibited.

ontario-wild.name: York Street Parking Lots
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice parking to sleep with a great view on the ramsey lake.
No toilets/shower and no electricity.

ontario-wild.name: road side
ontario-wild.notes: road side. No sign saying it's forbidden, just below electric line, but very quiet few traffic during the day probably none during the night. haven't sleep here but could be a nice spot. could be avoided during melting snow season.

ontario-wild.name: Parc Carillon
ontario-wild.notes:
Beautiful place in a Canada's Park along the riverside. Pit toilet, water and tables are available. Super quiet place and really windy.

Très bel endroit le long de la rive. Toilettes, eau et tables disponibles sur place.  
Très tranquille et venteux.

ontario-wild.name: Hydro Line - Tree Cut
ontario-wild.notes: Cleared area around hydro lines, access via open trail East of where lines cross Hwy #118.  Had a pack (pair) of wolves pass my tent approx 9pm mid June 2022

ontario-wild.name: Abandoned logging Truck
ontario-wild.notes: The giant fire pit was taken and the other one was to close to the road so we came here. No one seems to be bothered by us. There’s bullet shells and old tires lying around, so not the most picturesque place and lots of mozzies, but very close to the park. There’s space for any type of vehicle here. No amenities.

ontario-wild.name: Old gravel road
ontario-wild.notes: offshoot gravel road running next to 637, mostly grown over but can be parked on for a night and out of sight of the main road. Okay for small campervans but probably not good for big rigs as no room to turn around a bay be a bit narrow. And would probably be too snowy in winter

ontario-wild.name: Chemin des Piles Dead end
ontario-wild.notes: Atv, Side by side or Enduro bike. Easy access. No road showed on Google but use Apple map and its there.

ontario-wild.name: Wilson pond
ontario-wild.notes:
We found that gem while looking for a wild spot for a night.
located near Wilson Lake by Wilson Rd.
Accessible with a vehicle that have a high clearance. Start of the trail is a bit abrupt for small vehicles but the rest is fine.

ontario-wild.name: trail access parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: Large lot for atv and snowmobiling parking

ontario-wild.name: Roots river
ontario-wild.notes: Little place  with the little river very calm

ontario-wild.name: Parking in front of pond
ontario-wild.notes: Gravel parking spot that fits a couple of RVs in front of a pond/lake. Parking area is not untouched but the lake is nice. Quiet place, rare noises from the road in front.

ontario-wild.name: Rte du Nord wild camp
ontario-wild.notes: Near km marker 329 is a road going to off to the south. It crosses under the electrical towers and curves behind some trees where you come to a couple of small parking spots. Small vehicles only, no fire pits or other facilities. Nice open and quiet spot.

ontario-wild.name: Bruce Mines Trailhead
ontario-wild.notes: In an area where rest stops seem to be lacking, this worked to pull in at night. Not going to be a long term camp area but if you need a nap in this part of the world this works! No facilities, and a very small gravel patch. If you stop at the picnic table sign (coming from Sault Ste Marie) you could use the toilet before getting here. I'm SO grateful I was able to nap here, very dark and very quiet. I have cell service.

ontario-wild.name: unnamed road
ontario-wild.notes: one of those it'll do for a night spots when you're desperate for sleep in an area that seems like there's no where to go to me. privacy from the highway but def hear it. pretty darn buggy too sigh. but ya..if you need sleep.. there's a pull off not far after you turn off the highway. I walked a little ways down the road, it's narrow and overgrown, didn't see anywhere else to park within a few hundred meters at least. probably could pitch your tent I bet. not suitable for rigs. happy sleeping

ontario-wild.name: Native reserve island
ontario-wild.notes: A small road circles the island.  We passed one night and had a very quiet night.  But alot of mosquitoes after sunset, so much we had to close the slide outs.  We own a 32ft.

ontario-wild.name: graphic lake wild camping
ontario-wild.notes: Just off from hwy 71 perfect right on the lake spot with a fire pit. The space could accommodate maximum 2 campervan. previous camper left some fire wood there.

ontario-wild.name: Point Edward
ontario-wild.notes: Great little spot to spend the night with a view of the sea.  Fishermen park here all night so you could be fishing.  Had a quiet night

ontario-wild.name: John E Pearce Provincial Park
ontario-wild.notes: Quiet spot to rest.  Some Trails to walk with info signs describing area.

ontario-wild.name: Dead end
ontario-wild.notes:
Dead end of a road. Large gravel u-Turn.
Seem calm but noïse from road.
At least its free 
LTE ara ok

ontario-wild.name: elliot falls boat launch and dam
ontario-wild.notes: boat launch, portapotty, no no camping signs no no overnight parking signs. small firepit. cottages right across river.

ontario-wild.name: big public parking
ontario-wild.notes: Open free public parking overnight is ok. The parking is next to a soccer field.

ontario-wild.name: Town park
ontario-wild.notes:
Little park in town,  i pass the night here, calm at night. I saw only 1 local passing. More sound in the morning because People go to work but still a good place to stay.  Table, garbage and grass.

Petit parc tranquille dans le village. Je n'ai vue qu'un résident passer par ici. Très tranquille durant la nuit, un peu plus de bruit le matin. Il y a du gazon des tables poubelles et des bancs

ontario-wild.name: Mountjoy Historical Conservation Park
ontario-wild.notes: Not quiet but safe place to park overnight. 2 parking lots, one off the highway, other on North side of park. Nice park to walk around and next to the river.

ontario-wild.name: Panorama Park
ontario-wild.notes: Very small park, with some picnic tables and 2 outhouses. A 'lookout point' over the town of Minden, but trees obscure the view. A short but quite steep and curvy road leads to the park, perhaps not suitable for large rig. A few flat spots for parking. PARK ONLY OPEN FROM MAY 15 - OCT 31. May be a hangout spot for local teens on the weekend.

ontario-wild.name: Sandy Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Quiet spot by the water. Evidence of parties, trash. But I lucked out, you might too.

ontario-wild.name: Gillies Lake parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: Not quiet, next to hwy 655 but no signs indicating you can’t park overnight. Lights in parking, felt safe. Great view and walk around the lake, 2.4 km. Another parking on South side of lake with washrooms and chip stand but way busier.

ontario-wild.name: Rest area?
ontario-wild.notes: 3 picnic tables, 2 trash cans, outhouse surrounded by trees next to the highway warning about the portapotty it is a literal breeding ground for mosquitoes! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED seems like a good place to crash car camping

ontario-wild.name: Fielding Park
ontario-wild.notes: This is a city green space. Easy to park overnight for any size RV. Beautiful gardens, kids play area, 9km hiking trail along the river. Wasn’t too noisy from the road traffic. We stayed one night no problem.

ontario-wild.name: Beach at Spurline Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Beach south of Hornepayne, large parking

ontario-wild.name: Braeside Beach
ontario-wild.notes: Fairly isolated, good for a smaller vehicle like a Westfalia, etc. Picnic table, portable washroom

ontario-wild.name: Centre communautaire
ontario-wild.notes:
24 hour parking behind the community center. Park in the paved part because the other gravel section is a paid parking lot for the boat descent with Public toilet near the boat descent. Waterfront, children's park and sunset
---
Stationnement 24 h derriere le centre communautaire. Stationner dans la partie asphaltée car l autre aection en gravier est un stationnement payant pour la descente de bateau avec Toilette publique pres de la descente de bateau .bord de l eau , parc pour enfants et coucher de soleil

ontario-wild.name: Sand pit near cedar lake boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: When taking the cedar lake boat launch road, head to the right and there is a sand pit. Fairly Quiet, it looks like people drive ATV’s in it but we didn’t see any.  You can hear the traffic on hwy 105 but there isn’t much. Recommend 4x4.

ontario-wild.name: Nipigon river bridge
ontario-wild.notes: Very nice spot. Sound of the river all night, a music ! Two bridges , on the road under the bridge, right on the shore of the river. Little gravel road.  : road and railway. No noise.

ontario-wild.name: Aire de repos 1000 islands parkway
ontario-wild.notes: Parking on the 1000 islands parkway with toilets. You can stay 120hours. No others signs. May be a bit noisy with the highway but good for 1 night

ontario-wild.name: Boat ramp
ontario-wild.notes: Small spot by the highway near boat launch

ontario-wild.name: Near lake
ontario-wild.notes: A few campsite near the lakes. A few sites not so good for parking but quite a few are, mostly occupied during the weekend with atver's, quite and most are clean with already established fire pits.

ontario-wild.name: Little spot in the middle of nowhere
ontario-wild.notes:
I found this spot by chance because the Little pit was occupied. no water but quiet. big enough for 1 small tent or a small or medium van. There is a flat space on the spot and a pit to make a fire. a lot of black flies but that's normal in the woods... Isn't that right? 
----
J'ai trouvé ce spot par hasard car the Little pit était occupé. pas d'eau mais tranquille. assez grand pour 1 petite tente ou un petit ou moyen van. Il y a un espace plat sur le spot et un pit pour faire un feu. beaucoup de mouches noires mais c'est normal dans le bois... N'est ce pas?

ontario-wild.name: Small gravel area
ontario-wild.notes: Few kms at the east of Wawa, Ontario. Just a spot for sleeping. Narrow, hidden, on a gravel path on your left when you go east on the 101 direction Chapleau. There is nothing there. Just a lucky place to sleep. One Rv maximum.

ontario-wild.name: Close to Culver Park
ontario-wild.notes:
Swastika, just west of Kirklandlake, Ontario. Close to Québec border. On Route 66. Culver park, west of the entrance of Kirkland Lake.

Very large spot. Close to the established Culver park Campground. Close to the baseball field. Large parking for RVs and large grass field for tents.

ontario-wild.name: Parking with a view
ontario-wild.notes:
Quiet parking lot with a nice view on the lake.
No "no overnight parking" sign and we spent a quiet night.
A very few cars in the evening and no one at night.

ontario-wild.name: Free rough camping
ontario-wild.notes: Has no service.  very private.  Somebody already has started building something. please leave better than found.  ATV and road trail runs through here

ontario-wild.name: Free wild camping fishing spot
ontario-wild.notes: Gravel prakimg. beatufull scenery.  river with dam. Can sleep in car. I've seen tents on the far grass too

ontario-wild.name: Parking at boat launch
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking at boat launch.
Busy at weekends.
Only for Cars or Vans.
Stayed here for one night.

ontario-wild.name: Whitla parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: I think part of the rowing naval club? Next to river.  Nice and private.  Maybe car sleeping?

ontario-wild.name: River bank
ontario-wild.notes:
Spot right on the river. Used during the day by the people living near here to swim. Lots of ATV during the day and very calm and quiet during the night. Spent a night here without problem. There is no bathroom or showers but the river makes up for it. There is a little gravel road to get there easily done with any car or van. 
Lot of mosquitos when night fell. 
LTE and 5G work well .

ontario-wild.name: SCH
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking $20 for 24 hours. 15 min walk from the CN tower. Quiet night for the location.
---
Parking 20 dollar pour 24 heures. 15 min à pieds de la tour CN. Nuit calme pour l'emplacement.

ontario-wild.name: Claireville South Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes:
Stayed here for one night. Some strange people in the evening and a little noise from the building next to the parking in the evening and morning. But all in all good place to stay. Saw one coyote.
No toilet, only parking

ontario-wild.name: Irish mountain scenic lookout
ontario-wild.notes: Parking lot without non autorized signs. Beautiful view. Toilets. Quiet.

ontario-wild.name: Wolfe Island Picnic Area
ontario-wild.notes:
A cute little Picnic Area with two benches at the water. 
I spend one very nice quiet night here. No signs which forbid overnight parking. No 4x4 needed.

ontario-wild.name: Green Lake Campsite
ontario-wild.notes: Crown land campsites on Green Lake not far from Griffith. Not the best ground for tents. Rough access to the water. Two stone fire pits.

ontario-wild.name: Spring Valley Park
ontario-wild.notes: Small parking next to a street. Relatively quiet at night. No facilities.

ontario-wild.name: Rest Area (quiet at night)
ontario-wild.notes:
Rest Area next to Highway, but not many cars passing. Very quiet at night. 
No „no camping sign“ 

Pit Toilets, Picknick Tables 
Gras, but no shade 

Good to stay a night - a lot of other spots here has „no camping“ signs.

ontario-wild.name: Boat launch & picnic area
ontario-wild.notes: Right off the highway but large parking, can accommodate any size. Boat launch and sheltered picnic table. No signs indicating we can’t stay overnight. Pit toilet.

ontario-wild.name: Pleasant Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
tent camping to rv under 30', good gravel getting in. Two sites about 200yards apart. 
phone Data is slow here with Bell

ontario-wild.name: Beachgrove
ontario-wild.notes:
good spot for an overnight rest but a little exposed for tent camping(doable though).
great walking trail 100y to the N and fishing from the bridge to the E. Great cel service.
Quite dirt rd day and night.

ontario-wild.name: Millers Creek Park parking lot
ontario-wild.notes:
Aspalt parking lot for the park. 
Stayed one night and had no issues. Tucked in behind a substation so its hidden from the highway. The road is busy but the noise isn't obtrusive. some spots are very sloping but not an issue for us. no prohibitive signs present for camping or overnight parking. please respect the area and be polite to locals to keep this area free for our use.

ontario-wild.name: Labelle
ontario-wild.notes: A flat, big space near the 117. City approved for 2 nights.

ontario-wild.name: After boat ramp
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking lot after boat ramp, along a small road (with little trafic by night). Beautiful view. 
No sign about parking.

ontario-wild.name: Trail head for chutes des denholm
ontario-wild.notes:
MODERATOR NOTE: Probably still usable as a Wild Camping site, but note that the trail to the falls is temporarily closed.

Parking for trail head to beautiful waterfalls. Big enough to turn around a camper with a medium sized trailer. Fire pit. No no camping signs. Quiet

ontario-wild.name: Logging dirt n gravel roads - don’t need 4x4.
ontario-wild.notes:
It’s high n dry. Good for star gazing. 

Active logging roads so be prepared to stop - but there’s a couple veins off the roads that lead to meadows. 

Decent Rogers 3G as I post this.

ontario-wild.name: Lower Owaissa Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Take Cemetery Road off Hwy 11, keep left to dirt road, leads to clearing beside small lake with firepit. Crown land confirmed.

ontario-wild.name: Paul J. English Park
ontario-wild.notes:
Big park with big parking area, no sign saying we not allowed to stay overnight, some young people meet there in the evening and a baseball game was played, no disruption at night, beautiful view of the sky, near the main road but not a lot of noise to be honest, stayed one night no problems

 Car shows on Monday nights during the summer. No problem staying overnight. Good cell service

ontario-wild.name: Finlayson
ontario-wild.notes: dead end rd for an overnight rest. walking trail at end of rd. good cel service

ontario-wild.name: Dead Horse Creek wild camping
ontario-wild.notes: Logging roads. Follow the road to the end -  lake - or look for a pull-in along the way. It’s high n dry - great for star gazing and meteor showers. Gravel road with some sharp corners so stay alert for trucks.

ontario-wild.name: Hill parking Kékéko
ontario-wild.notes: This is the parking lot of the Kekeko hikes. It is a gravel parking lot on the side of the road (10-15 minutes from downtown Rouyn-Noranda) that leads to many amazing hikes on the mountain. There are no "no overnight parking" signs and there is a chemical toilet in the summer time. The road is quiet at night. You just drive on the Témiscamingue Boulevard (leaving the town) and there will be a sign announcing Les Collines Kékeko

ontario-wild.name: Little Pic River
ontario-wild.notes:
So these coordinates are for the rest-stop / view parking of the bridge, the railroad tracks and then Lake Superior on the left. 

There are porta-potties and a great view! Also a picnic table. But you could park a truck or camper up here for the night no problem. 

I couldn’t stop today (because they’re painting the hwy), but on either side of the bridge’s EAST end, there are gravel tracks. Viewing from a height, I can see prime parking spots under the bridge along the river.

ontario-wild.name: Ferme Neuve
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice little spot with access to the lake. 
Close to the road but not busy and hidden
4x4 recommended to get out
Can accommodate 2 small rigs

ontario-wild.name: Cove side tree spot
ontario-wild.notes: Turn off Glengarry County Road 2 and down the track, you will cross the waterfront trail so look out for pedestrians, continue following the track which curves to the right, and the end of the cove there is a grassy clearing. space for 2 or 3 vans. 4x4 is required as its uneven and muddy. Trailers and RVs not recommended. there is a small firepit.

ontario-wild.name: Guindon Park East Enter
ontario-wild.notes:
The parking lot for hiking or biking in the park. No sign about forbidden overnight. Toilet are available. 
You can ear the sound of the road near, but not so much.
We don't sleep here, just stay for a hike.

ontario-wild.name: Babcock Mill Park Playground
ontario-wild.notes: Little natural playground with parking and pique nique tables. In a quiet street. Near a little River. space for 8 cars and for 1 or 2 big rigs.

ontario-wild.name: long mallory lake
ontario-wild.notes: crown land beach and camping. very busy however.

ontario-wild.name: Marineland Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Perfect spot for overnight parking if you have bikes, easy access to the Niagara trail , less than a half hour peddle. FREE.

ontario-wild.name: St Albert Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes:
Conservation area at end of road, quiet parking area, dock, boat launch.
Porta-potty.

ontario-wild.name: Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: Parking Lot with overnight parking available for payment. Stealth Camping here was okay for one night. Residential and commercial area with lots of restaurants in walking distance. Small rigs only.

ontario-wild.name: Parking along Moira riverside
ontario-wild.notes:
This place is posted twice, it’s the same as the informal campsite next to it on the iOverlander map.

Flat parking in urban area in park along the river

Walking trails and a garbage can are the only amenities. 

Locals fish here.

Not sure it’s made for big rigs. Bigger rigs should use the parking at the soccer field also posted in this app. Or Walmart.

ontario-wild.name: Maidens Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Small road along lake, also lane that leads out on peninsula. Fire pit and suitable for van or tenting. Crown land confirmed

ontario-wild.name: Quiet gravel roadside spot w/o trees on Lac de Mille access road
ontario-wild.notes:
About 650 m off Highway 17 there's this spot where the gravel road widens and you can easily park 2-3 cars on the side of the road without disturbing anyone. Trees are cut around here (grass area now), allowing to have long sun and to help the wind keeping away bugs. 
No one bothered us, only one car passed. Perfect for a night of rest. Road noise was minimal with the distance to the highway.
Good cell service. Road is the public access to a camp site / lodge further in. More potential spots closer to the highway, too, but not as nice.

ontario-wild.name: Quiet Dirt Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Just a little flat pullout big enough for a sprinter, accessible with 2wd. Nice and quiet, no bugs today. Road is a bit bumpy but not too bad. Good for a night.

ontario-wild.name: Iroquois Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Small gravel car park adjacent to a boat launch. Accessed directly off Carman Road, suitable for most vehicles. No facilities but can park right next to the water. We watched some ships use the lock which is a few mins walk to the east.

ontario-wild.name: Lamure Beach
ontario-wild.notes: In the parking area of Lamure Beach, you can stay for the night (this information came from a resident). the beach is beautiful, sundown marvelous and there's à little playground for the kids. washrooms were not clean, but there was current water and drinkable water on site.

ontario-wild.name: Rest area of ​​the Township of Lochaber Municipality
ontario-wild.notes: Simple roadside rest area. A bit near the road but close to a beautiful provincial park.

ontario-wild.name: Farm Point Chelsea
ontario-wild.notes: Large gravel parking area next to community centre and community multipurpose trail. Gatineau River on other side of road. Chemical toilet. No signs about parking so should be OK.

ontario-wild.name: montagne blanche trail head
ontario-wild.notes: big sand pit and gravel parking lot. trail head to montagne blanche hiking trail. no facilities but lots of room for any kind of rv.

ontario-wild.name: Perry's Creek Bridge
ontario-wild.notes: A dead end at the bottom of Ojibway Dr South. View of Burleigh Falls lock. Okay for quiet overnighting, but be respectful. This is part of First Nation's land. Walking access to facilities at Lock 28.

ontario-wild.name: Preissac
ontario-wild.notes: Best ever spot.  Next to a river with rapid water   A picnic table free   You can even fish. A kilometre from à gas station and grocery.

ontario-wild.name: Minden Curling Club
ontario-wild.notes: Large gravel parking lot.  Level.  Next to tennis courts, baseball diamond.  Very quiet.  Easy access for big rigs.  We stayed the night undisturbed.  Excellent cell phone service.

ontario-wild.name: Smooth Water Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: Boat launch into Lady Evelyn Smoothwater Provincial Park. There's a handful of crownland camping spots in the area that are big enough for larger RVs.

ontario-wild.name: Next to a Lake
ontario-wild.notes: perfect place to sleep. last 0.5 km is Sand. only for 4x4.

ontario-wild.name: Mont Tremblant
ontario-wild.notes: Nice place to sleep. On “Rue du Couvent”. I stayed here with my 21’ RV. I saw another bigger one on the same street. Garbage truck in the morning woke me up. In the old village. Perfect place to stay for free.

ontario-wild.name: Boundary Road
ontario-wild.notes: Country Lane turn-around. Great spot - quiet.  Good for a car, or truck, or 1 class B.  No tent option. Good cell service.  The road does continue, but that section is not maintained in the winter.

ontario-wild.name: Trail Head Dryden
ontario-wild.notes: Trail Head near Dryden, 4km out of the 17. 1.7 good gravel road. Large flat parking on gravel. Don’t go to the second parking, on l’y 2smalas parking for jeep. Many trails. Cell New-York 2 bars

ontario-wild.name: Gravel Turnout off HWY 41
ontario-wild.notes: Large gravel turnout at intersection of highways 41 and 30. Road noise from 80 km traffic but safe since the entrance is not accessible from the main highway. Mostly unlevel ground. Otherwise good for big rigs. One sign states that the area is monitored for illegal trash dumping. Should be good for a night’s rest.

ontario-wild.name: Lakeside
ontario-wild.notes:
Small place near a lake. Space for two vehicles. Protected from the wind.
...
petit spot près d'un lac, il y a la place pour 2 véhicules.
juste une table de camping en fac du lac, protégé du vent

ontario-wild.name: High Falls, Timmins
ontario-wild.notes: beautiful hike to falls. some deepish pot holes on the way in.

ontario-wild.name: Simple Lake
ontario-wild.notes: not much but gets you a place to sleep for the night. lake view and access.

ontario-wild.name: Mont-Tremblant Village Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes:
New parking lot in Mont-Tremblant Village. No signs stating 'No Overnight Parking'. We had a great experience, it is right next to the beach as well. Washrooms during the day. Wifi! We were able to cook right outside our vehicle and had no problems. Plenty of restaurants nearby. 
Only some noise of trucks passing but nothing too loud.

ontario-wild.name: Wawa street parking
ontario-wild.notes:
Read Wawa BY-LAW NO. 2513-11 (easy to find on google) first for clarity as there are rules, but there are places and seasons when street parking over night is permissible. 

This particular location was nice and flat, btwn 2 street lights, and with a school sports field on the right side so I could open the passenger side door to get the dogs out to potty relatively unseen. 

There were other vehicles parked on the road and a travel trailer as well, presumably the property owners or their guest as it wasn’t hitched to a vehicle.

ontario-wild.name: Raby lake
ontario-wild.notes: On the 559 road to Killbear. Just a picknick site with nothing but a picknicktable right on the site of a wonderfull lake with a very fine view. Direct besides the road but there are only a few cars coming by and it deels very quiet at night . There is room for a few camper vans of all sizes on the gravel parking or even a small tent on the grassy ends.

ontario-wild.name: Lilypad Lake Trails trailhead
ontario-wild.notes:
The town of Ignace maintains a small network of trails around Lilypad Lake.  The trailhead is a sand parking area with no "no camping" signs.  The somewhat soggy surface and the parking area size makes it unsuitable for anything other than cars and vans.  
Very quiet except for the sound of bugs.
Across the road is a public beach with picnic tables and porta-potties.  The beach parking is marked "no camping".  We parked at the beach, and ate dinner then moved to the trailhead after dark so locals would not notice.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: Relatively large clearing with ample places to park.  Suitable for any sized vehicle, and tents as well.  There is access to water on one end, and more trails.  Several fire pits already. People come to not only camp, but launch canoes, dirt bike, ATV, etc. The bugs weren't too bad on the September long weekend, but in the spring, they can be awful. The road was fairly good, however it can be full of potholes, and washboards in spots, depending on what the weather has been- but still manageable with a car and some patience. No service with Koodo.

ontario-wild.name: Alton Grange trail
ontario-wild.notes:
Unposted overnight stay right at the start of a side trail to the Alton Grange.
tucked in just off quite rd.

ontario-wild.name: Opeongo River Site II
ontario-wild.notes: Nice and quite place beside the gravel  road.Take the gravel road which is described at the  Opeongo River Site. When we arrived the best places at the beginning of the gravel road were occupied by fishermen. So we went about 500m far.

ontario-wild.name: Magpie Falls boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: Gravelled boatlaunch with no anti camping signs. Grassy areas around the edges and a dock with small sand beach spots. people seem to camp by the waterfall and the bus parking lot as well. hard to get tent pegs into the ground.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside
ontario-wild.notes: A level pull-out on Turtle River Road just north of US border in Ontario off Hwy 11.  No service of any kind. Just a level and secluded spot we found for the night. Near an excavation site that may have some activity part of the year. Quiet for now.

ontario-wild.name: Ivar Road
ontario-wild.notes: Dirt road with plenty of space. Nice turn around  not too far from the main road. Good for one night.

ontario-wild.name: No Name Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Great site on a lake with no name, beside Cedar Lake. Go down through Lower Madawaska Provincial Park, following Hyland Creek Road until it forks into Hyland Creek Road and Two Island Lake Road, staying left on Hyland Creek road you’ll come up on a dirt road on the right side. Follow it until the end and there’s a site on the left on Cedar Lake and one on the right on No Name Lake. 

Someone was on the Cedar Lake site but it looked massive (they had 3 trucks plus ATVs etc.) and that’s where the sunset pictured is. 
We stayed on the No Name Lake site and it was smaller and didn’t have the epic views but a great site none the less. All other Lake photos are no name lake- great for swimming and would be amazing if you had a canoe or kayak!

No established fire pit or thunder box, so bring a shovel and prepare to be extra fire safe! 

Great area for 4x4 driving around lots of dirt road, missing etc.

Defs need 4x4 to get here.

ontario-wild.name: Hydro tower
ontario-wild.notes: At end of loop off 400N, grass turn around under hydro tower

ontario-wild.name: Ivor Road
ontario-wild.notes: 17/Ivor Road.  Good spot North of Thunder Bay.  Large gravel area off roadway.  A little road noise and not very scenic, but good for the night.

ontario-wild.name: Former Pipestone Campground
ontario-wild.notes: Former campgrounds, now crown land.  Tight drive to the water, ok for small trailer.  4x4 a good idea.

ontario-wild.name: Former Menako Campground
ontario-wild.notes: Former campgrounds, now crown land.  Near lake.  Suitable for small trailer/camper

ontario-wild.name: Pipestone River
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot by the river.  Tight, no room to turn around.  Fire pit on site

ontario-wild.name: Manitou Road Hwy 502
ontario-wild.notes: Spot next to Hwy #502 but hidden behind trees on one side and a beautiful lake on the other side. Very calm, only a few cars passed. Gravel and good levelled. No service.

ontario-wild.name: Street parking near OPP
ontario-wild.notes: This is a street parking that does not have any signs posted near it. Fairly level but dirt road, although easily accessible for big rigs via the intersection both ends from here.

ontario-wild.name: Lake Superior, Ontario
ontario-wild.notes:
Shore of Lake Superior on west west of highway 17 just south of Agawa Rocks. Near the 1148km marker.
Camping is actually encouraged here with a sign indicating you must remove all your garbage and look after your own waste in a responsible manner. There are no facilities here at all.
There are several spots with direct access the the lake and the most amazing view!
Some road noise but should quiet down at night. 
Look for a gravel road leading off the highway and a white and green sign indicating it’s ok to camp here.

ontario-wild.name: Random space above the town beach
ontario-wild.notes: The site is a random green space just up the hill from the beach/ marina in the town of Manitowaning

ontario-wild.name: Port Elgin
ontario-wild.notes: Parking pull-out on a curve in the road at the north end of North Shore Park. This is not a formal site, but no signage prohibiting overnight parking.
