Right on the shore of Lake Huron with nice bathrooms and a splash park nearby. This site is also right beside a paved multi-use pathway that links Port Elgin to Southampton to the north. There is a fair amount of on-street parking in the town for overnighting. We stayed beside an elementary school located a couple of blocks south of Green St. There is free public wifi at the main beach parking lot, along with cold outdoor showers.

ontario-wild.name: Brampton 410/ Clark Boulevard
ontario-wild.notes: it is a carpool parking lot. It's pretty quiet at night. I'm on my second night here. Well-lit, store or mall across the road, gas station on the east side of the 410, some noise but to be expected. No issues staying here overnight.

ontario-wild.name: By the dam
ontario-wild.notes: Cute little spot by the water. Has a established fire pit. Just off the road. Good for a night

ontario-wild.name: Road side trail entrance
ontario-wild.notes: Rough, unmaintained trail entrance opening. It is not glamourous, and the road is quit close so a little noisy, but I managed to have a good, undisturbed night. You might be able to explore the trail further up with a potent 4x4. The spot itself is just a few dozen meters in from the road side.

ontario-wild.name: Roadside Pull-Off On River
ontario-wild.notes: Little gravel pull off, right on the river, space for maybe 2 vehicles. No ‘no camping’ signs, but there is a ‘No Fishing’ sign

ontario-wild.name: Bruce Trail Hiking lot
ontario-wild.notes: parking lot for hiking on bruce trail. quiet but not very level. nice hike in forest with small creeks.

ontario-wild.name: Lac La Paix
ontario-wild.notes:
Very nice place to camp for a weekend or a few days. Lots of spaces to isolate yourself if you want to be away.


Très bel endroit pour camper une fin de semaine ou quelques jours. Beaucoup d'espaces pour s'isoler si on désire être à l'écart.

ontario-wild.name: Bilberry drive
ontario-wild.notes: Street parking overnight, close to park. Only need to worry about winter storm parking bans. Right next to park. Walking trails along Ottawa river close by. I have also camped in that area in a tent but it is a very popular area.

ontario-wild.name: Island
ontario-wild.notes: Island only accessible by boat. Secluded. Camped at this location in tents and hammock tents. Fire pit, beach, the area is in Quebec but most people speak English. It is technically private land but who knows who owns it. I’ve never heard of them being there

ontario-wild.name: Lot off the road
ontario-wild.notes: I think they use this lot for boat trailers in the summer but I’m here in winter and it’s empty. Could car camp here for a night with no problem. No fire pit or anything it’s just a parking lot. No lights and doesn’t have good service. If you continue on Harrison trail you end up at crownland and can camp there also

ontario-wild.name: parking chinatown
ontario-wild.notes:
pay parking.
22' and under.
8$ per day, 4$ per night 
Very quiet. no problem
Kensington market very close with tons of great restaurant !

ontario-wild.name: Truck Inspection Station
ontario-wild.notes: There is usually 1 or 2 truck that stay here over night though out the week. There is the odd car parked over night. The Ministry of Transport rarely use this inspection site. If you're to stay here in a tent it will be a noisy night as it right next to hwy 6, although the hwy is pretty quiet at night.

ontario-wild.name: Large empty lot
ontario-wild.notes: Large empty lot, single dirt road access near Chippewa river bridge (small hump in road before entrance). Partial asphalt/gravel/grass. Lot is extremely flat and plenty of trees provide privacy from highway. No signs of recent campers and no “no camping” or “private property” signs. Big enough for multiple rigs. Lot is roughly 1.5 acres. No amenities.

ontario-wild.name: future inspection station
ontario-wild.notes: pull off for trucks. Porta potties, garbage. works for a late night nap.

ontario-wild.name: Chandos Lake Boat Launch
ontario-wild.notes: A small boat launch and car park off the main road. Very little snow here in winter so we were able to stop for the night. No signs prohibiting camping, parking or otherwise. Quiet road overnight. Would likely be too busy here in summer and interfere with local boaters

ontario-wild.name: Havilland kayak
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice place with a small sandy beach on Lac Superior. 
boat ramp and  enough space for big riggs

ontario-wild.name: Tukanee Lake view
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice place by the lake.
Gravel road or 1.5 km but accessible  to all kind of RV

ontario-wild.name: Pull off
ontario-wild.notes: No sings that state no overnight. Or no parking  just on the side of highway 20 smithville

ontario-wild.name: Grass Creek Park
ontario-wild.notes: This is a beautiful large area that is maintained by the city of Kingston. There is a museum and as you follow down the road the next spot is a parking lot for the boat launch with an outhouse. If you follow the dirt road to the end, past the large dog park on the left-hand side you will come to the large parking lot for the playground and beach area. There is a washroom building. We stayed overnight with no issues. Lots of people around in the morning for the boat launch & dog park. Beautiful spot on the water.

ontario-wild.name: Dawson Picnic Area
ontario-wild.notes: 8 picnic tables and places to tuck in and camp. Mature trees and lots of shade. Circular road so you can pull in and out without turning around. No signs present to say what is allowed. There are pit toilets and garbage. Park is 20 feet from highway and 20 feet from busy CN rail line, sandwiched between them.

ontario-wild.name: Oscar's Bay Beach
ontario-wild.notes: Small public beach and picnic area with pit toilets. The water is high so most of the beach is under water, but it means swimming is great. Lots of shade and grass. Two large picnic shelters. The beach side of the park is gated and says no camping. The parking lot outside the gate holds 30 vehicles. Plenty of room to turn around. There is no signage indicating overnight parking is not allowed. This is clearly where the locals go to swim. Watch the lakes for the American White Pelican which nests here.

ontario-wild.name: Morely Park
ontario-wild.notes: Small picnic area with picnic tables, benches and pit toilets. No potable water. it is public access to Rainy River. Lots of weeds at boat launch but a kayak could do it. Located at the end of a long road. Plenty of room to turn around. There are no signs with rules except those governing the boat launch. Very quiet and secluded right now ( Wednesday midday).  Peaceful camping unless you were worried about nobody being close. So nice to see some turtles.

ontario-wild.name: Collines Béarn
ontario-wild.notes:
Large parking lot of the footpath of the Benarn hills. 2 km from the 109 road. Several places available. Fire place, chemical toilet, small space bbq, picnic table. Accessible for caravan, motorized. Tent OK. No prohibitions to sleep at night.
.....
Grand stationnement du sentier pédestre des collines béarn. À 2 km de la route 109. Plusieurs places disponibles. Fire place, toilette chimique, petit espace bbq, table de picnik. Accessible pour roulottes, motorisés. Tente ok mais plus ou moins confortable vu la gravelle. Pas de contre-indication pour dormir la nuit.

ontario-wild.name: free parking overnight allowed
ontario-wild.notes: free parking area. free with lights in. looks safe nearby in the park are restrooms.

ontario-wild.name: Chalk River close to town
ontario-wild.notes: Good spot to camp out, a bit of traffic, but seems like everyone is cool. Easy access right off a used dirt road off of hwy 17 west, an RV fits here for sure with space to turn around. A couple of trucks drove by, and they didn't seem to care. People from town also camp out here.

ontario-wild.name: Whytok park
ontario-wild.notes:
This community area is not far off the highway and there are plenty of spots for parking… There are no no parking signs. We stayed here one night and had no issues. The next morning, the city workers came to empty the garbage bins and waved to us :)

Madoc is a wonderful town to visit

ontario-wild.name: Palangio Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot, less than a km off the highway on a small lake.  Good road, some spots under water in spring.  Free dry camping up to 21 days.  No water, toilets, garbage cans etc.

ontario-wild.name: Not Worth
ontario-wild.notes: If you take the long, winding back roads to get here, you will eventually come upon this Lake. It is a small lake surrounded by thick brush, you have to drive through many washed out roads and overgrown brush just to make it here and in the end the juice isn't worth the squeeze. However, if you're looking for absolute privacy this would be my pick

ontario-wild.name: Barrage merci baskatong
ontario-wild.notes:
Beautiful spots along the river 4x4 or suv recommended

Beau spots sur le bord de la rivière 4x4 ou suv recommandé

ontario-wild.name: Mont Rigaud - Sanctuaire Trail Head
ontario-wild.notes: Grassy/gravely parking area just below road up to the sanctuaire. No "no overnight parking" sign. Stayed here in a camper van. In cellphone range and close to the town of Rigaud (great town). Great place to stop if you want to rock climb or hike on Mount Rigaud.

ontario-wild.name: Woods in the city
ontario-wild.notes:
On the Algonquin road, there is a path at the end of the Remington road. It’s a long path, but there is an entry for a shorter path where you can park. Space for a car or two. For one night it’s pretty a good place because you are right in the city. 

We did sleep here for two nights, waiting to receive a part from the dealer. Pretty spot, we did a fire! 

No one bothered us, no lights, no facilities, but a lot of privacy here!

ontario-wild.name: Carrick Tract Trails
ontario-wild.notes: Trailhead parking lot. 1 bar Bell LTE. Could fit a big rig but not a lot of space. Quiet. Buggy. Good for a nights sleep. No “no overnight camping” signs.

ontario-wild.name: Fort Erie Border.
ontario-wild.notes: It’s on the Niagara Pkwy in Fort Erie. You can face the water (Lake Erie) and enjoy the lights and reflections off the lake at night. It’s quiet and peaceful with garbage containers available. No running water or electricity. It’s just a parking lot that fits a 36ft motorhome no prob. They have a few of these lots along the parkway. This site is my fav for boondocking.

ontario-wild.name: Pullout on a dirt road
ontario-wild.notes:
This is a pullout on the side of the dirt road that leads to the other iOverlander pin! I opted for this spot just because the island is actually a cemetery which spooked me haha

I have a small ford transit connect but this space could definitely fit a larger sprinter, camper or even tent! 

There were a few of cans littering the area but it was an easy cleanup :)

ontario-wild.name: Across from Palisades Hiking
ontario-wild.notes: Nice big area by the highway, access to lake and old railway

ontario-wild.name: Mill Road
ontario-wild.notes: Turnaround at end of road, field beside road

ontario-wild.name: Loophole in city parking rules
ontario-wild.notes: Paid parking all over the city but this small section of street has no signs, free parking 24/7. Parked here 2 nights. One other van. 4 bars 5G on Bell. Just off the main road, relatively quiet at night (normal city noises) but busy during the day.

ontario-wild.name: Guindon Park
ontario-wild.notes: Big daily park place with picnic table, garbages and toilets. Nice playground. No “no overnight” sign. Easy water acces

ontario-wild.name: Old Fort Erie Look Out
ontario-wild.notes: It’s a parking lot. Lots to do and see in the area.

ontario-wild.name: K&P Trail Parking Lot
ontario-wild.notes: Small gravel parking lot.  No facilities, but will do for one night.

ontario-wild.name: Wolf Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Reception is okay in a few spots. Used to be a really rough drive in but someone was nice enough to pour gravel the whole way in.  Can be quite busy in some sections but usually along the water you can squeeze in. Water is okay. Nothing super special but its local for us.

ontario-wild.name: Perfect spot at Medicine Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Spot nearby the lake, the last 50m a little bit downhill, but doable. The beach is sandy and flat, the water clear and calm. Fireplace and rustic toilet available. There is enough space for 2-3 RVs. Feels like paradise. Quite and away from the village, great for more than one night.

ontario-wild.name: holt Mine Complex spot on the lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Translation: beautiful site directly on a small lake with the sunset in the background. Near the 101

beau site directement sur un petit lac avec le coucher de soleil en arrière plan. Près  de la 101

ontario-wild.name: Riverside
ontario-wild.notes: Super nice place for small rig, on the river with fire pit..... keep it clean ! it was not.

ontario-wild.name: Road to Outer Harbour Marine - gravel side road
ontario-wild.notes: This is an informal parking area with no signs restricting parking. It is on Lake Ontario.

ontario-wild.name: Glasford Lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Spacious area with boat launch. Room for about 6-8 Campers or tent sites. Great fishing in the Glasford Lake system. 
May need four-wheel drive or pickup to get to the camp site. Main road is in great condition but beaver dams have it underwater on occasion.

ontario-wild.name: Rabbit Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Spacious area. Room for approx. 10 Campers or tent sites. Open area looks to be an old logging camp at one time.  Located right next to Rabbit Lake Road with easy access.  Small pond across the road for water use.  Short half a km ride or walk to Rabbit Lake and boat launch area.

ontario-wild.name: Island View
ontario-wild.notes: Enough room for one van and a tent.  Right off Hughes Landing Rd.  Almost no traffic on this weekday in June.  Very picturesque.

ontario-wild.name: Little river in the woods
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice spot near a small river/brook. Fire pit. Space for 2 to 3 small tents or 1 or 2 RVs. Parking space. Close to a road but not very busy.
---
Joli endroit près d'une petite rivière/ ruisseau. Pit à feu. Place pour 2 à 3 petites tentes ou 1 ou 2 VR. Place pour stationner. Près d'une route mais peu passante.

ontario-wild.name: Logging road outside Quetico
ontario-wild.notes: Pretty much the end of the road.  Relatively recently logged off so it's wide open.  Starlink works great.  No cell coverage at all.

ontario-wild.name: Tatachikapika River tributary
ontario-wild.notes: 2.5 km from Hwy 144 on a forest road. Road is relatively good. Site is right by an unnamed lake, built fire pit. Lots of moose tracks around

ontario-wild.name: Anteater Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Steep boat launch with a nice flat campsite right next to it.  Road in is fairly short but on the rough side.  No need for 4x4 but go slow and you'll be fine.  1-2 bars of Bell wireless.

ontario-wild.name: Roy G Hobbs Community Centre Park
ontario-wild.notes: A very small parking lot next to the Ottawa River Pathway and an off leash dog park. A quiet place with minimal traffic in the evening. I didn’t investigate the ports potty. No posted signs.

ontario-wild.name: Below a power line
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot under the power line. Just before the Pourvoirie.

ontario-wild.name: Arran lake
ontario-wild.notes: Picnic table spot with toilet and trash can. No sign prohibiting camping. Really quiet place for 1 night

ontario-wild.name: Hunting Camp
ontario-wild.notes:
The route to the cell towers was locked so I went down the gravel road opposite that road.
Going right takes you to a dead end or potentially good sprinter camping.
Go left takes you up a hill with a fire ring & an old outhouse that looks like its used for hunting. 
Great spot. 
Telus cell would not work here.

ontario-wild.name: The large spot
ontario-wild.notes: Found on Lac Vert. This island offers 3 or 4 good camping spots. This gps location is the buggest camping spot out of the four. There can easily be 6-7 tent. There is a little table, for cooking (made my hand) and a private beach.

ontario-wild.name: Vermilion Bay clearing
ontario-wild.notes: You cannot park at the docks however at the top of the parking lot there is a short dirt driveway on the left. There are 2 clearings right on the water with no "no overnight" signs, evidence that people have. I stayed only for a break however wouldn't hesitate to stay overnight. Garbage on site and pit toilets at the dock. 1 firepit. Gorgeous spot.

ontario-wild.name: Parking behind tourist info
ontario-wild.notes: Small lot just up from the park that no longer permits camping.  Other municipal lots in town only have winter 3am-7am December to March restrictions, probably for snow removal. Should be fine otherwise.

ontario-wild.name: Tim Hortons Cataraqui Woods
ontario-wild.notes:
parking lot of Tim Hortons (open from 5AM to 10PM)
located in industrial area, parking lot has lights on all night, not too noisy, no traffic

ontario-wild.name: Sparta Municipal Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Complementary parking with no restrictive signage. Small playground and porta potty. Large fairly level paved lot.

ontario-wild.name: Dirt road campsite
ontario-wild.notes: 40m from the highway, clean and easy road.

ontario-wild.name: Watford municipal parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: Large flat gravel lot at entrance to town. No restrictive signage.

ontario-wild.name: No frills
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking without convenience, we asked the store staff if it was possible to sleep here, private parking, no problem, on the side of the store little noise, in the shade

------------------------------------------------------

Parking sans commodité, nous avons demandé au personnel du magasin si c’était possible de dormir ici, parking privé, aucun problème, sur le côté du magasin peu de bruit, a l’ombre

ontario-wild.name: Seven Oaks Point Park
ontario-wild.notes: A popular park for dog walkers in Fort Francis. No services, but cooler place to park adjacent to shade trees and water within the city. Close to train tracks, therefore noise. No “No Overnight Parking” signs.

ontario-wild.name: Street parking at a park
ontario-wild.notes:
There is a small circle at the end of a street. It's directly in a park where you can hang out and it's just 20min walk to downtown.
Between 9 am and 4 pm it's just allowed to park for 2 hours. After that there is no regulation and we stayed here overnight which was no problem. It's not so good for big RV,s I guess

ontario-wild.name: Marathon viewpoint
ontario-wild.notes:
Large gravel parking lot with nice view of the water. (You can't see the view in my pics because it was raining but it is a nice view.) No "no parking" signs. Two picnic tables and a bear safe garbage can. There is a very clean outhouse just down the road at the marina. (But lots of no camping signs at the marina parking lot.)
We actually stayed at the upper parking lot last night, which we found thru iOverlander. Saw this one the next day when we drove down to the marina. It would have been a better choice, nicer views and more secluded, away from any houses.
There is a train track nearby and it came thru about 2:30 am this morning, very loud, blowing its horn. Otherwise it's a very quiet area.

ontario-wild.name: Tom McCullough Park
ontario-wild.notes: Nice little park with beach access and trail. No sign about overnight. Not for big rig.

ontario-wild.name: Fred Raper Park
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful parking lot directly at the water. Didn't see a sign which says "no camping". There is a small beach where you can go in the water. You can reach a couple of restaurants in about 5-10 min walk. There are also some picnic tables and a toilet.

ontario-wild.name: Opposite Whitefish Falls
ontario-wild.notes: Across the road from the falls. A wide open, paved area. Nothing to indicate that it is private property and no ‘no camping’ signs. I stayed the night with no problem. Only other vehicle I saw was a truck that filled a bucket with gravel and drove away.

ontario-wild.name: Fairfield Historic Park
ontario-wild.notes:
Lakeside parking lot for walking trails. No signs saying anything about parking overnight so I'm going to try.  Lots of people coming and going to walk their dogs etc in the evening. there's a food trailer on site but it wasn't open while i was here.  pit toilets in the park. 
Update: nobody bothered me.  quiet night.

ontario-wild.name: Constance Bay Beach - Street Parking
ontario-wild.notes: Street parking with beach access all along the several km beach.  Beach access is marked with blue sign with three white lines.  By-Law is that you can park overnight on the street and up to two hours between 7-7 on weekdays and 6 hrs on weekends. Gorgeous Sandy beach with miles of walking in either direction. This is a residential area and folks may not love vanlifers hanging around but so long as we follow the bylaws we have as much right to enjoy this 'one of a kind' beach as anyone.

ontario-wild.name: Ottawa River
ontario-wild.notes: River access spot at the end of Dunrobin Road:  There is a small flat area on sand, if you’re confident you can get off it. Otherwise good spot for a dip in the river on a hot day.

ontario-wild.name: Ottawa River Walk-In Camp
ontario-wild.notes: This specific plot of land is largely ignored by the city. It's by far the most scenic view of the Ottawa River from central Pembroke. Its sheltered and private from the main Millennium Trail behind the Beer Store. No anti-camping signage, and the homeless of town haven't had issues occupying the various tent-camping spots available. Within walking distance of many amenities in town. River is shallow for quite a distance, but is still considered swimable! Accessible stairs from Algonquin Trail down to waterfront or Beach just a few more steps down trail...

ontario-wild.name: Shadow Creek Road
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful spot on abandoned rail line next to small lake - we spotted a Cougar at dusk last night - fire ring - many great locations along the abandoned rail line. Simply exit on Shadow creek rd and just past the single lane bridge take a right onto the old rail line.

ontario-wild.name: Spot by river
ontario-wild.notes: Perfect hidden access road to site off highway, nice views of wide river. Quiet at night. High clearance needed, 4x4 recommended. Turn around point halfway down - suggest reversing down to river to get out easier.

ontario-wild.name: off Site Highway
ontario-wild.notes: Nice spot directly off the highway, hidden behind some Rocks

ontario-wild.name: Sherwood Road 2
ontario-wild.notes: just a bit further up the road, wider spot.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Bisson
ontario-wild.notes: Nice quiet spot in the forest and a few kilometers away from the highway. Gravel road takes you there. Also possible with a Van, but no big rigs.

ontario-wild.name: Kemuel little falls parking
ontario-wild.notes: Small dirt parking lot, with a canoe launch off the side of the hyw. Cute walking bridge leading to a trail. About 5 cars could stay here at once comfortably

ontario-wild.name: Quiet spot (Accessible by boat)
ontario-wild.notes:
Nice little spot to go for a swim, have a picnic, take a nap.
Might be able to sleep overnight in a tent. 

We parked our car at the boat launch in Astorville (you can find the spot on iOverlander) and canoed there.
The spot is accessible by any boats.

No cottage near.

Enjoy!

ontario-wild.name: Not a boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: A rocky spot next to the highway, it looks like a boat launch but isn't. You can park your vehicle surrounded by water on three sides. Not a great place for a tent. There were more mosquitoes than I expected, but the waves were nice when not interrupted by occasional passing highway traffic. Cell reception is fleeting.

ontario-wild.name: Leamington municipal marina
ontario-wild.notes: Parking for visitors just in front of the marina, with a park, piknik tables and washrooms. No interdiction for overnight. Perfect for a little camper.

ontario-wild.name: chute a blondeau
ontario-wild.notes:
good place to stay for one night!! 
if you're in tent then you can park at the road block and walk down to the water, beautiful sunset and pretty quiet. 
right off the highway so i wouldn't suggest making any fires 

good for campervans too but not much privacy

ontario-wild.name: English Lake II
ontario-wild.notes: We tried the other spots around but they seemed pretty busy so we checked google maps and found another dirt road to a big clearing on the east side of English Lake. Sand and grass, any vehicle should be able to get in no problem. Room for plenty of vehicles on either side of the road. Tall grass and bugs kept us inside for most of the night, but it was nonetheless a great spot for a 1 night, quiet stay. 2 bars of LTE.

ontario-wild.name: North Branch Road Riverside parking
ontario-wild.notes: A gravel pull over lot. There is a fire hydrant pump house that pumps water from the river. Avoid parking near that. Otherwise, it's a quiet spot next to a beautiful river.

ontario-wild.name: Beaver Valley Rest Area
ontario-wild.notes: Official rest area right next to the highway. Flat gravel parking lot with several picnic tables on some grass and two porta potties. We only stayed for dinner, but there are no "no overnight parking" signs, so could be a good place to sleep of you don't mind the nearby highway traffic.

ontario-wild.name: Tobermory united church
ontario-wild.notes:
Very nice church parking lot on the edge of the street but not very busy. no sign prohibiting to spend the night there. We spent the night there. It is a private parking lot, in theory the ranger cannot issue a statement of offence.
--------
Tres beau stationnement de l’eglise en bordure de la rue mais pas tres achalandé. aucune affiche interdissant d’y passer la nuit. Nous y avons passé la nuit. C’est un stationnement privé, en théorie le ranger ne peut pas emettre de constat d’infraction.

ontario-wild.name: Horse pack camp
ontario-wild.notes: Located just outside east gate of Algonquin Park. Looks like a horse packing camp.  Dirt Road not far off Highway 60. Lots of room to turn around RV. Lots of camping spots. Good Verizon. Near lake.

ontario-wild.name: Pit of sand after pleasant lake
ontario-wild.notes:
Big pit of sand next to the gravel road. 
If you arrived until here and there no more space at the spot of pleasant lake it’s the solution for one night. There is a pit fire and enough space for a big RV or several tents, BUT you need to have a 4x4 or stay really near the road because the sand. 
Quiet et peaceful, but a lot of bugs. No restrooms. It’s just a little sleepy spot to help. 
The road in gravel to arrive to pleasant lake it’s disgusting, very destroy, Many bumps… not really pleasant …

ontario-wild.name: Roadside boat launch
ontario-wild.notes: Small boat launch beside highway,gravel. Also a wife spot on same short road suitable for another unit.

ontario-wild.name: Riverside power line camp site
ontario-wild.notes: The nearby riverside wilderness camp site was occupied when I arrived around 7pm, so decided to drive a bit further down the power line road and found a beautiful spot with a fire ring and lots of open pines to string up a tarp. One ATV drove past earlier, and about an hour after I had set up, another camper Tacoma came by looking for a spot. I had a dip in the river to wash up, but the slope down to it is steep and a bit slippery. there's a nice shallow sand edge in the river though, and didn't find any leeches! good cell reception.

ontario-wild.name: Sunshine creek
ontario-wild.notes: Small spot near highway and train, but cool. Little beach at 50m.

ontario-wild.name: Dude approved spot #1
ontario-wild.notes: Fairly wide open area, lots of parking spaces, a couple fire pits, and at the entrance of the road is fresh spring water under a small shed.

ontario-wild.name: Confederation Park
ontario-wild.notes: Beautiful picnic park which should be good for camping

ontario-wild.name: End of road
ontario-wild.notes: End of road (about 500 m from house). Quiet spot. Can turn around using side road. Quiet night.

ontario-wild.name: Hidden Beach
ontario-wild.notes:
Beatifull place, Flat grassy area with a little beach in front of the Lake, big enough for 10 cars 
There are picnic tables and a place for a campfire 
Nobody came during the night 
Simple gravel road to get here 
Keep clean

ontario-wild.name: Mont Bell - Domaine du Radar
ontario-wild.notes:
Authorised parking near the historic site - radar station of la Pinetree Line à Senneterre at the top of the hill. Flat, quiet. Spectacular view,

Stationnement autorisé près du site historique station-radar de la Pinetree Line à Senneterre tout en haut du mont. Plat, très tranquille mais pour vr autonome seulement. Vu spectaculaire sur la région.

ontario-wild.name: Mahzenazing River access road
ontario-wild.notes: Road parallel to 637 immediately after bridge. No boat launch but can walk down to river.Aprox 14. km east of Kilarney Provincial Park gate

ontario-wild.name: Tea PoT Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Lots of Roots.....Hidden just off the road....Lots of misquote....small put and close to the lake.

ontario-wild.name: Parking lot - RV only, no tents
ontario-wild.notes:
Asphalted parking lot for small RVs under 24 feet backing onto the bike path (not for trailers or tent trailers, no open extensions either).  Authorization was given to me by city employees working on site when I was there.  You can park and sleep there at night, but you can't camp there... Ideal for Class B or B-plus vehicle without extension. Quiet in the evening and at night. We had 3 RVs on site.

ontario-wild.name: Lac tellfer
ontario-wild.notes: Calm place with small access to the lake. Very quiet. Rough road to get there, but any vehicle can do it.  No internet.

ontario-wild.name: Aylmer
ontario-wild.notes:
On the side of the dirt road in the bend, a superb view of the Ottawa River. At the end of July and August, an apple tree offers you its fruit. No facilities available other than large stones that can be used as tables and benches.

Sur le côté du chemin de terre dans le tournant, une vue superbe sur la rivière des Outaouais. Fin juillet et août, un pommier vous offre ses fruits. Aucune facilité disponible si ce n'est que de grosses pierres qui peuvent servir de tables et de bancs.

ontario-wild.name: No name
ontario-wild.notes: Small parking lot on St Laurent river I did not stay overnight, but their is no sign saying that you can’t. We could even take our kayak to the river for an hour. Very nice spot

ontario-wild.name: owen sound near the water

Petite place avec pit à feux acet à la rivière de la place pour 2 tente un petit vr

ontario-wild.name: Gravel clearing off Highway
ontario-wild.notes:
Easy to get into this large gravel area off the highway. There is a small lake (our GPS called it Little Lake). 
There was cell service. Very little road noise because there is a berm between the highway and the camping area.

ontario-wild.name: Halte routière N-D de Pontmain
ontario-wild.notes: 2 spaces especially for RV. One night only. Nice picnic area next to lake.

ontario-wild.name: Rest area
ontario-wild.notes: Clean, quiet even if close to the road. Large leveled parking for big rigs too with many picnic tables.

ontario-wild.name: Ritchie Lake
ontario-wild.notes: Lovely spot on Ritchie Lake, after I cleaned up up the garbage. Solitude. Crown Land and posted legal camping.

ontario-wild.name: Dock Beach
ontario-wild.notes:
Like 10 or more parking lots. The street to this place is a bit like a unpaved road, but it's worth it.
You have like 150 metre beach and it's very quiet. Another car with a roof tent was also here at the same night.

ontario-wild.name: Road close opposite of bird sanctuary
ontario-wild.notes:
Great  spot to night sleep.
 lot's of mosquitoes, however, is free. cellphone reception is fine 3 bars

ontario-wild.name: Off-street parking West of the foot of Leslie St
ontario-wild.notes: Plenty of parking on a 20' wide gravel shoulder. This unassumed road is unsigned. It's across from the entrance to Tommy Thompson Park, aka Leslie Spit, and an easy bike ride to Woodbine Beach or Harbourfront.

ontario-wild.name: Lac Campion
ontario-wild.notes: Boat ramp area on Lac Campion. Part of the Poisson Blanc réservoir. Great beach!

ontario-wild.name: Truck stop by the road
ontario-wild.notes: Your typical truck stop by the road. Noisy given traffic, but for spending the night it's alright. Reasonable internet speed with Koodo.

ontario-wild.name: Large parking
ontario-wild.notes: Slept one night in large flat parking lot, behind a company. No signs no parking, near a bike path and a path to a lookout with a warning "at your own risk" !

ontario-wild.name: silver falls Road
ontario-wild.notes: Absolutely stunning place about 6km or less from highway 102. called Silver Falls Road. We parked our Ford F 150 with 27foot camper right in the on the side road by the so-called Crooked Rapids on Silver Falls road. 5 km from here is a boat launch but when we saw and heard these rapids it was stop here park. Some local people drive through and wave. Very friendly.  Our 2 dogs enjoyed the bushes and rock next to the rapids. Omg soooooooo peaceful and next to no traffic other than odd local drive by otherwise sounds of the rushing rapids. Stunning, peaceful for evening sit with most peaceful rushing sound of rapids hold your drink and enjoy. Morning sunrise sit to drink your hot coffee on the Rock watching the rushing rapids. Stunning

ontario-wild.name: Log cut pull off
ontario-wild.notes: A couple clearings off a dirt road just off of highway 11. No signs stating to keep out.

ontario-wild.name: Creek side pull off
ontario-wild.notes: 60 seconds down an old paved road, flat spot beside a creek, very grown in.

ontario-wild.name: The mighty white pine
ontario-wild.notes: A couple spots to pull off on a boat launch road. Nice deep pool under some rapids, great for a dip.

ontario-wild.name: Along McCarthy Lake Rd
ontario-wild.notes: The site is a pull-off of McCarthy Lake Rd ~1.5km from hwy 108. If you were crafty you could fit a small RV type unit in it, but it's more ideal for truck/car campers and tents. There is no cell service here for me (using T-Mobile), but we were able to use our satellite just off the back of the camp right beyond the tree line. Tree cover is available if you want it, but you can also park towards the edge of the spot nearer the road and get plenty of solar power. There's a clear fire ring and tent pad on the site. You're maybe a 1.5km walk to McCarthy Lake, and the site sits on a nice view of the marsh land leading to the lake (though it's elevated, so you're not all wet and soggy at camp). Not too much traffic on the road. Pretty and peaceful with plenty of space for our set up.

ontario-wild.name: Carlabert Street
ontario-wild.notes: About 5 minutes in from highway 17 towards Mouth Park. The Park has beautiful scenery area and bathrooms but no overnight camping.  there is a boat launch right across from the beautiful quiet boondocking spot. no noise great fishing and hiking in area. Right near Massey, Ontario. We ran our generator for a couple of hours and spoke to local kids fishing at the boat launch. So gorgeous.

ontario-wild.name: Logged place for a night
ontario-wild.notes: Place for one or two (big) rigs. Close to a minor intersection but hidden behind bushes and very quiet. Easy access. No services.

ontario-wild.name: Schreiber Beach
ontario-wild.notes:
A small parking lot above the beach with no signage at all about parking. Other signage shows maps and other information. Vehicles park overnight to use camping spots on the local hiking trails.

Angle parking and a few larger parallel spots, but none exactly level.

Google maps has photos and reviews of the beach, but none of the parking (08/2023).

ontario-wild.name: Geoff S. Gaston Park in Alliston Ontario.
ontario-wild.notes: very nice clean soccer parking lot with field. clean. lots of garbage cans, potty outhouses, and obviously a well maintained field and parking lot. unfortunately, we had to leave Earl Rowe Provincial Park after 1 night and couldn't find anything anywhere.  so we took our chances to come and crash rest here after ling exploring time and nothing available anywhere in this entire town, yet we all the way from Manitoba. it's dead here at 3 pm on a Saturday afternoon.  our dogs ran around a couple of local people who were here with their dogs. Keep the park clean, pick up your dogs stuff, and put it in the garbage disposal displayed. no fires here use your common sense and don't destroy a good stop place with nothing else in town here. there is a gate at the parks entrance, and the park can be found on Google. I guess no games nor big stuff going on. research why this park was created in 2017. kinda sad. but so peaceful and relaxing even to just come and hang here for the day. there us a sign on the road 500meters back says park open 5am to 11pm. but no signs displayed saying no overnight stopping or parking signs, however.  so I guess after talking with local people, you see lots boondocking here, yet no posting on it due to city bylaw. we also found nearby an old abandoned driveway by the corner light and could go there case we kicked out here our dogs enjoyed the race and run on the fields and catching Frisbee and the Ball. Be responsible and clean up, and NO fires also be respectful so others can come boondocking here for a night or couple since everything constantly is booked up in this area. Best time with relaxing and siltime here, no blasting music. be respectful to neighbors around. lots of room for big campers and turning. internet qith Telus 3 bars so good. Beautiful spot to come for a days away or as we did stay the night.

ontario-wild.name: Fort Creek Conservation Area
ontario-wild.notes:
the parking lot of a park.
very calm. 
you have access to many trails in the forest.
there are toilets, but they are disgusting !

ontario-wild.name: corner of road near Geoff S Park abandoned old place near road
ontario-wild.notes: we stayed for a short time it's right of a road, but you can easily back in and turn around nice shady tree. might hear some road noise but not crazy busy road.  it's right at a light. gorgeous place for 1 big rig only. don't think I'd tent here.

ontario-wild.name: Old highway #71 gravel pit.
ontario-wild.notes:
An unused gravel pit just off the highway on an unmarked trail.

Large open relatively flat area on gravel with some grass and weeds.

ontario-wild.name: parking lot
ontario-wild.notes: gravel lot on edge of town. sign posted "use at own risk"

ontario-wild.name: Nelson Road
ontario-wild.notes: Nice secluded spot to stop. No signage. I guess one could stay the night. This region is clean. So be respectful.

ontario-wild.name: Speckle creek, retired pump house
ontario-wild.notes: I nice little spot back in the woods, creek running close by and a bunch of old growth white pines scattered around. Definitely buggy.

ontario-wild.name: Bush clearing
ontario-wild.notes: Long rough road in, decent secluded spot

ontario-wild.name: Bush
ontario-wild.notes: Spot to pull off the road. Tons of trails to explore

ontario-wild.name: Wolf Lake Road Crown Land
ontario-wild.notes: once you get off 17. most of Wolf lake road is crown Land. drove till the road narrowed quite a bit and found a little spot that you can turn around. definitely out in the middle of nowhere. very quiet and secluded. slept in my rig. Toyota 4x4. very nice place.  My photos are drone shots.

ontario-wild.name: Great spot tucked away in the tree line
ontario-wild.notes: Space for a couple cars tents and a fire pit

ontario-wild.name: Real nice spot in the forest
ontario-wild.notes: This is a real nice spot in the forest 4km away from TCH. If you want, you can go swim in the „lake without name“ 20 meter away. You can hear the highway a little bit in the distance. There is enough place for 3 or 4 small rigs or vans. Starlink works fine! The forestroad is mostly good only a few parts a little bit rough. You don’t need 4x4 maybe a little bit high clearance. We stayed two nights and were the hole time allone. At the morning one truck pass the place.

ontario-wild.name: power line cut
ontario-wild.notes: Clearing on trails under transmission lines. Multiple clearings on access road from the highway.

ontario-wild.name: Rue Lina
ontario-wild.notes: Good street parking near FMG good for few nights.

ontario-wild.name: Little Falls Lookout
ontario-wild.notes: Nice place at the end of the road. Lookout parking. No „No overnight“ signs. Very quiet. Just a few dog walkers & 2 kids fishing. Picnic table. Garbage bin.

ontario-wild.name: Shouldice Lake Road, Bruce Peninsula, Ontario
ontario-wild.notes:
Just a hole in the trees off an old road that's really only an ATV trail north of the lake access.

Definitely not accessible by anything with a trailer.

The road north and back to the highway is nearly overgrown and the bridge over the Crane River was out.

I think officially it is in the national park.

ontario-wild.name: Place for wild camping with accommodations
ontario-wild.notes:
Petit endroit pour poser sa tente ou son camper, eau disponible 
Tables et cabane de pique nique

ontario-wild.name: Gibson Hills Alliston ON.
ontario-wild.notes: beautiful spot more like a hiking area. but literally right in town with Tim Hortons etc right of Industrial Parkway. good for big rigs and multiple vehicles.  no garbage bins. be respectful for your behavior noise etc it's very local yet at night quite and secluded within walking distance to Freshco Tims and so much more

ontario-wild.name: Baseball park
ontario-wild.notes: A parking lot and grassy spots to park on, stayed overnight with no issues. No mosquitoes! 👏🏻 WIFI!

ontario-wild.name: Pijitawabik Palisades
ontario-wild.notes: Just a gravel pull off across from a lake. It was large enough to accommodate our 40ft motorhome and trailer. Room for more. Trash can. It looks like there has been recent grading here.

ontario-wild.name: Temagami power station
ontario-wild.notes: Top of the hill, west side of Highway just past Milne Sherman mine rd. Large power station with a spot to the left in trees and a large one past and 100 m down past. Room for vans or car campers. It is 200 m from highway so road noise, but quieter over night. Close to town for morning fuel-coffee, cell good.

ontario-wild.name: Rest area
ontario-wild.notes: Typical rest area with picnic tables and pit toilets. Close to highway 17 so there is car sound but it is muffled somewhat. No signs that prevent no overnight. Probably best for car camping.

ontario-wild.name: Twin Gravel
ontario-wild.notes: Gravel area off the road which leads to Ratter Lake Campground. There are two gravel tracks which lead to a larger gravel area. No signs to say that you cannot camp. It is clean so must not be used by campers so please keep it clean as it will no doubt get closed. You’ll only have yourselves to blame. No toilet, no nothing except quietness away from RVs and generators. Camping only.

ontario-wild.name: Dead End Drive-in
ontario-wild.notes: Dead end road with large turn around beside drive-in. We watched a movie, then spent the night. Spot was used as parking for cyclists the next morning - some kind of trail nearby.

ontario-wild.name: in the forest
ontario-wild.notes: nice spot, 4x4 highly recommended. Beautiful view of the forest

ontario-wild.name: Ignace Lookout
ontario-wild.notes: Spot for 5 or 6 campervans. Panoramic view of the city of Ignatius. Presence of a garbage can, a picnic table and dry toilets. Slight road noise. Staying overnight seems allowed. no ban

ontario-wild.name: Pass Lake Lookout
ontario-wild.notes:
Parking area off 587 at Sare Road. Look for sign on 587 for a lookout trail. Don't take Sare Rd when you turn off - veer left and into a gravel parking area.
It's well off the road, quiet and private and spots for many vehicles. Aquire a daily vehicle permit using the QR code.
We stayed a night in September after labour day and so no traffic or hikers. Not sure if there would be an issue during summer or if it is checked by Municipal staff. 
Short hike into Pass Lake from here. Like all Overlander wild camping spots - please keep them free from any garbage and leave them cleaner than you found them so that we don't lose the privilege of wild camping.
